title: Screen pure-GF256 rank-one packet-coupled heavy column
description: Evaluate ldpc-r1col7-v0, a genuinely untried pure-GF256 successor. Preserve the legacy/WH1 binary peel graph and H6 factorization, add one packet-coupled GF256 column z with a stateless byte coefficient per packet ID, and use seven full-width periodic-Cauchy completion constraints. First prove exact construction/recovery rank and core behavior on the frozen K32768/K64000 trace slice, then run native timing only if the bounded coefficient screen survives. No GF(2^16), no promotion from modeled work, and no expensive all-K campaign before a short pass.
acceptance_criteria: Either produce a valid bounded rejection, or: (1) six exact candidate construction systems are full column rank; (2) all 24 frozen recovery cells and 96 nested OH0/1/2/4 prefixes are full GF256 rank with direct-vs-projected oracle agreement; (3) deleting zero-reference z reproduces the matched H6 peel/order exactly and Rtotal=Rbase+1<=1024; (4) q/delta/projected-heavy identities and all tiny/direct-GF256 oracles pass; (5) the corrected borrowed-source architectural work prerequisite is recomputed only from the pinned historical K32000 and K64000 ledgers, charging the whole H7 1742-muladd+1-XOR preparation, quotient, divide, and worst-case K missing-output z operations, and remains <0.99 versus the corresponding unchanged WH1 controls. There is no exact K32768 WH1 denominator, so K32768 work is explicitly non-decisional and must never be interpolated or mislabeled. Counter success is only a one-way native-timing license, never promotion; a survivor still requires reviewed native correctness and matched timing. Public-copy and memory costs are reported separately.
notes:
2026-08-21 exact-law clarification before any workload: This is a legacy-style joint systematic transform, not the V2 direct-identity packet law. The first K unknowns are latent peel/recovery symbols. IDs 0..K-1 use generated equations whose RHS is the original payload; only the external Encode fast path copies originals. Let S=GetDenseCount(K), N1=min(3,S), D2=0. Binary packet support is PeelRowParameters(id,p_a,K,S+6), PeelRowIterator over K, and exactly the three RowMixIterator columns over S+6; z is excluded from that binary mix and gets GF256 coefficient u_a(id). Staircase rows are BuildPrecodeSystem-style over K+S. There are six ordinary heavy/mix columns plus z and seven full-width PeriodicCauchy constraints HeavyCoefficient(r,c,7). p_a=uint32(GetPeelSeed(K)+a*0x9e3779b9); d_a=uint64(GetDenseSeed(K,S))+a*0x9e3779b97f4a7c15; u_a(id)=low8(SplitMixFinalizer(d_a XOR 0x7768325f6f377530 XOR (uint64(p_a)<<32) XOR uint64(id)*0xd6e8feb86659fd93)); zero is allowed. No screen has run. Parallel algebra, history/seam, and exact-falsifier audits are in progress.
Implementation seam found, still read-only/no workload: current WirehairV2Solve can host the exact graph. Build PrecodeSystem with S, D2=0, H=7; generate packet binary rows with PacketRowRuntime over precode_count=S+6 so z is excluded; call production PeelBinaryRows over L=K+S+7. The zero-reference z is deterministically inactivated and the remaining graph is the H6 pure-LDPC graph, giving R=R_base+1. Carry one GF256 z coefficient byte per row/peeled column through the binary projection, then solve the exact H7 quotient. This is preferable to inventing a second peel model. The required screen must differentially validate that R_base+1 identity and the bordered/full-rank oracle.
2026-08-21 math audit: GO to exactly one frozen exact-rank/counter screen; no analytic rank no-go. For B over n=K+S+6, packet z vector u, q=nullity(B), N=ker(B), and delta=rank[B u]-rank(B): if delta=1, full rank iff rank(G7*N)=q (requires q<=7); if delta=0 and Bv=u, full rank iff rank([G7*N, g+G7*v])=q+1 (requires q<=6, invariant to v). Thus q>=8 is absolute failure; q7 has both a left-null u syndrome and projected-heavy-minor resonance; q6/OH0 pays the 7x7 GF256 square-completion floor. Historical q tails imply about 0.53% heuristic OH0 failure at K32/K64, but periodic Cauchy projection destroys the raw MDS guarantee, so exact rank is mandatory and salt search on this slice is forbidden. Efficient path is affine: retain one base block plus one z coefficient byte per latent column and one z block; propagate bytes through the binary tape and pay at most one kappa*z operation only for each emitted/reconstructed packet. Naive K-wide z materialization is invalid for the speed gate. Binary work is unchanged; H6->H7 adds R+20 muladds plus one divide, with the divide charged at least one muladd equivalent. Historical B1280 modeled ratios remain about .9805/.9830 at K32/K64 when charging K packet outputs; B64 is riskier (~.9949/.9917) and requires native timing if the screen passes.
2026-08-21 encoder/decoder policy seam: the frozen native encoder scope already owns/copies source storage before the clock and moves it into NativeArm; the candidate may retain/borrow that exact source vector and direct-copy ids<K, matching WH1's borrowed-input semantics. Therefore timed extra initialization copy is zero in the adjudicating native model, while retained K*B source memory is explicit. Public V2 create currently promises to copy message bytes; report a separate public-copy diagnostic charging K memcpy-block equivalents and K*B retained bytes, and require a later borrowed native implementation/timing path rather than silently comparing unlike ownership. Decoder stays cache-off and reuses received systematic cold packets; only missing recovered ids pay a final affine kappa*z op. Preliminary conservative public-copy ratios remain about .9873/.9871 at K32/K64 and borrowed-native about .9807/.9831, so this seam is not an analytic work veto. All synthetic work remains a one-way falsifier; only native timing can license speed.

Current full-width PeriodicCauchy RHS preparation processes W=256-H residue buckets: H6 costs 1500 block GF ops; H7 costs 1742 muladds +1 XOR, so preparation adds 242 muladds +1 XOR. With base core R0 and candidate R0+1, quotient work adds R0+20 plus at most one extra divide. The conservative total delta is therefore R0+263 block ops plus one divide, with the divide charged at least one muladd-equivalent. title: [bug] Classify repair-v1 retryable attempt-zero weaknesses correctly
description: Authenticated rv4a.3 training exposed a v3 reporting/eligibility defect. Repair-v1 deliberately treats attempt-zero NeedMore or Error as retryable, and a corroborating zero-RHS NeedMore followed by a later successful attempt is a structural weak construction. The campaign instead counts only result codes 3/4 as fresh weak constructions and blanket-counts code 8 anywhere, including the expected attempt-zero real call, as candidate_runtime_error. Thus pure8 reports weak=0/runtime=5412 instead of 1286 deduplicated repaired weaknesses; pure9 reports weak=0/runtime=4422 instead of 1127. The authenticated no-survivor decision remains valid independently because both arms fail all encoder/decoder timing gates; v3 artifacts must remain immutable and receive an explicit erratum, not reinterpretation.
design: Add an additive post-v3 classification contract. A raw attempt-zero Error is exempt from runtime-error counting only when the exact same selector witness has attempt-zero real=Error, attempt-zero structural probe=NeedMore, a later selected probe and real solve=Success, committed descriptor, and successful repaired recovery. NeedMore and that narrowly corroborated Error count once per (arm,K,root) as raw structural weaknesses; repaired-final weakness remains separately counted. Any Error in selected/final/control/timing/dispatch/WH1 paths, any fatal attempt-zero mismatch, or any uncorroborated code remains a runtime error. Preserve the frozen v3 summary bytes and record a derived erratum; version any changed summary/policy schema before new outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove the exact pure8 1286 and pure9 1127 deduplicated retry-needed constructions from the authenticated v3 receipts, zero repaired-final weaknesses, and zero genuine runtime errors under the narrow corroboration rule; mutations of every corroborating field fail closed; genuine code-8 injections in all other paths still trip the zero gate. Historical v3 completion/verification hashes remain unchanged. Any future outcome uses newly frozen source/plan/pin/schema. Release, strict sanitizer, parser/campaign replay, and repeated source-reading bug hunts pass.
close_reason: Versioned additive erratum fully replayed and authenticated; corrected retry accounting, source/policy bindings, immutable historical artifacts, all quality gates, and repeated clean audits verified.

title: Repair and retest za5v pure-GF256 Pareto seeds
description: Use the authenticated raw za5v selection only as architecture evidence, then run a new predeclared seed-repair experiment for the speed leader pure8_s0m1_d3 and reliability leader pure9_s0m1_d3. Preserve and report the raw weak-seed/recovery metrics (1,208 and 1,034 unique weak constructions respectively); do not retroactively alter the no-survivor decision. Add no GF(2^16) rows. Define one deterministic payload-independent retry/selection policy before outcome measurement, bind its attempt-work overhead and profile identity, and retest on seed-disjoint every-K/all-six-schedule evidence against dispatch-v1 and WH1.
design:
FROZEN PRE-OUTCOME DESIGN (2026-07-29, repair-v1). This is a new authenticated v3 experiment; it cannot alter or retroactively promote the authenticated za5v v2 no-survivor result.

Arms: pure8_s0m1_d3 and pure9_s0m1_d3, both represented accurately as mixed-solver geometry with 8/9 GF(256) completion rows, zero GF(2^16) rows, S=SmallBand(K)-1, D3, P244, frozen X, mix3, K=2..100, and positive even block widths.

One shared deterministic repair policy applies to both arms. Cap is 8 total attempts indexed 0..7. Attempt zero is byte-for-byte the raw architecture: precode seed is the zero-extended uint32 root and packet seed is that root. Attempt a uses the existing frozen functions PrecodeParamsForAttempt and PacketConfigForAttempt: precode_seed = root + a*0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 mod 2^64; packet_seed = root + a*0x9e3779b9 mod 2^32. Arm/profile, K, block width, payload, loss, schedule, phase, and outcomes are excluded from seed derivation, preserving cross-arm pairing.

The production-speed policy is lazy but structurally exact. Solve the real payload at attempt zero. Success selects zero. On NeedMore/Error, run the fixed zero-RHS structural selector from attempt 0 through 7 and choose the lowest full-rank attempt. A zero-RHS success at attempt zero after a real-payload Error is fatal, not repairable. For selected a>0, solve the real payload exactly once at a and require success. Thus healthy roots avoid an unconditional probe, while selected attempt remains payload-independent. The decoder never searches: it validates and consumes the serialized selected attempt. Report all actual failed/probe/success work. No per-K tables, caches, dropped roots, fallback seeds, or hand fixes.

Protocol: add native/parser/campaign v3 schemas; never reinterpret v2. Preserve raw weak counts 1208/1034. Direct timing covers only the final selected configuration and retains the encoder-intermediate witness. Full encoder timing begins before lazy selection and includes every failed real solve, structural probe, final payload solve, initialization, first-K encoding, and descriptor serialization. Report decoder feed-through-first-success and deserialize/create/feed/recover scopes. Add selector-enabled versus forced-selected panels and A/A controls. Deduplicate selector distributions by (arm,K,root), not six schedules. Report attempts_executed and selected index histograms plus mean/p50/p95/p99/max, elapsed time, graph/solve stages, operations, scratch, result, and cap exhaustion. Exhaustions stay in denominators and block promotion.

Evidence lanes are frozen before outcomes: training has both arms, every K=2..100, all six schedules, 768 random roots (1,188 jobs; 456,192 recovery cells/arm; 76,032 selector configurations/arm). Pre-bind sealed manifests for either possible winner. Only an eligible training winner launches one joint sealed boundary containing (a) 256 disjoint random roots over every K/schedule and (b) the deterministic production root for each K over 256 disjoint loss replicates/every schedule. Apply the same gates independently to the prebound random and production lanes and to their union within one joint completion; do not inspect a lane before joint completion and allow no fallback to the other arm or lane. Production roots are SHA-256 domain-separated from K only. Prove finite seed-set disjointness from all prior selection and forbidden-holdout sets without inspecting outcomes.

Training eligibility and each sealed lane require: zero exhaustion/final weak/nonrepairable/runtime/OOM regression; H64 and tail AUC no worse than matched dispatch and WH1; statistically confirmed selected direct-solve advantage versus dispatch; frozen full encoder and decoder gates versus WH1; complete A/A, coverage, thermal/EDAC, recovery/memcmp, and authenticated receipts. title: Build same-process, same-path paired WH2 peel timing protocol
description:
Current peel_direct/funnel/validate run one compare process per arm in fixed order. Trained candidates use WIREHAIR_V2_PEEL_DEGREES while the shipped arm uses no hook. Prior A/A work showed an equation-identical identity override differs from no-override by roughly 1.8-2.4% because the code paths have different layout/branch behavior, so counterbalancing process order alone is insufficient. Add a native same-process paired protocol: the candidate and identity-PMF timing control must traverse the identical target-profile and hook path; a no-override arm is retained only as a semantic/equation check, never as the throughput baseline. Share exact loss traces, support IID and hard schedules, isolate decoder solve speed, and record per-replicate timing/recovery receipts.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Trace candidate and shipped-control execution in tools/peel_direct.py and tools/peel_validate.py.
2. Observe that each arm is launched in a separate fixed-order compare process.
3. Observe that the candidate enables WIREHAIR_V2_PEEL_DEGREES while the shipped control omits the hook, so the timing comparison changes both PMF and code path.

title: Align WH2 staircase-count architecture across metadata and public profiles
description:

Decide the WH2-native S rule, version it, and route it consistently through seed profiles, serialized public profiles, encoder/decoder, compare, peelpmf and training receipts. Freeze the associated completion contract (GF256/GF16 rows, geometry and profile ID); proxy/search regimes may not silently use GF16=0 while validation uses 10+2. title: Rebaseline and redesign the WH2 small-K completion band after S/profile freeze
description:
Goal (user): WH2 must beat WH1 encoder throughput at K=1..100. Protocol (user): sample 10 percent of K values, 3 construction seeds each, no per-K seed tuning on either codec, each K range measured separately because the ranges are different regimes.

MEASURED BASELINE (foureyes-class box, bb=2, 9 reps, K=2..100 sampled at 10 percent x 3 seeds; harness bench/wh2_smallk_race.py on worktree at 00fcc96): dispatch profile v1 runs at median WH2/WH1 = 2.15x SLOWER, aggregate 1.70x, worst 4.06x at K=4. Per-K: K=2 3255ns vs WH1 830, K=8 4487 vs 2254, K=100 23075 vs 11477. Note WH1 is erratic across K here because of its per-K tuned dense-count table (K=56 17325ns vs K=100 11477ns).

ROOT CAUSE. WH2's completion band is a fixed 12 rows (10 GF(256) + 2 GF(2^16)) at EVERY K, and binary_def_mu measures exactly 12.000 at every K from 8 to 100 and for every binary dense row count from 1 to 24 - the deficiency is reserved by construction, not emergent. Adding binary dense rows does not reduce it; it only inflates the inactivated set (inact 14 -> 27 at K=8 going d=1 -> d=24), making the residual solve strictly slower. H=12 also forces R >= 12 inactivated columns at every K (R=13 at K=2, 16 at K=8). Consequences measured by the mapping pass: FactorMixedCompletionQuotient() is a 12x12 GF(2^16) scalar Gauss-Jordan costing a FLAT 2292-2350 ns at K=2/8/32/100/400 (WirehairV2Solve.cpp:2231, called :3218) - at K=8 that one function costs more than WH1's entire encoder init (1962 ns). Encoder init also performs 70 heap allocations at K=8 and 62 at K=2, 42 of them inside the solve.

By contrast WH1 at K=8 builds a 15-column GF(2) system with ge_pitch = 1 uint64 word (WirehairCodec.cpp:4721) so every row operation is a single 64-bit XOR, completes Gaussian elimination in 281 ns, scales its dense rows with K via kTinyDenseCounts (WirehairTools.cpp:756; K=8 -> 6 rows), and copies its heavy band from 108 static .rodata bytes rather than constructing it.

REFUTED HYPOTHESIS: the P=244 coefficient tables are NOT a per-generation cost - they are function-local static const built once per process (WirehairV2Precode.cpp:770). Measured confirmation: period=32 is SLOWER than period=244 at small K (4517 vs 4257 ns at K=8), so shrinking the period is not a lever.

RESULT SO FAR. kMixedGF256RowsMin was 8 (WirehairV2GF16.h:16), a reliability policy rather than a structural bound - the code already documents that trims take a leading Cauchy subset of the frozen ten-row table. Lowering it and sweeping the band on the user's protocol: 10x2+d4 = 2.171x, 8x2+d1 = 1.721x, 4x2+d1 = 1.563x, 3x2+d1 = 1.365x, 2x2+d1 = 1.483x. Best is 3 GF(256) + 2 GF(2^16) + 1 dense at median 1.365x (aggregate 1.424x), fail@+0 = 1 cell of 30, versus 2 of 30 for the baseline. Residual at K=8 drops 2113 -> 771 ns; the K=2 floor drops 3255 -> 1803 ns. Caution: failure rate is non-monotonic in the trim (g=6 measured 15 percent fail at K=8 while g=4 measured 0 percent), so naive leading-subset truncation is not a sound design below 8 rows - the trimmed subset and its X coordinates need choosing, and 30 cells is far too few to certify a failure rate.

REMAINING GAP 1.37x. The cost is no longer concentrated: at K=8 trimmed it is peel 711 / residual 771 / project 341 / sysbuild 371 / build 210 ns. Closing it needs (a) a properly designed small-K band rather than a truncation, (b) elimination of the ~70 per-init heap allocations, (c) a word-packed GF(2) residual representation at small K instead of the scalar mixed-field one, matching WH1's single-word row ops. A fourth lever, deferring the precode solve past the first K systematic symbols, is confirmed feasible (the systematic path is already a memcpy when the cache is populated, WirehairV2PrecodeEncode.cpp:2189; the only observable depending on the eager solve is the one-byte seed_attempt in the serialized profile) but it moves cost rather than removing it and needs a user decision.
design: Corrected execution plan (2026-07-28): (1) add exact canonical dispatch-v1 10+2/D4 to the forced tiny-fastpath on/off correctness grid and run the full K=2..100 grid; (2) add a test-build-only native bandtiming protocol rather than overloading peeltiming, with experimental candidates explicitly outside the dispatch contract identity; (3) measure exact dispatch control and each candidate in the same process on shared nonzero messages, raw construction seeds and candidate-independent loss traces, using ABBABAAB panels, alternating labels, identity A/A floors, CPU/fault/cache/thermal receipts, isolated decoder solves, and encoder init plus first-K symbol timing; include a counterbalanced raw WH1 reference with the same timing scope; (4) screen control 10+2/D4, pure GF256 10/9/8-row bands, mixed 8+2 and 9+1 where reliability warrants, frozen versus tracking-X geometry, then local S and D2 neighbors only for survivors; (5) preserve every raw weak construction as evidence, with no retries, tables, seed repair or fixups; (6) use the historical ten-K/three-seed panel only as a timing screen, then validate survivors on every K=2..100 with large matched raw populations, all six loss schedules, exact censoring and full byte recovery; (7) freeze a winner only from the raw Pareto surface and an independent holdout. If a completion geometry wins, bind it per instance under a new contract/profile and fingerprint it; do not mutate global completion-row state or the frozen public profiles. K=1 remains owned by wirehair-4azp.
acceptance_criteria: On the current post-umrh branch, canonical dispatch-v1 D4 passes forced tiny-fastpath on/off correctness through every K=2..100, with per-call evidence that every successful forced-on mixed solve actually accepted the tiny path and forced-off/nonmixed solves did not. A native same-process bandtiming receipt compares experimental bands, exact dispatch control, and raw WH1 with shared nonzero payloads, matched raw seeds, counterbalanced order, arm-specific A/A floors, encoder-init-plus-first-K timing, candidate-vs-dispatch isolated direct-solver timing, and honest cross-codec decoder-receive-through-first-success latency; it must not compare WH1 final-feed time against the WH2 batch solve. Receipts include complete CPU/cache/fault/thermal provenance. The ten-K/three-seed panel is only a throughput screen. Final reliability evidence covers every K=2..100, large matched raw populations, all six schedules, byte recovery, overhead tails and censoring. Reports retain raw weak-seed counts and candidate-only/shared failures before any seed fixes. A winner must improve the throughput-leading objective without hiding reliability loss and must receive a new per-instance contract/profile plus fingerprints; otherwise retain dispatch-v1 and record the unresolved WH1 gap. K=1 is explicitly deferred to wirehair-4azp.
notes:

Do not use them as the current baseline. Rebaseline only after wirehair-umrh makes S and the target profile exact.

The removed harness did not actually bind raw construction seeds on either WH2 or WH1, its zero-source WH2 encoder timing was biased relative to WH1 nonzero timing, and its S/tiny-path state predates the current branch. Cross-codec decoder timing must therefore measure a fresh decoder from the first nonzero feed through first success, with recovery/memcmp outside; it is decoder_receive_to_solved_intermediate latency, not final-call solve time. Use candidate/dispatch, candidate/WH1, dispatch/WH1 and arm-specific A/A ABBABAAB panels, raw 32-bit common seeds, fixed censored weak rows, all six candidate-independent schedules, and an untimed canonical experimental-descriptor vs dispatch semantic bridge over effective coefficient rows, packets, intermediates, payloads, solve and recovery. comments.author: catid
comments.text:
RESULT: removed the GF(2^16) rows and swept the band, per user direction (target <1% recovery error).

Zero extension rows WORKS structurally (kMixedGF16Rows was the floor in SetMixedGF16RowsForTesting; there was no separate min). With gf16=0 the completion degenerates to a pure GF(256) Cauchy band and, importantly, binary_def_mu stops being pinned at 12 and instead tracks H = gf256_rows: at H=6 the reserved deficiency is 6 and inactivated columns at K=8 drop from 15.2 to 8.8.

SPEED (aggregate WH2/WH1 over the sampled K=2..100, reps=25, three repeats each): production H=12 (10+2, d4) = 2.177/1.935/2.331; pure-GF256 H=8 d1 = 1.548/1.619/1.557; H=7 d1 = 1.489/1.520/1.476; H=6 d1 = 1.391/1.446/1.397. So dropping the extension rows and shrinking the band is worth roughly 35 percent of encode time (2.15x -> 1.41x of WH1). Removing GF16 alone at H=10 is NOT the win (measured 2.41x); what matters is total band size H, which sets the reserved deficiency and hence the residual dimension. Note bb=1 is still rejected with gf16=0 - the mixed solve is tied to two-byte blocks elsewhere - so WH2 still moves 2 bytes per symbol against WH1's 1.

RELIABILITY: the <1% target is NOT met by trimming. Dense K sweeps (1000-2000 trials per K) show per-K SPIKES: H=6 reaches 2.6-5.0% at K=42..58; H=7 reaches 15.7% at K=3 and 6.6% at K=59; H=8 reaches 2.4-2.5%. The spikes are non-monotonic in H (H=6 is both faster and less spiky than H=7), which is the signature of an undesigned matrix rather than a reliability/speed curve. Neither geometry (frozen vs shared-x) nor extra binary dense rows fixes it: H=8 d2 measured 4.5% at K=23 and H=8 d4 measured 10.0% at the same K. The production H=12 band is spike-free on the same probe set (0.0-0.1% at K=3,23,31,47,55,59,71,83) - that is precisely what the twelve rows buy.

MECHANISM (WirehairV2Precode.cpp:669-712): the Cauchy band is built with const uint32_t H = kMixedGF256Rows + kMixedGF16Rows, i.e. the PRODUCTION 12, and cauchy_x = H + residue. The in-code comment states the X coordinates are deliberately frozen at the H12 values [12,256) because moving X with H would rewrite every coefficient. So a trimmed band keeps X coordinates designed for H=12 while shrinking Y to [0,H'), and the H' x H' completion corner selected at a given K can be singular. The same comment records that Y=10 was rejected because it develops a singular corner at K=23092 and that Y=11 and Y=46 were chosen because they are exhaustively nonsingular for every K=2..64000 - i.e. this exact search has precedent in the codebase.

NEXT STEP (well-defined, bounded): run that same exhaustive search for the reduced band - choose the Y set and the X offset for H' in 6..8 such that the H' x H' corner is nonsingular for every K=2..100. The search space is tiny compared with the H12/H15/H16 searches already done. If it succeeds, the ~1.41x measurement stands with spike-free reliability; if no H'<12 admits a spike-free corner over the range, that is the real reliability floor and the remaining speed has to come from the other levers (per-init heap allocations, word-packed GF(2) residual).

All measurements on worktree at 00fcc96 with kMixedGF256RowsMin lowered to 1 and kMixedGF16RowsMin added at 0 (both test-build-only policy floors, not structural bounds). Harness bench/wh2_smallk_race.py implements the user protocol (10 percent of K, 3 seeds, untuned both arms, range measured on its own).

comments.text:
MINIMIZING GF(256) WORK AGAINST A WH1-RELATIVE ERROR BAR (user direction: do not chase zero failures, just compare favorably with WH1 everywhere).

METHODOLOGY CORRECTION - my earlier failure sweeps were invalid and made the reduced bands look erratic. precodefail WITHOUT --construction-seed uses production seed derivation INCLUDING seed_attempt retries, i.e. exactly the per-K seed tuning the protocol excludes, while the WH1 arm was untuned. Redone with --construction-seed over 250 uniform construction seeds per K on both arms, single attempt, loss 0.1, bb=2, K probe of 29 values spanning 2..100.

EXACT GF WORK MODEL (from the mapping pass, verified to within 2 ops at every K): BlockMulAdds = min(L,244)*H + (R-H)*H + H^2. Every term scales with the band size H, and at K=8 only K*H = 96 of 552 block ops are attributable to source data - 83 percent is structure. So H is the GF(256) work knob.

RESULTS (250 untuned construction seeds per K, fail@+0):
  WH1                       mean 5.26%  max 29.6% (K=4)   -
  WH2 H=12 (10+2) prod      mean 0.68%  max  6.8%   worse than WH1 at 0/29 K   143 muladds
  WH2 H=10 pure GF(256)     mean 1.20%  max  6.4%   worse than WH1 at 0/29 K    99 muladds  (-31%)
  WH2 H=8  pure GF(256)     mean 1.74%  max  9.2%   worse than WH1 at 1/29 K    63 muladds  (-56%)  [loses only at K=2]
  WH2 H=6  pure GF(256)     mean 3.02%  max 10.8%   worse than WH1 at 4/29 K    35 muladds  (-76%)  [K=2,15,91,95]

RECOMMENDATION: H=10 pure GF(256) (drop both GF(2^16) extension rows, keep ten subfield rows, one binary dense row). It cuts GF(256) work 31 percent, is never worse than WH1 at any probed K, and is 4.4x better than WH1 on mean error. H=8 is available if K=2 is special-cased, for 56 percent less GF work.

ENABLING CHANGE - Cauchy X coordinates must track the band. WirehairV2Precode.cpp:669 built the table with const uint32_t H = kMixedGF256Rows + kMixedGF16Rows (the production 12) and cauchy_x = H + residue, so any trimmed band inherited X coordinates chosen for twelve rows. build_rows now takes the band size and a trimmed band re-derives its own X; gated on WIREHAIR_V2_BAND_TRACKING_X for the sweep. Verified as an exact no-op at H=12 (identical failure profile and muladd count with the flag on and off). Measured effect on a 25-K probe: H=10 max failure 1.70 -> 0.90 percent, H=9 4.40 -> 3.50, H=8 8.90 -> 2.60.

SPEED (aggregate WH2/WH1 over the sampled K=2..100, reps=25, three repeats, all at d=1): production 10+2 at d=4 is ~2.15x; 10+2 at d=1 is 1.78x; H=10 pure GF(256) is 1.72x; H=8 is 1.52x. So the band work is now a minor part of the remaining gap - WH2 is still ~1.7x slower than WH1 at small K even after removing 31 percent of its GF(256) work.

WHAT THE REMAINING GAP IS (not GF arithmetic): the mapping pass measured a K-INDEPENDENT floor of ~6.2 microseconds per solve at bb=2, present even at K=2, made of the H x H completion factor (2292 ns flat), the H-row planar RHS Gauss-Jordan plus writeback (3569 ns flat), the quotient build (204 ns) and entry/alloc. Plus 70 heap allocations per encoder init at K=8 (4,835 bytes of scratch to encode 16 bytes of payload). Shrinking H reduces the first two but does not remove them. The next levers are therefore allocation elimination and a word-packed GF(2) residual matching WH1's single-uint64 row operations (WH1 runs its whole K=8 elimination in 281 ns at ge_pitch=1).

comments.author: catid
comments.text:
ES-LEARNED STAIRCASE DEGREE DISTRIBUTION. Plot: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8b9aad85-f6fd-46b0-a2c2-a8d72e7aeb19

Added a shaped row-degree construction behind WIREHAIR_V2_STAIRCASE_DEGREES (comma-separated weights for degrees 1,2,3,...). Key constraint discovered while building it: ValidatePrecodeSystem requires the graph to be COLUMN-REGULAR - every source column must carry exactly SourceHits edges - so the edge budget K*hits is fixed and only its distribution across rows is free. The first implementation sampled row degrees freely and was rejected by the validator; the working version generalizes AppendDegreeBalancedStaircaseEdges, whose bucket greedy realizes any feasible target degree sequence, not just the balanced one. Degrees are rescaled onto the budget MULTIPLICATIVELY - an additive +1/-1 repair flattens the very shape being searched and makes most of the parameter space degenerate (verified: flat and flat-times-100 now give identical results, as they must).

ES setup: objective is mean inactivated columns (structural, so immune to CPU contention, unlike timing). Antithetic sampling, centered-rank fitness, and common random numbers - every candidate in a generation sees the same 8 construction seeds and the same loss-pattern seed, which matters more than population size. Parameters are 10 control points on a log-degree grid expanded by interpolation, so the search is over shape at fixed mean. Ran on foureyes (128 cores, idle): 7 K values x 70 generations x population 40 x 8 seeds x 400 trials.

RESULT vs the STOCK construction (not vs the flat baseline the ES log prints):
  K=2    8.228 -> 8.228   0.0%
  K=4    8.284 -> 8.285  -0.0%
  K=8    9.462 -> 9.279  +1.9%
  K=16  11.738 -> 12.078 -2.9%  (WORSE)
  K=32  17.266 -> 16.863 +2.3%
  K=64  23.698 -> 20.688 +12.7%
  K=128 35.508 -> 28.771 +19.0%
So: a wash below K=32, an actual regression at K=16 that is most likely overfitting to the fixed CRN seed set, and a large win once there are enough staircase rows for shape to matter. Note the stock Poisson construction is almost exactly as good as a flat shape at every K (e.g. K=128 stock 35.508 vs flat 35.572), so the ES gain is genuinely new structure rather than beating a strawman.

THE LEARNED SHAPES ARE BIMODAL, which is what the user predicted before the search ran:
  K=64  59.0% of rows at degree 1, plus a 13.6% tail at degrees 33-64
  K=128  8.3% at degree 1 and 53.6% at degree 2, plus a 23.6% tail at degrees 33-64
i.e. a large mass of very low degree rows to start the ripple plus a heavy high-degree tail to finish coverage. Mid-degree mass is suppressed.

CAVEATS. (1) These are inactivation numbers only - the error rate and the end-to-end encode time for the learned shapes have NOT been measured yet and must be before any of this is adopted. (2) The K=16 regression means the search should be re-run with a held-out seed set to separate real shape gains from CRN overfitting. (3) The gain is concentrated at K>=64, which is the top of the K<=100 range of interest and beyond, so for the small-K goal specifically this is worth less than the N1=1 result.

comments.author: catid
comments.text:
ES v2: mirrored PAIRED-DIFFERENCE estimator + 4x batch + held-out validation. Plot updated: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8b9aad85-f6fd-46b0-a2c2-a8d72e7aeb19

ESTIMATOR FIX (user direction, after EGGROLL / 'Evolution Strategies at the Hyperscale', arXiv 2511.16652). v1 rank-normalized the whole population, which destroys the antithetic pairing and throws away exactly the variance cancellation the mirrored pair exists to provide. v2 forms the per-pair difference d_i = f(theta+sigma*e_i) - f(theta-sigma*e_i) and rank-shapes the DIFFERENCES, so the shared evaluation noise between a pair cancels exactly rather than merely averaging down. EGGROLL's low-rank perturbation trick does not apply here - the parameter vector is 10-dimensional, there is no matrix to factor - but its variance-reduction stack (mirrored sampling, common random numbers, rank shaping) is the relevant part. Batch raised 4x: 16 CRN seeds x 800 trials = 12,800 samples per fitness evaluation, up from 8 x 400.

Also added held-out scoring: after each search the winning shape is re-evaluated on 16 construction seeds the search never saw. This is what separates real structure from CRN overfitting and it changed the conclusions.

RESULT vs STOCK on HELD-OUT seeds (the decision-relevant number):
  K=2    8.300 -> 8.294   +0.1%
  K=4    8.148 -> 8.152   -0.1%
  K=8    9.166 -> 9.029   +1.5%
  K=16  11.473 -> 11.777  -2.7%  WORSE
  K=32  16.418 -> 15.372  +6.4%
  K=64  23.836 -> 19.909 +16.5%
  K=128 35.961 -> 28.892 +19.7%
Against v1 (unpaired estimator, 1x batch, same comparison): K=32 went 2.3 -> 6.4 percent, K=64 12.7 -> 16.5, K=128 19.0 -> 19.7. So the paired-difference estimator plus the larger batch materially improved the search, most at mid K where the signal was previously buried in noise.

The K=16 regression PERSISTS on held-out seeds (-2.7 percent), so it is not overfitting - the search converged to a genuinely worse-than-stock shape there. That K needs a restart from a different init or a larger sigma; it is a search failure, not a property of the problem.

LEARNED SHAPES are strongly bimodal and get more so with K, which is what the user predicted before the search ran:
  K=32   55.2% of rows at degree 1, 14.7% at 9-16, 10.0% at 17-32
  K=64   67.4% at degree 1, 14.2% at 33-64
  K=128  71.0% at degree 1, 19.0% at 33-64
Mid-degree mass is actively suppressed. Many degree-1 rows start the ripple, a heavy top-end tail finishes coverage.

STILL UNMEASURED and required before adoption: error rate and end-to-end encode time for the learned shapes. Inactivation is a proxy - a good one, since R sets the dimension of projection, back-substitution and the (R-H)*H muladd term - but it is not the objective. Note also the gains sit at K>=32 and grow with K, so for the K<=100 small-K goal this is worth less than the N1=1 result, and it is likely worth MORE above K=128 where it has not yet been searched.

title: Skip empty WH2 heavy residue buckets for tiny K
description: The heavy RHS loop iterates all 256-H=244 residues even when L is smaller, issuing H full-block muladds from zero buckets for each empty residue. At K=2 this performs 2592 pointless muladds per solve and contributes to extreme tiny-message slowdown.
acceptance_criteria: Iterate only residues that can contain a column, preserve exact outputs and stats semantics as documented, add tiny-K regression/operation coverage, and demonstrate a repeatable create/decode speedup across block sizes with full scalar/SIMD/sanitizer tests.
notes:
Implemented in the shared tree without staging/commit. Solver change bounds the heavy RHS residue loop to min(256-H, L), so residues that cannot contain a column no longer issue H full-block operations from an all-zero bucket. Focused PrecodeSolveTest coverage uses the independent tiny dense oracle at K=2 and block sizes 1, 3, 1280; pins exact output parity and block-size-invariant executed BlockMulAdds=528 while proving 2592 empty-residue muladds are skipped (old total contribution retained those 2592). Repeated code-reading pass confirmed the bound preserves every populated modulo-period bucket for both L<period and L>=period and accurately reduces operation stats only for calls no longer executed.

Pinned taskset CPU0 benchmark, same Release binary/config/seed, K=2, 300 trials per bb, before -> after WH2 v2_precode: bb=1 create rounded 0.0->0.0 MB/s, decode 0.2->0.3 MB/s; bb=1280 create 0.7->3.6 MB/s (5.14x), decode 1.5->7.5 MB/s (5.00x); bb=102400 create 1.5->8.5 MB/s (5.67x), decode 1.5->8.3 MB/s (5.53x). Recovery/overhead outcomes remained unchanged for the deterministic run.

Validation: strict Release build and CTest 41/41; fresh rebuild of final-asan-current target plus explicit ASan/UBSan focused test and sanitizer CTest 36/36; native SIMD/gf256 full-suite lane passed; RISC-V scalar cross-build/QEMU portability golden 1/1 passed with backend=scalar; git diff --check clean. Solver overlap note: recovery-profile work already present in the shared WirehairV2Solve.cpp changes HeavyCoefficient calls to HeavyCoefficientForParams. This bead only changes the adjacent residue loop bound; test covers the default certified family while full tests cover both family=0 and family=1 solve paths.
close_reason: Bounded heavy RHS work to populated residues; oracle/operation regressions and 5.0-5.7x tiny-K create/decode speedups validated across SIMD, scalar, and sanitizers.

title: Version the legacy wire profile before seed-table changes corrupt cross-release decoding
description:
## Problem

Legacy packet equations are derived from mutable dense/peel tables and other implementation constants, but WIREHAIR_VERSION remains 2 and raw packets carry no wire-profile identifier. A decoder built after a contract change can accept older repair packets, report success, and reconstruct different bytes. Because the raw format is unframed, it cannot distinguish a caller-selected wrong profile from corrupt equations on its own.

## Evidence

include/wirehair/wirehair.h:47 still defines WIREHAIR_VERSION 2. WirehairTools.cpp:1063-1080 and 1182-1195 apply 768 peel and 163 dense exact-N fixups over the original tables, accumulated across many commits. At N=2373 the old/base peel seed is 8 and the current seed is 19.

## Steps to Reproduce

Encode a one-byte-per-block N=2373 message using the base peel seed, send only repair packets, and decode with the current raw public API. The audit harness received 2373 unique packets; wirehair_decode and wirehair_recover both returned Wirehair_Success, but 2365 of 2373 recovered bytes differed.

## Scope

Inventory released or plausibly deployed equation-contract commits, assign each an immutable profile identifier/hash, and freeze its row generator, dense-count table, seeds/fixups, PRNG, heavy matrix, and GF polynomial. Expose explicit profile selection and a trusted framed/descriptor path; preserve a documented fixed default for the unframed legacy API.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory tags/releases and materially different deployed commits rather than treating only "base" and "current" as history. Check in a contract manifest and repair-only golden fixtures for every supported historical profile and affected representative N. Explicitly selecting a matching profile recovers byte-exactly; a trusted descriptor with an unknown profile rejects before data acceptance. The raw legacy API remains incapable of authenticating an incorrectly selected/advertised profile, and its deterministic cross-profile fixture plus documentation require an application-provided digest/MAC rather than promising automatic mismatch detection.
notes:
Implemented two immutable legacy-v2 profiles and explicit trusted descriptor APIs while freezing the raw API to the dated current profile. PRE_FIXUP removes only exact-N seed overrides; FIXUPS_2026_07 retains all 768 peel/163 dense overrides. Added profile-aware encoder/decoder creation (including owned input), descriptor/flag validation, reuse reset, Python/C bindings, exact export governance, security/migration docs, seed-table hashes, repair-only mismatch fixtures, decoder-to-encoder retention, and full reuse checks. Historical validation built actual anchors 557c00c and 63f7591: all-N seed hashes and N=2373/N=5550 vectors matched; a wider 301-N/1,505-repair corpus reproduced byte-for-byte (pre d69a6563d81cf247, current 26898d9bc72d6f10). A wrong profile deterministically reports decode success but yields wrong bytes, proving the documented digest/MAC requirement. Validation includes strict portable and native GFNI/AVX512 builds, C/C++ and installed Python/package E2E, exact 18-symbol shared export set, 278,176 + 321,696 randomized native fuzz trials with zero failures, ASan+UBSan focused suite, and corpus/profile reuse tests. WH_SEED_KNOBS experiment builds are explicitly documented as non-conforming.
Authorized Claude Fable Max/plan adversarial review completed successfully and its findings were reproduced locally. Remediations: reject named profiles when WH_HEAVY_ROWS/COLS, WH_SEED_KNOBS/WH_PEELCAP, or CAT_IDENTITY_LOWER_RIGHT alter equations; document all escape hatches; add native Python PRE_FIXUP borrowed-input coverage; and pin/document the historical short-final repair-ID alias (current corrected seven-byte output versus anchor's four-byte encoder bug). Custom heavy-geometry and identity-heavy builds return UnsupportedPlatform and zero descriptors. Final evidence also includes 104 concurrent profile processes, package static/shared/both E2E, 19 Python unit tests plus native package coverage, exact historical-anchor corpus comparison, latest Release and ASan+UBSan legacy gates, and repeated clean source reviews.
close_reason: Two immutable legacy profiles, trusted descriptors, raw-default freeze, historical manifests/goldens, cross-profile corruption proof, experiment-build rejection, C/Python/package integration, Fable review remediation, anchor reproduction, fuzz/stress, big-endian, and sanitizer validation are complete.

comments.author: catid
comments.text:
Initial static feasibility result, no codec or new benchmark workload: a rank-monotone row update must avoid the span of the other rows in EVERY incident constraint for which that span is proper, including currently full-rank constraints where the row is essential. Restricting avoidance only to deficient constraints can break passing cases and is unsound. A union of d proper subspaces of GF256^K has at most d*256^(K-1) vectors, so d<256 is sufficient for an admissible replacement. Choosing a row dependent on the others in a deficient constraint then raises that target rank without decreasing any protected rank. This finite-family existence argument does not establish cheap random-access construction or generalization.

For the structural family of every K-subset with distinct integer packet IDs and maxID-minID <= W-1, an interior ID belongs to exactly D=K*binomial(W-1,K-1) distinct constraints: fix each pattern's minimum at zero and translate each of its K positions onto the chosen ID. Root independently enumerated the local subsets and obtained K3/W7:45; K6/W8:126; K6/W9:336; K6/W10:756, matching the formula. Therefore the simple d<256 union-bound primitive does NOT suffice even for all K6 subsets in a consecutive K+4-ID window. This is a limit of that proof, not an impossibility theorem for GF256 or row repair. Actual sparse-loss traces can span more raw IDs, and a global convergent repair process can still have unacceptable memory/construction/random-access costs. Next design must address these points, not merely repair the three observed .58 IDs.

comments.author: catid
comments.text:
STATIC ADVANCE: the prior degree756 bound is not an obstruction to local MDS construction. Append-only construction needs only the previous nine coefficient vectors. For K6, choose the next vector outside the spans of their binomial(9,5)=126 five-subsets. These are proper subspaces of GF256^6, and126<256 ensures an available vector; initialize the first six as the unit vectors. Inductively every six-subset in every ten-consecutive-ID window has full rank. Existing windows are never modified, so there is no factor six from incident old constraints. This proves algebraic feasibility of the local family, not efficient uint32 random access, acceptable construction memory, long-period behavior or distant-ID recovery. Sequentially generating billions of rows or storing them is unacceptable.

A compact conditional mechanism to investigate is a fixed GF256 6x6 companion matrix T with columns [e1,e2,e3,e4,e5,a], a0 nonzero, and coefficient column c_i=T^i e0. The first six packets are identity systematic. If all210 six-column subsets of [I6 | a, T*a, T^2*a, T^3*a] have rank six, every shifted ten-ID window inherits full rank by multiplication with invertible T^n. A lookup of32 precomputed GF256 matrix powers bounds arbitrary-uint32 derivation, but naive row generation costs up to32 matrix-vector applications and must be priced against actual WH1 repair speed, especially narrow payloads. Sequential recurrence is cheaper, but no stateful cache assumption may change packet equations or arbitrary-order support. No explicit qualifying T has been found or tested, and local-window rank alone does not imply the frozen loss/hard-pattern or distant/strided-ID gates.

Pure GF256 matrix-only sufficient no-alias condition, without introducing any extension-field completion arithmetic: P=(256^6-1)/255=1103823438081, with local factorization P=3*7*13*97*241*257*673. Check T^P is a nonzero scalar multiple of I and T^(P/p) is not scalar for each prime factor p. This makes T's projective matrix order exactly P. If T^d e0=lambda*e0, commutation with T and cyclic basis e_i=T^i e0 for i0..5 force T^d=lambda*I. Hence no two coefficient vectors at distinct uint32 IDs are proportional because their distance is less than P. This is a conditional proof, not evidence an explicit T passes it, and does not prevent higher-order rank deficiencies at distant IDs. All arithmetic remains ordinary GF256 matrix/vector operations; no new field or retired profile is proposed.

Offline decomposition identifies one recurring allocator address with wide-copy control slowdown independent of implementation, plus strong B64 temporal candidate/current drift at identical addresses. Before another optimization screen, isolate the material source of those effects. Do not revive .53 arithmetic or .48 cached-count candidate, repeat old namespaces, or assume another memcpy page variant addresses this cause.
acceptance_criteria: Begin read-only callpath/allocator/assembly/history audit and freeze one small mechanistic falsifier before any new timings. .53 slowhandle0x5e582049fef0 follows ownership rotation: K128/B1280 geometric1.034080 andK8192/B1280 1.025669;47/48conditions positive each. Metadata offsets0xf0..0x10f place slowhandle metadata in ONE cacheline at pageend, while other3handles span TWO, so split-cacheline causation is contradicted as a simple explanation. Also explain/measure separately why identical-address K8192/B64 replicate ratios move0.823376/0.815739/0.893634/1.002405. Preserve rawoutliers and originalFAIL; no posthoc subset promotion, larger-sample rescue or new functionality without a demonstrated mechanism. Require a passing bounded instrument screen before direct WH2/WH1 comparisons across public systematic/repair and fresh/prebuilt paths. Keep recovery/selected-equation and final all-K goals intact.

comments.text: Read-only continuation evidence: no public handle lifetime, packet-order or ownership bug found in source/assembly audit. This remains a hypothesis, not a cause or optimization claim. comments.author: catid
comments.text: Additional read-only instruction/address audit: libc forward tail stores occur at end-64, end-128, end-192, end-256, then the initial64-byte head store. For output phase0x920 and B1280, the page-crossing tail store at offset0xfe0..0x01f occurs at packet ID10 mod16, reached by K128/K8192 but not K8. B64 also has a page-crossing destination store at ID27 mod64, so this phenomenon is not exclusive to wide copies. A hypothetical +64 output shift moves the crossing to another tail-store position rather than eliminating it; +32 aligns the stores but also changes alignment, a confound requiring an interaction/control design. These are address/assembly-derived hypotheses only. No new timing is frozen or run. Fable original session3940 remains live at25minutes without a report and must be polled, not restarted solely for elapsed observation time.

comments.author: catid
comments.text: Fable read-only review completed successfully in the original resumable CLI session 3940 (exit 0); no retry or second review was launched. Root and local reviewer checked its claims against baseline disassembly and immutable .53 raw evidence. Useful new hypothesis, not a confirmed cause: low-page-offset interactions between the public call's return/prologue stack stores and PublicCodec hot metadata. Exact native geometry: with pre-call RSP=S, return store S-8 and three pushes S-16/-24/-32 line up with metadata h+0xf0..0x10f when S=(h+0x110)&4095. Mode is loaded before the three pushes, so an all-loads delay claim is overstated. Actual memcpy is the 64-byte ZMM path, not the recalled 32-byte path; both baseline and candidate absolute B64 timings vary, contradicting the report's stable-baseline claim. Slow-handle metadata fits one cache line and its aligned scalar loads do not cross the page; neither intrinsic page-end cost nor specific cache residency/cycle penalties were established. Similar heap/mmap ratios do not exclude every higher-bit alias. Broad allocator interposition and indiscriminate stack sweeps are not approved as the next experiment. A small two-handle-by-stack-offset crossover is being designed using natural baseline objects and measured call-site RSP, plus a disjoint null. The memcpy return store S-40 and batch-local stores must enter the disjointness proof. Candidate design uses compiler-managed bounded alloca with unchanged ordinary CALL/RET and frozen disassembly; no stack-changing inline assembly, no new timing, no production edits. External Exa lookup was unavailable; official AMD PDF content could not be fetched, so no unverified external hardware claim is adopted.

# Adversarial proof review: byte-offset arithmetic in wirehair_v2_encode (.53)

## Context
Read-only advisory review of the proposal to replace the per-call `BlockCountWide(M,B)` in
`wirehair_v2_encode` with `offset = uint64_t(blockId) * B`, `systematic = offset < M`,
`required = systematic ? uint32_t(min(uint64_t(B), M - offset)) : B`. Baseline is the
immutable commit a460d93df7aed68ad4bc57e71f3d25fccd4d764f; all line refs are `git show` of
that commit. No speed claim is evaluated. The rejected cached-BlockCount design (.48) and the
failed page-AA screen (.51) are not recommended and not revived.

## Verdict
Equivalent to baseline for every publicly reachable state. No public behavior change found.
One forged-only divergence (B == 0 with M > 0) and five implementation hazards listed below.

## Invariants at every publication point (codec/WirehairV2Profile.cpp @ a460d93)
Publication points: 824-831 (create), 921-928 (create_profile_id), 598-604 + 964
(CreateEncoderForProfile via create_profile), 1183-1187 (decoder, Mode=Decoder). The
`_with_options` variants (1017-1027, 1081-1093, 1140-1144) delegate and then only rewrite
SourceState/BorrowedSource via PublishEncoderSourceState 451-463.
- I1  1 <= B <= 0x7fffffff, M >= 1: ValidateDimensions 176-180 (via 781, 878, 730).
- I2  K = ceil(M/B) in [2, 64000]: 181-186; WirehairTools.h:80-81; re-checked by
      WirehairV2Codec.cpp:42-57 from InitializePrecodeEncoder 165-169.
- I3  M <= SIZE_MAX for ALL encoders: 788-790, 885-887, 578-582. Corollary M < 2^47.
- I4  Borrowed: BorrowedSource non-null (785/882/575) and [src, src+M) does not wrap:
      CompleteMessageRangeRepresentable 317-329 at 992, 1056, 1125. For 1125 the second parse
      at 1140->948 reads the same const bytes (codecOut disjoint from descriptor at 1108).
- I5  Encoder SourceState is never Invalid (602, 828, 925 + PublishEncoderSourceState);
      detach 1265-1266 -> Independent + nullptr.
- I6  M and B are immutable after publication (no setter).
- I7  PublicCodec is anonymous-namespace (18, 60-69); no external construction.

## Proof
Let K = ceil(M/B). By I1: (K-1)*B < M <= K*B.
1. Overflow: blockId <= 2^32-1, B <= 2^32-1 => offset < 2^64. min(...) <= B fits uint32.
2. systematic <=> blockId < K: blockId <= K-1 => offset <= (K-1)B < M;
   blockId >= K => offset >= K*B >= M. Matches baseline guard 1245 (`blockId < block_count`).
3. required: blockId <= K-2 => M-offset >= (M-(K-1)B)+B > B => B (baseline 1205).
   blockId == K-1 => M-offset in (0,B] => M-(K-1)B (baseline 1207-1208). Partial and full
   final both covered. blockId >= K => B (baseline 1205). IDs K, K+1, 65536+K-1 (<=129535),
   UINT32_MAX all fall in the repair branch in both.
4. Invalid/null/decoder: required stays 0 (1201), borrowed false (1212-1213), 1222-1227
   identical. Requires offset to be computed only inside the valid_encoder branch (H1).
5. Error priority 1214 -> 1222 -> 1228 -> 1233 -> 1241 -> 1242 consumes only required,
   borrowed, BorrowedSource, (size_t)M. All identical => identical ordering and results,
   including short-buffer cases.
6. memcpy: (size_t)offset == (size_t)blockId*(size_t)B when blockId < K, because both equal
   offset < M <= SIZE_MAX (I3), so neither wraps on 32-bit. offset+required <= M, and by I4
   the range does not wrap. Bytes identical.
7. Delegation 1252-1253 unchanged for repairs and for Independent/detached encoders;
   *dataBytesOut = required published at 1241 in both.

## Forged (unreachable) divergences
- F1  Mode=Encoder, B==0, M>0, attached borrowed: baseline BlockCountWide->0 (161-163),
      required=0, guard 1245 false, delegates. Proposal: offset=0<M => systematic,
      required=0, memcpy 0 bytes, Success. Unreachable by I1. Optional zero-cost hardening:
      `systematic = impl->BlockBytes != 0u && offset < M`.
- F2  M==0: both required=B, both delegate. Same.
- F3  M>SIZE_MAX on 32-bit: both already narrow (1218/1237); no new exposure. Unreachable (I3).
- F4  SourceState==Invalid on an encoder: borrowed false in both. Same.

## Implementation hazards
- H1  Compute offset only under `if (valid_encoder)`; null handle otherwise derefs at 1198.
- H2  Initialize systematic=false; memcpy gate must be `borrowed && systematic`.
- H3  Use `uint64_t(blockId) * uint64_t(impl->BlockBytes)`; `std::min` needs <algorithm>
      (absent at 11-16) with both operands uint64_t, or use a ternary.
- H4  Keep BlockCountWide 159-166: still used at 181 and 473.
- H5  Cite I3 (shared constructor checks) for M<=SIZE_MAX and I4 for non-wrapping; the
      borrowed-only check alone is not the source of the size_t premise.

## Existing coverage (baseline)
V2ProfileTest.cpp:735-749 and V2BorrowedSourceTest.cpp:65-79, 336-340 probe IDs
{0, K-1, K, K+7, 2K-1, UINT32_MAX} x shapes {(K-1)B+1, (K-1)B+B-1, KB} across routes and
Legacy/Independent/Borrowed with guard bytes and expected_bytes. Fuzz
V2BorrowedFacadeFuzz.cpp:265-271 probes {0, K-1, K, K+7, UINT32_MAX} with random final size.

## Minimal regression tests (proposed, not run)
- T1 (P1) Add `K+1` and `65536u + K - 1u` to both PacketIds tables above; expect
  required==B and byte-identical borrowed vs independent output.
- T2 (P1) Dimension-limit shapes, borrowed and independent: (K=2,B=1,M=2) IDs 0,1 -> 1 byte;
  ID 2 and UINT32_MAX -> repair 1 byte. (K=2,B=3,M=4) ID 1 -> 1 byte. (K=64000,B=1,M=64000)
  IDs 63999 -> systematic, 64000 and 65536+63999 -> repair.
- T3 (P2) Borrowed final partial packet: outputCapacity=required-1 -> BufferTooSmall with
  *dataBytesOut==required; counter inside packet range -> InvalidInput, counter untouched.
- T4 (P2) Null handle, decoder handle, detached encoder, IDs {0,K-1,UINT32_MAX}: InvalidInput
  and *dataBytesOut==0 (guards H1). Add only if not already present.

## Remaining uncertainty
- MessagePrecodeEncoder::EncodeResult internals not inspected; proof does not depend on them.
- .48/.51/.53 bead bodies not present in the jsonl export; relied on the user summary.
- Nothing compiled or executed; 32-bit reasoning is by inspection only.

comments.author: catid
comments.text:
2026-09-01 finite primary-literature screen at HEAD 47ca9dca55fcaa896a09be21b45f037403c4943d. Exa was unavailable, so primary sources were fetched directly with the browser. No source, simulator, build, timing, or recovery workload was run.

FINITE GATES
- Every received matrix must satisfy <=1% failure at each K<=64000 and OH0..4 with exact stateless uint32-ID row identity.
- Labels cannot fix support/Hall violations or peel stopping sets. The current H12 quotient requires binary residual deficiency q<=12; at q=12 an ideal random square GF256 quotient still fails about 0.39215%.
- The optimistic total encoder ceiling is 13K/1.02 = 12.7451K full-block XOR equivalents. Reserving half for a replacement family gives 6.37255K binary incidences. At 1280 bytes, measured muladd/XOR=1.8304, leaving only 3.4815K payload muladds. This is necessary, not sufficient, and no sealed all-width muladd calibration exists.

PRIMARY-SOURCE LEADS
1. BATS and overlapping-generation network codes: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.4811 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.05573 . On a point-to-point erasure channel, flattening each batch gives ordinary GF256 rows with correlated support; an invertible inner basis cannot increase received dimension. Published finite regimes use packet-percent overhead and network-transfer assumptions rather than absolute OH0..4. Batch work and partial-batch arbitrary-ID semantics fail the contract.
2. Fulcrum: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6620 . The inner random-linear layer is dense or trades density directly for recovery; the outer algebra is completion behavior already excluded by the architecture. It has no below-WH1 all-pattern work case.
3. Perpetual: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.04492 . Sparse consecutive windows trade overhead against width. Published examples reach low packet overhead only with widths 16..128 and compare against dense RLNC, not Wirehair1. RepairOnly work is width times K payload operations, far above the admission budget.
4. Cyclone and Zigzag: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.00695 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.09125 . These shift/XOR vector constructions are genuinely differently named, but Cyclone retains robust-Soliton LT work and its published K8192 overhead is percent-scale; Zigzag changes packet length and uses payload-bit iterations whose latency grows with packet size. Both also add vector/subpacketized equation semantics and cannot be universally faster across B64/B1280.
5. Primitive deterministic rateless codes: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05774 . The finite construction evidence is for very small dimensions and noisy-channel ordered-statistics decoding; arbitrary-ID jump-ahead rows and packet-scale erasure decoding do not supply a sparse finite K64000 candidate.
6. Recent nonbinary LDPC: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08500 . This is a short fixed-block code with hybrid BP/ML evidence, not a rateless arbitrary-ID construction; nonbinary labels preserve support/core and add payload muladds.

LOCAL DEDUPLICATION
- WH2 already uses an LDPC staircase, structured dense binary rows, and H12 GF256 completion. Accumulator, coupled, equality-graph, source-transform, array/permutation, radix, triangular, and finite MDS lanes were closed in .20.4-.14, .20.22, .20.24, and .20.27-.32.
- A square invertible transform is rank-neutral: rank(M_I T)=rank(M_I), so it only adds work.
- Sparse superregular or prescribed-zero MDS variants retain Hall/stopping-set failures; full superregular transforms are dense and the finite scalar direction roster cannot provide distinct arbitrary uint32 rows through K64000.
- BATS, fixed arrays, and global MDS-style matrices are exact no-gos for this contract.
- A binary irregular deterministic lift or a selectively labeled finite protograph remains abstractly conceivable, but no source supplies an exact finite lift, stopping-set/core tail, punctured-rank theorem, all-K systematic invertibility, stateless ID extension, and below-WH1 work proof. A name or asymptotic density-evolution result is not an experiment-ready candidate.

CONCLUSION
No concrete lead reaches exact equations or the <=2-minute falsifier gate. The only legitimate future aperture is a construction-specific binary irregular lift that replaces current precode work and proves finite expansion/core and arbitrary-ID behavior before code. Current repository evidence gives no such construction. Close as a primary-source-backed no-go; do not launch or rerun a workload from these families.

title: Falsify domain-separated row-varying MIX2 pairs
description: Test one genuinely untried pure-GF256/H12 Two07 MIX2 row law after fixed pairs and fixed packet offsets were rejected. For each packet row, select two of RowMixIterator's three distinct columns from a stateless full-uint32 packet-id mapping keyed by the effective packet attempt seed. This is a bounded recovery/work falsifier only: it is not covered by the closed fixed-pair or fixed-offset evidence, but it adds scalar selector work and therefore cannot be promoted under the prior no-more-complexity condition without a later explicit complexity and native-timing gate.
design: Freeze exactly one law before code or workload and never scan constants: x = Avalanche32(block_id XOR effective PacketRowConfig.PeelSeed XOR 0x4d495832), using the existing bijective xor-shift/odd-multiply constants 0x7feb352d and 0x846ca68b; pair_mode = high32(uint64(x) * 3); modes 0,1,2 select iterator ordinals {0,1},{0,2},{1,2}. The avalanche is a permutation for each seed, so the complete uint32 id domain maps to pair counts 1431655766,1431655765,1431655765. The effective attempt seed changes the mapping without p/q offsets. Require P>=3 so all chosen columns are distinct; fail closed at P<3. Add only benchmark/test-hook support and bind the law into resume equation identity; hook-free production objects/equations must remain byte-identical. comments.text:
Terminal read-only audit result for `.20.35` (2026-08-30): PASS. This does not revive, alter, salvage, or authorize a rerun of `.20.34`.

IMMUTABLE `.20.34` EVIDENCE

- Evidence `/dev/shm/wirehair-rdpru-batch128-aa-ece6b05-evidence.csv`: 16,947 bytes, SHA-256 `7306565a14b6422643f13c904f678bd559e2b8538cbd7a2f63af0d606b0d23d1`.

- The likely freeze-time probe `/dev/shm/wh2_cpuid_probe` has SHA-256 `ba8086236284686bdd62b8e486cd20a11e27123b0d93048af259bb54a7eb0c05`, build ID `3a56f550d59bd857550449e590212bcb6555f95e`, no affinity call, no `sched_getcpu`, and no CPU receipt. Its historical executing CPU therefore cannot be proved. The current topology makes CPU84 the unique CPU whose initial APIC byte is `0x29`; this is an inference, not a rewrite of historical evidence.

PINNED LOCAL RECEIPTS

- Original audit probe source SHA-256 `bf8ad180de3ca5259c692fb300979b51f5538f784ff98a1c0cfda17ca1941445`; binary SHA-256 `b212c8594dbe49017ff48ba04db2368e876e5e7579c1ab30233e18c71b81b55f`, build ID `a470f606dd466909ce19c4ce3ede80001faede5c`. Two CPU50 receipts were byte-identical with SHA-256 `b69c632e205b8a829f807fce3016074b25a8a5609a30843eade4552a55b2c009`.
- A final harmless extension queried advertised leaf `0x80000026`: source SHA-256 `7173708df4115a64bc5dbb829b5b9b3942f97dcc5ae992d674cdbd70cb1e0d1c`; strict binary SHA-256 `00781304276b7d58ab921f796defe92f0e260c5f21cebc65ac55e11a780b0381`.
- Full 128-CPU pinned sweep: `cpu_count=128`, `stable_tuple_count=1`, `identity_mismatch_count=0`. On every CPU, `CPUID.1:EBX[31:24] == CPUID.0B:EDX[7:0] == CPUID.8000001E:EAX[7:0] == /proc/cpuinfo APIC ID`; all IDs are below 256 here. The canonical full Linux CPU/APIC map SHA-256 is `d51bf8bf7c1b249d081d8447fd35f118f2d5bfeee49d2a8f3bc2aba507744d8b`.
- CPU50 maps to APIC/x2APIC `0x64`: leaf1 EBX `0x64800800`, every valid leaf `0xB` EDX `0x64`, leaf `0x8000001E` EAX `0x64` / EBX `0x132`, and every valid leaf `0x80000026` EDX `0x64`.
- Its sibling CPU114 maps to APIC/x2APIC `0x65`: leaf1 EBX `0x65800800`, leaves B/8000001E/80000026 full ID `0x65`, and 8000001E EBX `0x132`.
- CPU84 maps to APIC/x2APIC `0x29`: leaf1 EBX exactly the frozen `0x29800800`, leaves B/8000001E/80000026 full ID `0x29`, and 8000001E EBX `0x114`. Linux CPU41 instead has APIC ID `0x52`; Linux CPU number is not APIC ID.
- Package-stable observations across all 128 CPUs were leaf1 EAX/ECX/EDX, leaf1 EBX low 24 bits (`0x00800800`), leaf6, leaf80000008, and leaf80000021. This observation does not justify assuming package scope on another host; a new capture still records them on the target.

PRIMARY-SOURCE INTERPRETATION

- AMD CPUID Specification 25481 Rev 2.34 defines `CPUID.1:EBX[31:24]` as the initial local-APIC physical ID assigned at power-up, so it is logical-processor-specific, not host-wide: https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/archived-tech-docs/design-guides/25481.pdf
- AMD Family 1Ah PPR 57238 C1_0.49 (March 2026) defines thread-specific 32-bit IDs in `CPUID.B:EDX`, `CPUID.8000001E:EAX`, and `CPUID.80000026:EDX`, and identifies 80000026 as the preferred topology superset of B: https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/57238_C1_pub_049
- AMD APM Vol. 2 Rev 3.44 documents x2APIC expansion of APIC IDs from 8 to 32 bits: https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/24593_3.44_APM_Vol2
- Linux topology parsing prefers AMD 80000026, then B, then 80000008/8000001E; B/1F and 8000001E carry per-CPU IDs: https://docs.kernel.org/arch/x86/topology.html and https://docs.kernel.org/virt/kvm/api.html#cpu-topology
- Linux affinity may be silently intersected with cpuset restrictions, so successful `sched_setaffinity` is insufficient without an effective-mask check: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/sched_setaffinity.2.html and https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/sched_getcpu.3.html

FROZEN FAIL-CLOSED RULE FOR ANY SEPARATELY PREREGISTERED FUTURE CONTROL

1. Capture only after selecting and pinning the exact Linux target CPU. Require effective `sched_getaffinity` to be exactly that singleton and `sched_getcpu` to equal the target immediately before and after the entire CPUID bundle. Repeat both plus APIC identity around every untimed evidence stage. Any change is terminal `INVALID`.
2. Separate package/capability fields from logical-processor identity in the schema. Bind leaf1 EBX low 24 bits as stable fields and bind its high byte separately as the target initial APIC ID; never silently mask or ignore the high byte.
3. Bind the full 32-bit AMD target APIC identity using advertised, valid topology leaves: prefer 80000026 EDX, otherwise B EDX, otherwise 8000001E EAX only when TopologyExtensions makes it valid; otherwise fail closed. Enumerate valid subleaves and require one ID throughout. Query every additionally available source and require agreement. Use 1F only as an optional advertised/valid cross-check, not as an assumed AMD leaf.
4. Require `CPUID.1:EBX[31:24] == full_apic_id & 0xff`; never use the 8-bit field alone as unique identity when IDs can exceed 255. Bind Linux CPU number and architectural APIC ID independently, together with vendor/max-leaf/family-model/topology and the exact Linux CPU/APIC mapping. A new protocol must explicitly bind or reject boot/hotplug/topology changes.
5. For this current host/target specifically, require Linux CPU50, full ID `0x64`, leaf1 high byte `0x64`, derived SMT thread 0, core 50, package 0, sibling set `{50,114}`, and agreement among valid 80000026, B, and 8000001E identities.
6. Any affinity, CPU, APIC, topology, stable-field, or cross-source mismatch fails before fixture construction. Never recapture, repair, rewrite, switch target, or reinterpret a frozen manifest.

No codec, timing, controller, candidate, calibration, K2/K3, GF16, screen, profile, or census workload was run in `.20.35`. title: Prove deterministic GF256 row repair for hard-pattern windows
description: Find a genuinely new pure-GF256 architecture after .20.30 proved that stateless all-uint32 complement hashing has excellent average K3 rank but cannot guarantee every authenticated hard-pattern subset. This is not a salt scan, avalanche retune, domain deletion, profile reinterpretation, or continuation of the rejected mapper.
design: Start read-only and analytic. Specify exactly what context selects repaired rows, how encoder and decoder derive the same choice without hidden session state, what metadata or frozen per-K profile data is required, how raw-ID aliases and collinear rows are handled, and why retired profiles fail safely. Prove a finite repair bound, GF256 work/memory ceiling below Wirehair1, and compatibility with incremental receive before code. Prefer bounded offline per-K seed repair or certified replacement rows only if the proof preserves the frozen loss/overhead contract. A future one-shot falsifier must predeclare rejection receipts with cell ordinal/hash, subset positions, raw IDs, mapped rows/buckets, determinant, and alias-versus-collinear class.

comments.author: catid
comments.text:
READ-ONLY ANALYTIC DISPOSITION: REJECT. No admissible row-repair survivor was found, so no implementation, recovery screen, timing, profile promotion, or census is licensed. No repository workload ran.

Local wire-contract proof. Shared equation context is exactly profile_id, message_bytes, block_bytes, seed_attempt, and raw packet ID. The decoder gets only the 32-byte descriptor plus ID and payload; it has no sender receive-window or row-choice state (V2_WIRE_PROFILE.md:3-28; include/wirehair/wirehair.h:545-591). Rows are regenerated deterministically from the raw ID and immutable configuration (codec/WirehairV2Solve.cpp:422-507,2918-2955,5323-5325). Replacing sender row r with decoder row s is unsound for arbitrary messages whenever r differs from s, because transmitted payload r*x need not equal s*x. Loss, reordering, resume, and duplicates also make mutable order state unavailable; existing resume and duplicate paths explicitly preserve immutable equation identity (WirehairV2Solve.cpp:5263-5294; WirehairV2PrecodeDecode.cpp:1360-1450).

Universal stateless repair is impossible. Nonzero GF256^3 rows project to 65,793 directions in PG(2,256), so 2^32 IDs necessarily alias. Three-wise independence is an arc and an even-q projective-plane arc contains at most q+2=258 points. Thus no f(profile,K,id) can make every distinct uint32 K3 triple independent. Primary finite-geometry references: https://www.math.colostate.edu/~betten/pub/betten33.pdf and https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/13/9/1489 .

The tempting <=84-ID override for the 12 authenticated K3 traces is validation-corpus leakage and is rejected. It hard-codes 420 known constraints, retains the rejected .20.30 mapper elsewhere, proves no disjoint roots or other K, and aliases non-union low IDs because the low law globally consumes all 258 hyperoval points (Wh2K3HyperovalCodec.h:11-16; .cpp:193-255). It violates this task's genuinely-new-architecture boundary.

A generic frozen profile/K/ID replacement table is wire-correct only under a new profile, but has no all-K sparse bound. For one repaired ID each certified K-subset forbids one hyperplane. Fewer than 256 proper hyperplanes cannot cover the GF256 vector space, but at 256 constraints the bound disappears and it does not guarantee a member of the sparse WH2 row family. An unrestricted replacement is generally dense and costs O(K) full-block operations; current K64000 packet-row tests bound ordinary rows to 4-67 terms (codec/PrecodeSolveTest.cpp:6597-6648). This cannot prove faster-than-Wirehair1 work.

The existing per-K attempt wrapper is the only narrow compatible mechanism: one frozen attempt byte for each K2..64000, already represented by seed_attempt, with no per-packet metadata (V2_WIRE_PROFILE.md:24-28; WH2_BENCHMARK_CONTRACT.md:176-204). It is a certification wrapper, not an architecture theorem: search is capped at 256 attempts and can return BadPeelSeed (WirehairV2Solve.h:24; WirehairV2Solve.cpp:5573-5594,5630-5658), with no guarantee for every K or disjoint hard roots. Applying it to .20.30 would merely be the forbidden salt scan. Explicit per-packet K3 directions need at least 17 bits and new framing; version-1 reserved bytes cannot be reinterpreted, and any new law requires a new profile ID (V2_WIRE_PROFILE.md:90-98,168-180).

Independent primary-source audit found no exact finite pure-GF256 alternative satisfying K<=64000, OH0..4, arbitrary uint32 IDs, zero hard-window failures, incremental decode, and below-Wirehair1 work. RFC6330 uses frozen per-K systematic index J(K) to make the source/intermediate matrix invertible, but received subsets remain probabilistic and K stops at 56,403, so it supports only the wrapper concept: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6330.html . Decoder-feedback rank completion changes the contract by requesting a new sender equation: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.01802 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02371 . Dense random GF256 meets average reliability but costs O(K) per row plus dense elimination. QC/protograph fixed-matrix rank does not certify punctured loss submatrices and stopping-set search is hard: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.0702 and https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.2258 . Expander, sparse RLNC/inactivation, repairable fountain, and superregular/MDP results provide fixed-rate, probabilistic/asymptotic, dense, or larger-field guarantees rather than this finite absolute-overhead contract: https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/spielman/Research/superc.html , https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05814 , https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.05573 , https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.05555 , https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0734 , https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0607089 , and https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.08388 .

Conclusion: retain profile-static per-K attempt selection only as a future certification layer after a genuinely new sparse base architecture independently proves finite recovery and work. It is not sufficient evidence to implement anything under this task. Exa was attempted first as required but returned an authentication error; primary sources were inspected directly instead.

Replace .29 superblock-wide X/Y mapping with a local Latin crossover. Define sequence family g=0 for ABBA/BAAB and g=1 for AABB/BBAA. Let orientation flip f=bit1(u) in exposed mode and bit2(u) in isolated mode. For each measured sequence map logical A to X iff g xor f is zero; B uses the other bank. At every period in every superblock this yields exactly one A-X, A-Y, B-X and B-Y batch. Rotation balances sequence/orientation across list positions.

Each timed unit is one homogeneous batch of eight fresh invocations. Exposed mode executes per sequence W,W,W,W,M1,M2,M3,M4; isolated executes W,M1,W,M2,W,M3,W,M4. W is one clock-free W-bank batch8. For each c,r,mode observation compute dL=log(sumA/sumB) and dP=log(sumX/sumY). Within the logical partition A and B are disjoint and cover all 16 measured receipts; within the physical partition X and Y are disjoint and cover all 16. rho_ns=max(ceil(steady_clock period in ns),CLOCK_MONOTONIC clock_getres in ns). Every observation must satisfy qL=8*rho_ns/sumA+8*rho_ns/sumB<=0.005 and qP=8*rho_ns/sumX+8*rho_ns/sumY<=0.005.
