Run each of unset,64,56,48,32,24,16 in a separate process with mixed H12, periodic coefficients, mix1, block_bytes1280, iid loss0.10, OH0, and identical precodefail seeds. Because precodefail trial RNG excludes the environment cap and prints failure_trials, compare exact common-trace failure sets by trial index across processes. Before interpreting candidates, require unset versus cap64 exact equality for systematic seed attempt, successes/errors, deterministic histograms, failure trial IDs, inactivation, BlockXors, and BlockMulAdds; exclude solve_ms. Any mismatch invalidates the protocol.

Stage A gross screen per arm: K1000 x100,000 trials, K10000 x20,000, K64000 x2,000. Immediate kill if systematic selection fails at any K, any non-NeedMore error occurs, or the candidate shows a clear paired structural regression. Low caps are intentionally retained only through this screen. Rank survivors using structural failures (binary deficiency >12), not field noise, then exact total work; report field shortfalls separately. A survivor must have no gross recovery regression and must reduce deterministic work. Select at most one nonidentity cap before opening confirmation, preventing an adaptive many-cap promotion claim.

Stage B independent confirmation for the one selected cap versus unset, with cap64 retained as identity: two fresh predeclared common-trace seeds, 500,000 K1000/OH0 trials per seed and 250,000 K1000/OH1 trials per seed; additionally K10000 x100,000 and K64000 x25,000 OH0 per arm as work/scale endpoints. Primary recovery gate is the same paired gate used for mix1: exact two-sided McNemar alpha .05 plus one-sided 95% paired UCB on p_cap-p_unset below absolute 0.00005, reported per seed and pooled; OH1 must report failures and Wilson95, not merely PASS. Since Stage A chooses the arm, Stage B alone is confirmatory. Report matched cells, structural/field split, inactivation, binary deficiency histograms, seed attempt, BlockXors and BlockMulAdds. If the objective is a recovery improvement rather than speed-only noninferiority, additionally require a lower cap marginal failure rate with multiplicity-free confirmatory significance; otherwise describe it only as noninferior.

A speed claim requires exact output/work accounting and repeatable wall-time improvement, not the analytic degree saving alone. Any promoted result must get a new canonical profile string/ID containing the cap and mix1 row contract, new goldens, and unchanged existing defaults/IDs/wire bytes. title: Batch WH2 block XOR accumulation up to eight sources
description: Extend PairedBlockXorAccumulator with a bounded gather that uses the existing exact gf256_add_multi_mem kernel for up to eight sources at calibrated block sizes, retaining pair behavior where wider gathering is not beneficial.
acceptance_criteria: Oracle covers 0-9 terms, duplicate/alias-safe source patterns, threshold boundaries, and all production consumers; frozen-code A/B across solve and packet workloads shows repeatable gains; work counts and output bytes exact; strict/sanitizer gates pass.
notes:
Read-only profiling baseline: a 20s perf sample under 44 pinned WH2 workers attributed 32.47% self cycles to gf256_add2_mem, 10.15% gf256_muladd_mem, 9.94% gf256_add_mem, 8.60% SolvePrecodeSystemWithRuntime, 6.65% gf256_muladd_multi_mem, and 3.83% PeelBinaryRows. Primary consumers are PairedBlockXorAccumulator at WirehairV2Solve.cpp:286-323, instantiated in projection (:1891), residual RHS (:2004), periodic residue buckets (:2185), and back substitution (:2510), plus the mixed bucket call near :655. Existing persisted cold-pool k=8 calibration: gather/chained 2.2173x at 1280 B, 1.3385x at 100 KiB, 1.1272x at 1 MiB; existing codec prototype gate is <=128 KiB and prior exact count evidence confirms fallback at 131073 and 1 MiB. New 44-worker cache-contention sweep supports the lower end (median k8 gather/chained 1.366x bb1, 1.515x bb2, 1.985x bb16, 2.145x bb32, 2.118x bb64, 1.243x bb1280, 1.561x bb100KiB, 1.511x bb128KiB), but odd-size rows in that older harness use an unrelated byte fallback, so 131071/131073 timings are not candidate evidence. Planned direct test hook: 0..9 terms; sizes 1,2,7,8,15,16,17,31,32,33,63,64,65,127,128,129,1280,102400,131071,131072,131073,1048576; unaligned offsets 0,1,7,15,31,63; adjacent/nonadjacent duplicate pairs, all-same even/odd parity, and disjoint destination. Compare against byte oracle and assert no overrun. Production E2E matrix: certified+mixed, mix2+mix3, K 2/64/320/1000/10000, threshold-1/exact/+1 and MTU/1MiB, frozen packet/work bytes and PrecodeSolveStats exact. Frozen-code alternating A/B should measure create/decode phase and solve Project/Residual/BackSub times separately, with <=128KiB candidate and >128KiB exact fallback. Strict native/portable, Clang ASan+UBSan, full ctest, and repeated code review required.
Threshold governance amendment (2026-07-14): The earlier isolated-kernel freeze (count 3-4 >=1280 B, count 5-8 >=512 B, <=131072 B) was provisional and is superseded by controlled production E2E evidence at root direction. Clean CPU42 AB/BA v3 (40 rounds, 3 samples/arm, exact non-timing parity) showed the 512-B activation regressed solve by +1.82% encode and +2.75% decode, driven by +5.22%/+6.79% projection; artifact /tmp/wh2-e9tw4-controlled-511-512-v3, manifest 72e8f051680f0ece179c1a498c1fb7116dfaed2b1c8f345eb70b3b4d86717181. Therefore the accepted production lower gate is 1280 B for all effective counts 3-8, with upper gate 131072 B. Broad production no-regression supersedes the synthetic 512-B kernel win. Final acceptance must demonstrate old-path parity at 511/512/1279 and gains at 1280+.
FINAL REJECTION (2026-07-14): Five production shapes were implemented and exact-output tested, but none met the strict sub-threshold no-regression requirement. The bounded gather itself is valuable at the accepted 1280-B gate: clean final2 CPU42 AB/BA at K10k/mix3 measured encode solve -7.10% and decode -6.89% (project -5.68/-4.46%, residual -9.02/-9.22%, backsub -10.73/-10.69%), with exact hashes/stats. However every integrated selector perturbed fallback performance. Final3 mixed-mode methods inlined gather bodies (Paired Add grew 0x28 to0x1d5) and regressed 511/512 solve about4.3-4.5%. Final4 split classes restored Add to0x28 but an out-of-line paired projected-row helper caused residual +7% and solve +1.3-2.4%. Final5 restored literal fallback loops, exact 0xcc0 base stack frame, identical 0x28 Paired Add, and moved all gather objects into noinline eligible wrappers; compiler basic-block layout still changed the hot residual loop and clean CPU43 AB/BA (40 rounds x3 samples, no nonidle userspace audit hits) measured: bb511 encode +2.214% CI +0.531..+3.925 and decode +2.790% CI +0.855..+4.762; bb512 encode +1.728% CI -0.192..+3.686 and decode +1.412% CI -0.445..+3.303, with residual +3.15..+4.91%. Earlier audit artifacts: saturated initial a595c2a9fbd76c29042f3923a2a4627eb6eab45785e229760a7f7e504203768a; clean v3 72e8f051680f0ece179c1a498c1fb7116dfaed2b1c8f345eb70b3b4d86717181; final2 lower de3004efc69ad50a416bfbfd7ec44b78e23123b85ad89b319c023aba15c85336; final3 f51c789d3b2d10438b6f05bb109d3d8e01f55607fece86578db2e4eab623a10f; final4 cf45f516ff61c98f1664e53d269575422a5f6c538681fe0a1db3aa9af23de060. Root rejected further whole-solver duplication/alignment tricks. All gather production/header/test changes were reverted via apply_patch. Shared files are byte-identical to the accepted e9tw.7 frozen baseline: Solve.cpp 9ac6f55c6057a5f973ad763f897470c56cdcc9b4e47ad6c60a3c52758b05e0e8, Solve.h b9ad90fc9e7b6d2136137b039febf97e4a81da8f8b1e28676af93b837e772e29, PrecodeSolveTest.cpp ef27afb4be9e035d1ff90df8908830079d85402208c1bffeee037082331e367d. Preserve the accepted low-degree-XOR work; do not ship the gather optimization.
close_reason: Rejected after five exact candidates: 1280-byte gather gains were real, but every integration measurably regressed fallback paths. All gather changes reverted byte-for-byte to accepted e9tw.7 baseline; focused native test passed.

title: Evaluate mix1 packet profile and binary-tail seed selection
description: Follow the 1M-per-arm screen showing mix1/mix2/mix3 recovery consistency and lower mix1 work. Independently confirm mix1 tails, quantify packet speed, and use a seed/topology census to target the dominant binary-deficiency failure mode rather than changing the completion field.
acceptance_criteria: Predeclared common-trace independent-seed recovery confirmation and multiplicity-aware statistics; exact packet and E2E profiling; any promoted configuration gets a distinct frozen profile ID and leaves existing defaults/wire bytes unchanged.
notes:
PREDECLARED CONFIRMATION (recorded before observing either primary seed): Primary comparison is mixed completion mix1 versus promoted mixed/mix2 at K=1000, block_bytes=1280, iid loss=0.10, zero packet overhead, using common deterministic packet traces. Run exactly 1,000,000 trials under seed 0xbb67ae8584caa73b and exactly 1,000,000 under independent seed 0x3c6ef372fe94f82b. Report each seed before any pooled result. Primary gates: exact paired two-sided McNemar alpha=0.05 and a one-sided 95% upper confidence bound on p_mix1-p_mix2 below absolute noninferiority margin 0.00005. Classify every failure contribution as binary deficiency >12 versus H12 field-rank shortfall. Mix3 is descriptive: report per-seed pair tests with Holm multiplicity correction and do not promote from a nominal secondary result. Safety endpoint: at overhead 1 run exactly 250,000 common-trace trials per seed for mix1/mix2/mix3 and report failures plus Wilson 95%. Existing profile claims remain conservative. If recovery gates pass, follow with exact payload E2E and frozen packet-speed validation; any mix1 promotion receives a distinct profile ID, retaining all existing defaults, IDs, and wire bytes. NONINFERIORITY CI METHOD (also fixed before primary results): Let n10 be mix1-only failures, n01 mix2-only failures, n total, delta=(n10-n01)/n, and q=(n10+n01)/n. Use the paired Bernoulli-difference influence-function variance SE^2=(q-delta^2)/n and one-sided 95% upper bound delta+1.6448536269514722*SE. Counts are expected in the hundreds; exact two-sided McNemar remains the separate equality gate. Also report marginal Wilson 95% intervals and all four matched cells so the approximation is auditable.
PREDECLARED RESULTS. Seed 0xbb67ae8584caa73b, 1,000,000 OH0 common traces: mix1 274 failures = 257 binary-deficiency-13 + 17 H12 field shortfalls; mix2 267 = 250+17; descriptive mix3 287 = 273+14. Primary mix1-vs-mix2 matched cells both_fail=0, mix1_only=274, mix2_only=267, both_success=999459; exact two-sided McNemar p=0.796466371139; delta=+0.000007; paired one-sided U95=0.0000452583177374, passing 0.00005. Seed 0x3c6ef372fe94f82b, 1,000,000 OH0 common traces: mix1 265 = 250+15; mix2 244 = 228+16; descriptive mix3 259 = 239+20. Cells both_fail=0, mix1_only=265, mix2_only=244, both_success=999491; exact p=0.375373503238; delta=+0.000021; U95=0.0000581095732257. Equality passes but seed2 alone does not clear the margin. Pooled only after both seed reports: mix1 539/2,000,000, rate .0002695, Wilson95 [.000247691064,.000293228626], causes 507+32; mix2 511, .0002555 [.000234289139,.000278630605], causes 478+33; mix3 546, .0002730 [.000251043987,.000296875690], causes 512+34. Primary pooled cells 0/539/511/1998950; exact p=.404721914630; delta=+0.000014; U95=.0000406496696332, passing both gates. All six per-seed pairwise p values .375-.827 and Holm-adjust to 1.0. OH1 safety: each seed had 0/250,000 for every mix; pooled 0/500,000 per arm, Wilson95 upper .000007682859. Existing profile claims remain unchanged.
PAYLOAD E2E (common message/loss traces, seed 0xd1b54a32d192ed03): actual precode encode -> 10% loss -> decode -> packet verification -> all K source blocks exact passed for mix1, mix2, and descriptive mix3 at K=1000 and block_bytes 1280, 102400, and 1048576. Each arm delivered 1000 packets. Separate-process command maxima: elapsed 6.81s/RSS 8,192 KiB at 1280; 11.86s/433,624 KiB at 100 KiB; 53.35s/4,405,828 KiB at 1 MiB. These direct internal experiment contracts do not publish a mix1 public profile.
SEED/CONFIG CENSUS: exploratory 32 even block-byte profiles, 50,000 OH0 trials/profile (1.6M/mix), independent seed 0x6a09e667f3bcc909. mix1 366 failures=349 def13+17 field; mix2 412=387+25; mix3 382=355+27. Independently retested each mix census minimum and maximum under seed 0x510e527fade682d1 at 1M/config: mix1 bb30/bb42 277 vs262 (screen 4 vs21 per50k, reversed direction); mix2 bb62/bb48 260 vs279 (screen5 vs22, collapsed); mix3 bb4/bb48 265 vs241 (screen6 vs19, reversed). All differences |z|<1.1. One mix2 trace reached binary deficiency14; otherwise structural failures were deficiency13. Best-of-base-seed/inactivation selection is deprioritized.
ADAPTIVE DESCRIPTIVE AGGREGATE (not a promotion test; includes exploratory, loss-depth, census, predeclared, and selected-extreme datasets): 7.6M OH0 trials per mix. mix1 1,936 failures (.00025474)=1,830 structural +106 field; mix2 1,944 (.00025579)=1,832+112; mix3 1,920 (.00025263)=1,811+109. Directions are effectively identical. Field-shortfall rates 1.39e-5 to1.47e-5 agree with the random GF(65536) 1/65536 floor; extra/full-column field rows are not the recovery priority.

The certified periodic/full-column-hashed coefficient replay produced 4,025/3,976 field shortfalls per 1M (both consistent with GF256 oracle), while adaptive mixed field rates 1.39e-5..1.47e-5 are consistent with GF65536 oracle. LARGE-K LOSS-DEPTH FOLLOW-UP (recorded before results): freeze benchmark executable sha256 88a8e528f5b231b091a110c29faed4e6b0f24823b0e4dcbe2b3d5b2d4fac5ac1. As each of the 42 pinned lane workers becomes free, run one independent K=64000/block_bytes=1280/OH0/mixed-periodic screen at loss=0.50 and then loss=0.90, 5,000 trials per worker. Assign mix count by fixed worker index modulo three, giving exactly 14 workers and 70,000 total trials per arm at each loss depth; seeds are fixed as 0x50000000+CPU and 0x90000000+CPU. These are descriptive large-K consistency/work screens, not a profile-promotion hypothesis test. Aggregate only after all 42 shards for a loss depth complete; report structural and field failures separately plus exact work counters. Refill monitor is pinned to the authorized CPUs 21-41,85-105 and does not exceed one compute worker per logical CPU.
INDEPENDENT MIX1 INTEGRATION REVIEW (2026-07-13, read-only): no blockers. title: Optimize WH2 precode encoder heavy coefficient setup and residue buckets
description: Measure and prototype exact-output-preserving encoder improvements: cache the immutable certified periodic H12 coefficient table and avoid XORing the first value of each zero-initialized full or streaming residue bucket.
acceptance_criteria: Frozen-code A/B across small/medium/large payloads shows a repeatable create-time or total encode improvement; output bytes and operation accounting remain exact; mixed and certified paths plus allocation/error contracts pass focused and full gates.
notes: Prototype cached the immutable certified H12 table, used uninitialized full buckets seeded by copy, bulk-copied the first source period, and copy-initialized streaming buckets. Native focused encode and roundtrip tests passed, including exact certified/mixed full-vs-streaming oracle and unchanged HeavyBucketXors accounting. Isolated physical-core frozen-binary ABBA under stable background load showed no repeatable gain: mixed K1000/K320/K64 create-time medians were about +0.09%/+0.27%/+0.70%, while certified were -0.31%/+0.55%/+0.27%; the unchanged mixed K64 control itself moved +0.70%. At K1000 x 1MiB (streaming buckets), v2_mixed create throughput medians were 1038.3 MB/s baseline versus 1033.5 MB/s candidate (-0.46%). Classified below noise and rejected; source changes reverted.
close_reason: Exact prototype passed but produced no repeatable performance improvement and was reverted.

title: Avoid redundant quotient work when binary deficiency exceeds heavy rows
description: Certified GF(256) q>H tails cannot reach full rank, but the current solver still builds a q-by-q quotient, q payload blocks, and for a retained checkpoint may then materialize an R-by-R byte basis and replay all H heavy rows. This is a solve-speed optimization only: it must not change equations, recovery probability, terminal results, or q<=H successful solves.
design: For packed certified q>H with no checkpoint candidate (no resume request or a conservative budget proof of rejection), stream each free-variable quotient column as an H-byte vector into an H-by-H GF(256) RREF basis. Derive Q[:,f] = C_f + sum_p B[p,f] C_p directly from projected_heavy and the packed binary RREF, reducing relation-bit probes by roughly H. If the streamed span reaches H, NeedMore is proven without building completion RHS. If rank is deficient, evaluate exact left-null syndromes before NeedMore/Error. For a retained q>H checkpoint, bypass quotient construction: materialize packed binary pivots transactionally when necessary, then insert the H original full-R heavy rows exactly once into the legacy byte basis. Preserve q<=H unchanged, including success reconstruction; preserve H=0 scratch/checkpoint behavior and allocation-failure hooks.

design: After successful enc.InitializePrecodeEncoder, call dec.InitializePrecodeDecoder(message_bytes, block_bytes, &enc.Profile()). The cache-systematic option is local encoder policy and need not be passed to the decoder. Validate profile fields/seed attempt match in trial details or a focused test.
acceptance_criteria: Initialize the compare decoder from the encoder-selected wire profile exactly as public encoder_create/profile serialize/decoder_create does; keep the same common packet schedule. Add a regression proving one selected attempt is shared and no independent decoder search occurs. Re-run representative create throughput cells and label any intentionally separate cold-unprofiled diagnostic.
notes: Implemented exact public-protocol handoff: after encoder initialization, RunV2PrecodeTrial passes &enc.Profile() into decoder initialization and verifies selected attempt, packet peel seed, and precode seed match. Compare header now records precode_profile_handoff=encoder-selected-v1; CLI regression asserts it. Isolated native A/B used identical cc1d944 code/libs with only this one-line profile handoff changed, common iid trace seed 20260712, pinned CPU50. At bb1280 across 3 process rounds: K1000 create median 656.0->998.2 MB/s (+52.2%, 31 trials/round); K10000 457.8->663.5 (+44.9%, 15 trials/round); first completed K64000 round 151.8->214.2 (+41.1%, 7 trials; further background rounds not needed for decision). Encode/decode/recover are expected to remain the same selected wire equations; the corrected comparison no longer charges an artificial decoder seed search. Current integrated representative results also improve but include other second-pass changes, so isolated numbers above are authoritative for .9. Validation: Release CLI ctest passed; full Release suite before this small benchmark-only edit passed 41/41 including build-policy; ASan+UBSan direct compare with both precode arms/trial details passed; diff-check passed. Raw: /tmp/wh2-pass2-prof/handoff_stable.txt and handoff_{old,patched}_k*.txt; isolated binaries /tmp/wh2-pass2-prof/base_handoff_{unpatched,patched}.
close_reason: Compare now reuses the encoder-selected wire profile; isolated native A/B shows 41-52% create-throughput correction and CLI/sanitizer validation passes.

title: Evaluate true-identity systematic rows for a future WH2 profile
description: Current WH2 message encoding solves a generic K-row packet transform so ids 0..K-1 reproduce the source, making creation and decoding much slower than legacy. Prototype an explicitly versioned packet-row profile where ids below K are unit source rows and recovery ids retain WH2 sparse/precode generation; use direct precode encoding and measure creation, decode, recovery rank/tails, and compatibility implications.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark-only or versioned implementation proves exact systematic bytes, repair payload E2E, deterministic contract/goldens, common-trace rank/OH tails at representative K, and create/decode throughput. Existing profiles remain byte-identical. Promote only with statistically non-regressing recovery; otherwise park with evidence.
notes: Prototype completed then fully removed from production/internal paths after decisive rejection. Direct identity-corner encoder creation was fast: pinned K1000/bb1280 generic 3.585ms vs direct 1.145ms (3.13x); K3200 8.735 vs 1.622ms (5.38x). Actual-solver benchmark used default-false unit rows for ids<K, unchanged sparse repairs, exact direct parity/payload validation, and common deterministic 10% loss traces. Recovery collapsed: K1000 1000 trials maxOH8 generic 1000 success/OHmean .001 vs identity 56 success/944 fail; maxOH128 identity OHmean41.815/max107; K3200 maxOH256 identity 0/100 while generic 100/100. Root cause: shipping low-degree repairs are designed as a full generic transform and fail to cover random missing unit sources. No config branch, test hook, experiment target, profile field, serialization, or golden change retained. Follow-up wirehair-1t0m.10 parks repair-degree redesign.
close_reason: Rejected: large speed potential is outweighed by catastrophic recovery with the current repair law; prototype removed and retuning parked

title: Replace decoder node hash with bounded flat packet-slot table
description: WH2 MessagePrecodeDecoder uses std::unordered_map<uint32_t,uint32_t> for ReceivedSlots. Even after reserve this performs one node allocation per unique packet and pointer-chases on every receive/duplicate; at K=64000 and bb=1 its allocator/cache overhead is large relative to payload and the now-CSR solve. Replace it with a preallocated bounded open-addressed id->slot table sized for K+1024 accepted equations, preserving arbitrary uint32 IDs including UINT32_MAX, exact duplicate/conflict semantics, checkpoint behavior, transactional insertion rollback on payload OOM, and the existing K+1024 cap.
design: Use contiguous power-of-two arrays and explicit occupancy/state rather than sentinel packet IDs, because every uint32 packet ID is valid. Reserve enough capacity during decoder initialization so DecodeResult performs no table growth. Provide find/insert/erase/clear/swap operations needed by the decoder transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Paired benchmarks at K=1000/10000/64000 with bb=1 and 1280 report unique-receive latency, late-duplicate latency, allocation count and/or RSS. Tests cover empty, collisions, UINT32_MAX, exact/conflicting duplicates, rollback under injected OOM, checkpoint adoption and terminal cleanup. Release and sanitizer tests pass; implementation remains bounded under decoder's documented receive limit.
notes: Implemented decoder PacketSlotTable: contiguous keys/slots/occupancy, 32-bit avalanche hash, <=0.5 load, backward-shift deletion, arbitrary uint32 IDs including UINT32_MAX, normal K+32 preallocation, transactional doubling only for rare tails, and a hard K+1024 entry bound. This removes K-1 unordered_map node allocations from normal cold receive. Paired native benchmark (cc1d944 old worktree vs shared-tree new; taskset -c46; selected profile; median of internal reps, 3 process rounds) measured unique ns/packet: K64 bb1 13.19->8.11 (-38.5%), bb1280 21.94->15.43 (-29.7%); K1000 bb1 14.52->8.11 (-44.1%), bb1280 24.97->16.88 (-32.4%); K10000 bb1 14.46->8.80 (-39.1%), bb1280 23.74->18.44 (-22.4%); K64000 bb1 14.08->11.88 (-15.7%), bb1280 195.95->198.90 (+1.5%, noisy/bandwidth-dominated). Late duplicate lookup improved modestly: bb1 near-neutral 3-7%, bb1280 generally 10-14%; K64000/bb1280 17.16->15.11ns (-12.0%). /usr/bin/time peak RSS at K64000/bb1280: 92244->91648 KiB (-596 KiB); other cells were allocator/page-granularity neutral/noisy. K64 normal capacity is only 256 entries=2304 useful bytes, avoiding K+1024 overprovision. Tests: direct std::map oracle over 20k operations, max id/value, full bound, duplicate-at-growth no-grow, transactional growth, clustered deletion, explicit wraparound probe chain, existing conflict/checkpoint behavior, plus injected OOM immediately before growth proving size/capacity/keys unchanged before retry. Gates: full Release 41/41 passed before final benchmark-only edit; rebuilt Release decoder+CLI tests pass; ASan+UBSan decoder test passes; diff-check passes. Raw paired output: /tmp/wh2-pass2-prof/receive_pairs.txt.
close_reason: Flat bounded packet-slot table implemented with measured unique-receive and memory wins; Release full suite plus sanitizer targeted validation passed.

title: Skip known-zero inactive WH2 block XORs
description: During cold WH2 solve, inactive value slots remain zero until the residual solution is known, yet projection, residual RHS, and heavy RHS construction still issue full-block XORs from those slots. Skip these algebraic no-ops without changing coefficient projection, stats semantics beyond accurately lower block-op counts, wire behavior, or outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Exact-oracle and payload E2E tests remain identical; focused instrumentation demonstrates fewer BlockXors; paired benchmarks cover small and large K/block sizes; release and sanitizer gates pass.
notes: Implemented in codec/WirehairV2Solve.cpp: affine projection and unused-row residual RHS now skip known-zero inactive value slots; periodic and experimental heavy RHS accumulation likewise skips inactive constants while retaining coefficient projection. Deterministic paired post-cc1d944 precodefail N=1000 bb=2048 overhead=0 trials=20 seed=12345: block_xors_mu 27186.25 -> 23551.05 (-13.37%), solve_ms_mu 0.778 -> 0.685 (-12.0%), identical 20/20 success, R/rank histograms, and 4813.8 muladds. Exact-oracle/production solve, roundtrip Release passed; focused ASan+UBSan passed.
close_reason: Implemented and validated measured WH2 hot-path wins

title: Stream encoder heavy residues for large blocks
description: ComputePrecodeValues abandons periodic residue bucketing when window*block_bytes exceeds 64 MiB and falls back to H*L full-block muladds. Add an O(block_bytes) streaming residue path analogous to the WH2 solver so large blocks retain L XORs plus H*window muladds without a 244-block scratch allocation.
acceptance_criteria: Differential parity/oracle and payload E2E tests cover both sides of dispatch and very large block sizes; allocation/OOM contracts hold; paired benchmark shows material large-block speed or memory improvement without MTU regression; release and sanitizer gates pass.
notes: Implemented O(block_bytes) per-residue streaming fallback in ComputePrecodeValues when heavy_base>=2*window and full 244-block bucket scratch exceeds 64 MiB. Production dispatch remains threshold-only; test-only thread-local cap forces both algorithms. Differential K=500 bb=37 proves byte-exact parity, identical stats, VerifyValues constraints. Paired post-cc1d944 K=500 bb=280000 on pinned CPU4: baseline direct median 321.064 ms, streaming 155.634 ms (2.06x); exact full parity FNV64 12159291868393396303 both; operations 6600 muladds -> 550 bucket XORs + 2928 muladds. Release and focused ASan+UBSan solve/encode/roundtrip pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated measured WH2 hot-path wins

title: Audit WH2 solve/encode/decode hot paths for second-pass gains
description: Fresh source-level review of post-cc1d944 WH2 solve, encode, and decode hot paths. Identify correctness/recovery consistency hazards, redundant passes, avoidable GF operations, cache/layout improvements, and measured optimization candidates. Read-only audit first; any implementation requires exact file coordination.
acceptance_criteria: Prioritized findings include exact file:line evidence, expected impact, correctness rationale, validation plan, and explicit rejection/parking of unsound or unmeasured ideas.
notes: Fresh post-cc1d944 audit covered WirehairV2Solve.cpp, PrecodeEncode.cpp, PrecodeDecode.cpp and peeling/precode construction. Two high-confidence hot paths were implemented/closed as .4/.5: known-zero inactive block XOR skips (-13.37% block XORs, -12% deterministic solve time) and large-block streamed heavy residues (2.06x at K500/bb280k, exact parity). Identity-systematic design was prototyped/rejected under .7 despite 3.13-5.38x create potential because unchanged repairs catastrophically failed; stronger repair law parked .10. Remaining measured-design candidates filed .11 q>H quotient double work and .12 production top-K boundary heuristic. Lower-priority opportunities: batch/fuse H-corner RHS elimination in ComputePrecodeValues (~H^2 block ops, likely small beside accumulation); cache PacketRowRuntime in rare VerifyPrecodeSolution R=0 path rather than recomputing primes per packet; avoid per-call completed-decoder validation scratch allocation if post-completion packet checking becomes a measured workload. Correctness review found no shipping recovery/data hazard after existing transactional, resume, duplicate, row-domain, and dense/heavy validation; identity prototype exposed a row reference-count prepass requirement, but the entire mode was removed. Focused Release and ASan+UBSan exact solve/encode/roundtrip gates passed and .4/.5 tests include forced differential parity/constraints.
close_reason: Audit completed; actionable wins implemented and remaining/rejected ideas filed with evidence

title: Evaluate overdetermined WH2 heavy profiles
description: Under wirehair-1t0m, quantify whether explicitly versioned WH2 profiles with one or two extra independent heavy equations can escape the current square H=12 GF(256) completion floor. Establish expected failure exponent, actual high-trial solver/payload evidence across representative K, runtime/memory costs, compatibility constraints, and the cheapest safe implementation route. Existing profiles and wire output must remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Paired high-trial measurements and confidence bounds cover baseline and at least +1/+2 overdetermination; implementation/compatibility implications and rejected alternatives are documented; any edits have focused tests and benchmarks.
notes: FINAL EVIDENCE (temporary instrumented prototype removed; no production edits). Dimension: current H means H parity columns + H constraints, so H12->14/16 remains square; adding rows without variables generically overconstrains arbitrary K-source systematic encoding. Exact random n=12 failure: GF256 square 0.003921508788; +1 row 1.531862654e-5; +2 rows 5.98383885e-8; GF65536 square 1.525902189e-5. Actual precodefail bb1 loss10%: 100k OH0/OH1/OH2 K1k=405/3/0, K3.2k=422/6/0, K10k=450/8/3. K10 1M OH1=112 fails (18 heavy shortfalls, remaining q>12); OH2=66 (1 heavy shortfall, remaining q>12): extra packet suppresses field floor but binary tail dominates. Actual-projection focused OH0: K1 n100k GF256426 (0.00426, Wilson95 .003875-.004683), mixed10+2=21 (.00021,.000137-.000321), q>12=19; 20.3x observed reduction. K10 n100k GF256462 (.00462,.004218-.005060), mixed=56 (.00056,.000431-.000727), q>12=56; 8.25x. K64 n2k GF2562, mixed0, q>12=0 (too few to certify). Primitive-power Cauchy GF65536 used quadratic extension lambda32/generator266 and 244 residue period. An affine-coordinate Cauchy was rejected because conjugation symmetry retained subfield-like failures. H14/H16 controls: GF256 remains ~1/256 (K1 41/47 of10k; K10 16/17 of5k), GF16 0 in these samples, confirming H growth alone is dimension-neutral. Rejected hybrid 2 binary+8 GF256+2 GF16: at K1 n100k 83 fails vs q-tail19; K10 111 vs tail56. Random GF2 bridges can lose rank, and total12 rows still cannot solve q>12. Selected 10 GF256+2 GF16: GF256 10x12 prefix failure ~256^-3, then GF65536 2x2 floor ~65536^-1; no bridge risk and only2 extension rows. Planar extension muladd measured2.057x GF256 at1280 and2.071x at102400 for equal full bytes, projecting ~17.6-17.9% heavy-row kernel premium (ideal 16.7%) before transpose; enforce even block bytes initially. N1/mix actual projection screens: K1 n20k tails N1=2 mix2/3 8/6, N1=3 5/4, N1=4 4/6; K10 tails 8/15,11/10,9/5; no consistent win worth extra staircase cost. K64 N1=2 catastrophically worse tails11-15/1k vs N1=3/4 zero; certified N1=3 remains required. Mix2 no consistent recovery win. In-progress true-identity profile screen was decisive rejection at exact K: K1 q_mean21.7-30.2 and99.59-100% fail; K10 q_mean617-619 and100%; K64 100%; unit systematic rows leave too few useful repair equations. Compatibility: mixed field requires new public profile ID, precode contract dispatch, coefficient rule, even-byte restriction; existing profile bytes untouched. Followup wirehair-1t0m.14 owns self-contained payload/kernel prototype.
close_reason: Completed mathematical/actual-projection evaluation; selected mixed 10 GF256 + 2 GF(2^16), rejected false overdetermination/bridges/identity/N1-mix alternatives, and filed implementation prototype wirehair-1t0m.14.

title: WH2 second-pass speed and recovery improvements
description: Profile the optimized WH2 path at cc1d944 and pursue additional measured throughput, latency, memory, recovery-rate, and tail-consistency gains over the legacy baseline. Focus especially on escaping the square GF(256) heavy-completion floor through an explicitly versioned overdetermined profile while preserving existing wire profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Independently tracked changes have reproducible paired baselines, exact-oracle and payload E2E evidence, statistically supported recovery or measured speed/memory wins, explicit wire-profile treatment, and full release/sanitizer/fuzz/portability/package validation. Rejected ideas and remaining work are parked in beads.
close_reason: WH2 second-pass speed/recovery epic completed: measured optimizations and opt-in mixed-field recovery profile certified; rejected identity laws recorded; remaining optional follow-ups explicitly deferred.

title: Add optional WH2 systematic source cache and direct-copy encoding
description: WH2 discards its initialization source and reevaluates every systematic block through sparse equations. Add an explicit encoder memory/speed mode that retains source blocks for direct systematic memcpy while repairs continue through the solved intermediate system; provide a detach or disable path so the extra message-sized cache is caller-controlled.
acceptance_criteria: Systematic packet output remains byte-identical including the partial tail. Cached mode materially improves systematic encode and typical recovery-facing workloads; uncached mode preserves current memory behavior. Ownership, detach/disable, OOM transactionality, ABI/API compatibility, sanitizer, E2E, and benchmark gates pass.
notes:
Implemented internal runtime-only default-off CacheSystematicSource mode. MessagePrecodeEncoder retains exactly message_bytes only when opted in, memcpy-emits systematic ids including partial tail, leaves repairs on solved equation evaluation, and exposes idempotent detach/cache state accessors. Selected profile validation excludes this local policy; profile/wire contract remains identical. Codec facade exposes internal detach. Cached init/reinit/OOM is transactional; successful default reinit clears cache. Added paired compare --precode-cache benchmark and CLI smoke. Public ABI left unchanged because the existing create ABI has no options channel; filed wirehair-x8rs.14 for a versioned public API. Validation so far: release build and all 41 CTests pass (ABI/export/package/fuzz/E2E included); focused ASan+UBSan precode encoder and roundtrip pass; K1000 bb1280 systematic encode 6512.1->17580.1 MB/s (2.70x), iid 10% loss 6383.8->25821.4 MB/s (4.05x), K10000 systematic 3444.2->6674.9 MB/s (1.94x). Separate K10000 bb1280 process peaks: uncached 67564 KiB, cached 82560 KiB, consistent with one opt-in 12.8 MB message cache plus allocator overhead. Awaiting final Fable adversarial report before closure.
A fresh focused Claude/Fable max-plan adversarial pass was launched with the prescribed secret-stripped read-only command but produced no report after about nine minutes and was stopped at coordinator request; it is not counted as a review. The earlier successful integrated Fable review covered this area. Final manual bug-fix pass found no additional issues; git diff --check is clean.
Closure note: the preceding 'awaiting' sentence records the interim checkpoint only; the subsequent no-report disposition and completed local review are final.
close_reason: Closed

title: Batch WH2 heavy-row GF(256) RHS updates
description: Profiling attributes substantial residual cost to repeated gf256_muladd_mem calls where one source block updates H=12 destinations. Add a multi-destination GF256 kernel or equivalent loop fusion that reuses the source load and reduces dispatch/call overhead in encoder and decoder heavy-row RHS updates.
acceptance_criteria: Representative MTU, 100 KiB, and large-block benchmarks demonstrate a repeatable win or the experiment is reverted and documented. Scalar/SIMD, unaligned tails, alias constraints, sanitizer, cross-architecture, and full E2E recovery tests pass with unchanged wire output.
notes: Implemented gf256_muladd_multi_mem and wired certified periodic and experiment heavy RHS generation in SolvePrecodeSystem plus encoder heavy generation. Kernel contracts disjoint destinations/nonoverlap source, handles 0/1/general scales, odd/unaligned tails, groups scalar and SIMD tables, and dispatches GFNI to its already optimal per-destination kernel. Differential coverage now spans counts 1,2,3,7,12,13,128; lengths 0..1023; offsets; guard bytes; init selftest scales 0/1/2/0x6c. Pinned 12-destination 1MiB benchmark: default scalar repeated 2.037s vs fused .902s (2.258x); AVX2 repeated .113 vs fused .105 (1.08x); GFNI dispatch nonregressing (separate runs approx neutral). AArch64 NEON QEMU differential and package/golden roundtrip passed. Whole residual phase after quotient+batch at K1000/bb2048 was 4.104ms versus pre-batch 6.775ms; K3200 6.350ms versus 17.841ms (machine/load sensitive, final whole-codec gate pending). Fable Max and local adversarial review both flagged an earlier byte-scalar regression; reproduced, replaced with grouped 8-byte table kernels, and expanded count-edge tests.
close_reason: Batched heavy RHS kernel validated for scalar/NEON/SSSE3/AVX2/GFNI, counts through 128, tails/unaligned data, full E2E and sanitizer/portability gates; scalar 2.26x kernel win and residual-phase gains.

title: Instrument and eliminate WH2 heavy-completion rank floor
description: Actual production-solver trials show WH2 zero-overhead failures around 0.36-0.54%. A reproduced K=10000 failure had R=221, binary rank=209, final rank=220: binary deficiency exactly H=12 but the projected 12x12 GF(256) heavy completion gained only 11 ranks. Add actual-solver deficiency/heavy-rank diagnostics, compare wire-compatible solve strategies and profile-versioned coefficient alternatives, and implement the smallest statistically supported correction.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostics distinguish binary deficiency from heavy rank gain. Candidate and baseline use identical packet schedules across boundary K values and OH0-OH3. At least 100k paired primary trials support any profile change; nonzero-payload E2E recovery, deterministic golden/profile contracts, and performance gates pass. If no safe correction exists, park with reproducible evidence and a versioned design.
notes:
Implemented actual-solver diagnostics in precodefail: per-cell binary-deficiency and heavy-rank-gain means/extrema/count histograms plus heavy-shortfall counts. Added experiment-only HashedNonzero full-column coefficient family and paired CLI selector; named/public profiles remain PeriodicCauchy. Primary paired gate: K=3200/OH0, 100000 trials, loss=0.10, seed=0x5eedf010, 96 threads. Periodic failed 411 (0.411%): binary def 12:99973|13:27, heavy gain 11:384|12:99616, heavy shortfalls 384, 20.509 ms mean. Hashed failed 409 (0.409%): identical deficiency schedule, heavy gain 11:382|12:99618, shortfalls 382, 20.991 ms (+2.35%). Removing 244-column periodicity does not improve the GF(256) square-completion floor; do not promote. Boundary K=9999/10000 OH0-3 10k paired grid completed: OH0 periodic 0.51% at both; hashed 0.36%/0.38% (sample variance, contradicted by 100k primary); OH1 zero; K=10000 OH2 one shared def=13>H failure; OH3 zero. Nonzero-payload lossy hashed actual-solver roundtrip and VerifyPrecodeSolution pass. Target build, precode solve test, and bench CLI test pass. Tiny-boundary 100k paired grid is still running.
Tiny/boundary certification: K=2 and K=5, OH0-3, 100k paired trials/family had zero failures; K=2 selected attempt 2 under both families. K=64 periodic OH0 346/100k (0.346%), hashed 368/100k (0.368%); periodic OH1 1/100k, hashed 0; OH2/OH3 zero. All OH0 K=64 failures were heavy shortfalls at binary def=12. MTU performance smoke K=3200/OH0/bb=1280, 500 paired trials: periodic and hashed both 1 fail; 16.584 vs 16.666ms mean (+0.49% hashed). Versioned design verdict: any alternate coefficient equations must bump the precode contract/profile because encoded heavy constraints change. Hashed full-column removal of periodicity is not a safe correction: 100k primary shows no reliability gain and a speed cost. The observed ~1/256 square-completion floor is generic to H equations completing the minimum H-dimensional binary nullspace; eliminating it needs a fundamentally different versioned construction/field, or one additional received equation (OH1 makes the heavy solve rectangular). Current evidence supports keeping the frozen profile and retaining diagnostics for future designs.
Final reproducibility commands: (1) primary: taskset -c 0-95 build/codec/wirehair_v2_bench precodefail --N 3200 --bb-list 1 --overhead 0 --trials 100000 --threads 96 --loss 0.10 --seed 1592651792 --heavy-family periodic,hashed. (2) N1 boundary: taskset -c 0-95 build/codec/wirehair_v2_bench precodefail --N 9999,10000 --bb-list 1 --overhead 0,1,2,3 --trials 10000 --threads 96 --loss 0.10 --seed 1592651793 --heavy-family periodic,hashed. (3) tiny boundary: taskset -c 0-95 build/codec/wirehair_v2_bench precodefail --N 2,5,64 --bb-list 1 --overhead 0,1,2,3 --trials 100000 --threads 96 --loss 0.10 --seed 1592651794 --heavy-family periodic,hashed. (4) pinned MTU timing: taskset -c 120 build/codec/wirehair_v2_bench precodefail --N 3200 --bb-list 1280 --overhead 0 --trials 200 --threads 1 --loss 0.10 --seed 1592651796 --heavy-family periodic,hashed. Pinned MTU: periodic 15.181ms, 87595.3 XORs, 5548.8 muladds; hashed 15.506ms (+2.14%), 84464.9 XORs, 41763.0 muladds (7.53x), with no recovery gain. Final code reports block-op means in addition to rank histograms. Validation: focused build succeeded; precode, precode_encode, precode_solve, profile, bench_cli CTest 5/5; hashed nonzero lossy roundtrips at bb=17 and bb=8192; git diff --check clean. Frozen profile unchanged.
close_reason: Closed under the explicit no-safe-correction clause: actual-solver diagnostics and a versioned full-column control prove the ~1/256 OH0 floor is generic GF(256) square completion, not the periodic Cauchy mapping. The candidate gives no 100k-trial recovery benefit and costs speed/block ops; public profile remains frozen.

title: Factor WH2 residual over GF(2) before the GF(256) quotient
description: SolvePrecodeSystem expands the full residual to GF(256) and residual elimination consumes 83-97% of solve wall time. Binary rows retain rank over GF(256), so factor their packed GF(2) span first, transform RHS using XOR, project heavy rows into the binary nullspace, and run GF(256) elimination only on the small heavy quotient.
acceptance_criteria: New solver is bit-for-bit recovery-equivalent to the current solver on deterministic paired systems, corrupt/inconsistent RHS cases, tiny and boundary K, scalar and SIMD builds. It measurably improves solve/create/decode throughput without recovery, resume, memory, sanitizer, portability, or wire regressions.
notes: Implemented exact wire-compatible two-stage residual solve for block_bytes>=2048: keep unused binary rows in GF(2) RREF, reduce heavy rows into its free-variable quotient, solve only q<=H GF(256) variables, reconstruct binary pivots by XOR. Below 2048 retains legacy insertion after paired crossover measurements. On rare deficient solves requesting resume, materialize the original combined R-column pivot checkpoint only then; no-resume failures avoid the fallback. Pinned phase A/B at bb2048: K64 wall 3.584->1.820ms (also includes empty-residue fix), K1000 8.481->7.868, K3200 22.840->21.691 before batched heavy kernel; at bb4096 K1000 13.779->12.397 and K3200 33.455->29.623. At bb102400 earlier paired residual reductions were ~340.5->254.7ms K1000 and 380.1->324.5ms K3200, though whole wall is load-sensitive. Dense oracle boundary test covers 2047/2048. Fable Max and independent agent review found the algebra sound, specifically confirming allow_insert=false preserves the binary basis and reconstruction coefficients stay 0/1; both required added >=2048 deficient resume, inconsistency, OOM/no-write, and nontrivial dense-oracle coverage, now being integrated before closure.
close_reason: Exact GF(2)-basis/GF(256)-quotient path validated against dense oracle, conflicting RHS, >=2048 deficient resume, Release 41/41, sanitizer 36/36, fuzz, SIMD and cross-architecture gates; measurable solve wins.

title: Optimize WH2 speed and recovery consistency versus legacy
description:
## Problem

The new WH2/V2 codec path has strong correctness coverage but needs a fresh measured pass focused jointly on throughput, decode latency, recovery probability, and tail consistency relative to the legacy codec.

## Evidence

codec/README.md exposes compare, precodecheck, precodefail, peelcost, densecheck, and resume benchmarks, while experiments/precode and experiments/peeling contain previously certified alternatives and cost models. No current bead owns an end-to-end production optimization pass after the serialized/incremental V2 integration.

## Steps to Reproduce

Build wirehair_v2_bench and run compare/precodefail across representative N and block sizes with fixed seeds, then profile encode/decode and inspect successful-overhead/failure distributions. Compare against the legacy path under the same message, loss, and trial schedules.

## Scope

Profile the production WH2 path, reproduce mathematical/recovery opportunities, implement only changes supported by paired evidence, and validate speed, memory, recovery rate, overhead tails, determinism, wire compatibility, and sanitizer/portability behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Publish reproducible V1/WH2 baselines across small, medium, large N and multiple block sizes. Implement and Beads-track independently reviewable improvements that provide a measurable speed or memory win without recovery regression, and/or statistically supported recovery/tail-consistency gains without unacceptable speed cost. Preserve deterministic profiles and serialized packet contracts unless an explicit new profile version is documented. Pass strict full CTest, sanitizer, fuzz/property, package/ABI, cross-architecture, and high-trial paired recovery gates; document rejected ideas and tradeoffs.
notes:
Measured pinned baselines before source edits (compare --precode): WH2 versus legacy remained much slower but had tighter overhead tails. Representative WH2 before: K64/bb1280 create 35.1, decode 36.6 MB/s; K1000/bb1280 126.6/190.7; K3200/bb1280 107.4/195.8. Legacy was 839.9/632.0, 1941.2/1128.5, and 1998.4/1161.8 respectively. At bb102400 WH2 K64 was 37.4/37.4 and K1000 287.3/287.6 versus legacy 843.1/584.0 and 1559.8/864.1. Profiling put 83-97% of solve wall in residual work. Current integrated Release compare (30/20/10 trials, common IID loss pending final trace patch): WH2 K64/bb1280 create/decode 59.7/64.7; K1000 265.6/317.1; K3200 351.1/494.6. At bb102400: 55.6/55.0, 239.7/253.2, 490.2/438.4. K2 empty-residue fix independently improved create/decode 5.0-5.7x. Encoder init zero-copy staging saved 12,288 KiB at K10000*1280 and 98,304 KiB at K1000*102400. Decoder receive map improved unique K10k*1280 receive 29.8% and late duplicates ~139x; K64k/bb1 late duplicates ~3568x. Actual solver recovery: K1000/3200/10000 OH0 failures 0.54/0.36/0.37%; reproduced deficiency=H=12 and heavy gain=11. Paired 100k K3200: periodic 411 failures vs nonperiodic hashed 409 (no improvement, hashed slower), proving generic square-GF256 completion floor. Shipping profile stays frozen.
Final integrated evidence: systematic source cache improves systematic throughput 1.94-2.70x and 10% loss workload about 4.05x opt-in; CSR equation/adjacency pooling cuts allocation lower bounds to 5, peak row storage 16-20%, and cold solve latency 11-21%; quotient GF(2)-then-GF(256), fused heavy RHS, prime caches, duplicate map, empty-residue skip, portable bit scans, and zero-copy initialization all passed exact-oracle/no-write checks. title: Make installed C++ standard propagation test portable to MSVC
description:
## Problem

The installed C++ consumer correctly verifies that wirehair::wirehair publishes cxx_std_11, but its source separately rejects MSVC because __cplusplus remains 199711L unless /Zc:__cplusplus is requested, even in a conforming C++14-or-newer mode.

## Evidence

Hosted run 29128445380 static MSVC job 86478909934 builds all library/tests and passes CTest 32/32, then test/package/consumer.cpp:9-10 raises its own #error while the exported target property check has already passed.

## Steps to Reproduce

Configure a static installed-package consumer with Visual Studio 17 2022. CMake confirms INTERFACE_COMPILE_FEATURES includes cxx_std_11 and upgrades the requested C++98 target, but compilation fails on the non-portable __cplusplus preprocessor test.

## Scope

Use a compiler-portable proof of C++11 feature propagation without requiring consumers to enable an unrelated MSVC conformance-reporting flag.
acceptance_criteria: Static/shared/dual installed C++ consumers still request C++98, verify cxx_std_11 on the imported target, compile C++11-only header/API constructs, and run. Native MSVC static and shared package flows pass under /W4 /WX without /Zc:__cplusplus being required.
notes:
Removed the redundant non-portable __cplusplus preprocessor rejection. The external consumer still starts from CXX_STANDARD 98, requires the imported target to list cxx_std_11, and compiles/runs std::array, static_assert, uniform initialization, and the C++ RAII V2 API, so both declarative and actual feature propagation remain tested. Local relocated package static/shared/both E2E passed 3/3; strict focused profile/package 4/4 and diff check pass. Await hosted MSVC.
Hosted acceptance passed at exact commit 06d80d1 in run 29128713010. MSVC static job 86479665302 compiled the imported C++ consumer without /Zc:__cplusplus, verified the exported cxx_std_11 property, and passed installed C/C++/plugin 3/3; MSVC shared job 86479665269 passed the same package flow 3/3. Run: https://github.com/catid/wirehair/actions/runs/29128713010.
close_reason: Portable imported-target C++11 propagation is verified locally in all package variants and by hosted strict MSVC static/shared installed consumers.

title: Stage the Wirehair DLL for the V2 profile test on Windows
description:
## Problem

In shared Windows builds, the V2 public-profile test executable is emitted under the codec configuration directory while wirehair.dll is emitted in the root configuration directory. Windows has no build-tree RPATH, so CTest cannot start the executable.

## Evidence

Hosted run 29128445380 shared MSVC job 86478909961 compiles warning-clean and passes 30/31 selected tests; wirehair_v2_profile_test alone exits 0xc0000135 before main, the Windows loader status for a missing dependency.

## Steps to Reproduce

Configure BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON with Visual Studio 17 2022, build Release, then run the codec profile test through CTest without adding the root Release directory to PATH. The loader cannot locate wirehair.dll beside codec/Release/wirehair_v2_profile_test.exe.

## Scope

Make the test self-contained on Windows by staging its linked Wirehair DLL beside the executable or setting an equally robust test runtime environment, without affecting installed layouts.
acceptance_criteria: The shared Windows V2 profile test starts and passes via CTest and direct execution with no manually prepared PATH. Static builds remain unchanged. Linux/macOS build-tree behavior and exact public ABI tests continue to pass.
notes:
Added a Windows/shared-only POST_BUILD staging command that copies $<TARGET_FILE:wirehair> beside wirehair_v2_profile_test using configuration-aware target-file generator expressions. A generation probe with WIN32 and shared primary confirms the exact copy_if_different rule; static configurations remain untouched. Fresh strict shared-primary build passed the profile test through CTest and direct execution; Clang ASan+UBSan profile passed; local package/profile focus passed 4/4. Await native Windows loader validation.
Hosted acceptance passed at exact commit 06d80d1: shared MSVC job 86479665269 staged wirehair.dll beside codec/Release/wirehair_v2_profile_test.exe; the test started and passed in the 31/31 CTest graph. Static job 86479665302 remained unchanged and passed 32/32. Run: https://github.com/catid/wirehair/actions/runs/29128713010.
close_reason: Configuration-aware DLL staging makes the V2 profile test runnable on native Windows; hosted shared/static MSVC and local strict/shared/sanitizer tests pass.

title: Keep newly added audit tests warning-clean under strict MSVC
description:
## Problem

Hosted native Windows builds for commit f898d5c configure successfully but fail under /W4 /WX because newly added audit tests contain implicit narrowing and constant-condition constructs diagnosed by MSVC.

## Evidence

Run 29123055555 jobs 86462408135 and 86462408179 report C4244 at test/PeelAvalancheTest.cpp:267, C4127 at test/LegacyCoreTest.cpp:352-359, and C4267 at LegacyCoreTest.cpp:1756,1771,1841,1989.

## Steps to Reproduce

Push f898d5c and inspect the two Windows jobs in run 29123055555, or compile all test targets with MSVC 19.44 using /W4 /WX. Configuration succeeds, then peel_avalanche_test and legacy_core_test fail during compilation on the diagnostics above.

## Scope

Make the test expressions type-correct and warning-clean without suppressions, then re-run local strict gates and hosted MSVC static/shared end to end.
acceptance_criteria: Both hosted windows-2022 MSVC static and shared jobs compile every target with /W4 /WX and pass their complete CTest/tool/package flows. No warning suppression is added. Local strict Release tests and focused regressions pass, and a source review finds no equivalent new narrowing/constant-condition defects.
notes:
Implemented minimal warning-clean corrections: use a uint8_t fill value; replace compile-time CHECK expressions with C++11 static_asserts; pass the already-typed uint32_t block_bytes capacity instead of narrowing vector::size() at the four reported encode sites. No suppression added. Local strict Release build is warning-clean; focused Clang ASan+UBSan legacy/peel 5/5 and Python/runner 69/69 pass. Full Release CTest is running before push.
Final local validation on the settled fix: strict GCC Release full CTest 41/41, including static/shared/both packaging and build-policy E2E; focused Clang ASan+UBSan legacy/peel 5/5; Python runner/portability/binding 69/69; git diff --check clean. Repeated warning-source review against both native MSVC logs confirms every reported C4127/C4244/C4267 site is corrected without suppression. Await hosted native MSVC static/shared.
Hosted run 29128445380 confirms every prior C4127/C4244/C4267 warning is fixed: both MSVC cells compile all targets warning-clean. Full E2E exposed two subsequent independent defects now tracked as blocking bugs: wirehair-95cy (non-portable __cplusplus assertion in installed C++ consumer; static job 86478909934) and wirehair-o7ea (shared V2 profile test cannot locate wirehair.dll; shared job 86478909961).
Final hosted acceptance at 06d80d1: native MSVC static job 86479665302 passed warning-clean build, CTest 32/32, installed consumers 3/3, and tool smoke; shared job 86479665269 passed warning-clean build, CTest 31/31, and installed consumers 3/3. No warning suppression was added. Run 29128713010: https://github.com/catid/wirehair/actions/runs/29128713010.
