Instead, for exact K=8 systematic ids only, screen a transient stack pointer-gather plus existing EvaluatePacketSetXor path after current validation/alias checks. Add no persistent source storage or allocation; every repair id and K!=8 stays on the old path.
acceptance_criteria: Differential K8 ids0-7 against scalar evaluation across SIMD/block/tail boundaries, all evaluator entry points, aliases/no-write and OOM; test-hook counter proves systematic use and repair fallback. Explicit false/null/true cache semantics stay unchanged. Paired first-K scope must gain at least1%; repair-only and K32 controls must remain within2%, with exact bytes/work counters and strict/sanitizer/source audits before promotion.
notes: REJECTED after same-binary scheduler A/B. Equation-neutral K8 systematic set-XOR was screened in two forms. All 5-7 term rows regressed cross-binary K8/B64 1.0154 and B1280 1.0049. Restricting to the existing >=6-term crossover produced unstable cross-binary apparent gains while semantically false K32/K100 controls swung about -1.6%..+1.0%, proving layout/frequency confounding. A test-hook same-binary ABBA/BAAB harness (SHA 926abbeb617d6f94f16d97e5a43173c8240ab1357f672629f0c82de81031745a) forced current tail-paired vs set-XOR schedules with identical layout: B64 inner8192 ratio .996579 CI[.991663,1.001520] (neutral); B1280 inner4096 ratio1.011044 CI[1.006746,1.015360] and independent inner1024 ratio1.012762 CI[1.008903,1.016636] (resolved slower); B4096 1.001881 CI[.998486,1.005286]. Repair-only cross-binary controls were neutral B64 .99852 CI[.98442,1.01282], B1280 .99575 CI[.98381,1.00784]. Therefore set-XOR does not improve the real scheduler and violates speed objective. Keep promoted head4a635b5 unchanged; no code promotion.
close_reason: Rejected: identical-layout A/B shows B1280 set-XOR 1.1-1.3% slower and B64 neutral.

title: Screen single-word affine projection for tiny WH2 solves
description: Implement and bound-screen an equation-neutral pure-GF256 specialization for affine projection when 1 <= inactive rank R <= 64. Accumulate the one-word projection directly for peeled and unused rows while preserving the existing multiword path exactly. This is a speed-only experiment for the remaining tiny/narrow decoder-solve veto; it must not change recovery architecture, seeds, equations, decoded bytes, overhead, or logical counters.
design: Gate only on words == 1. XOR inactive bits or the existing one-word peeled projection into a local uint64_t; retain the current payload XOR and all words != 1 code. Do not combine with residual-policy, storage, field, or equation changes. Historical 1941cb6 is hypothesis-only and must not be cherry-picked.
acceptance_criteria: Forced old/new correctness oracle covers R=1,63,64,65 plus cold success, deficient resume, duplicate/conflict, OOM, partial tails, and byte/packed residual policies. Twelve-round paired short screen covers K=8,32,100 at B=64,1280; seam follow-up covers K=189,190,191,384,448,1000. Reject any semantic/counter difference, any cell >2% slower, any resolved multiword slowdown, or eligible aggregate improvement below 1%. Require ordinary receive-to-success to resolve faster and direct-systematic traces to remain within 2% before promotion. Run focused Release, ASan/UBSan, and repeated source-reading bug hunts.
close_reason: Promoted: exact semantics and all correctness/compiler gates pass; tiny solve 4.19% faster, ordinary receive 5.52% faster, encoder path 4.25% faster, direct and multiword fallthrough within no-regression gates.

title: Screen one-word packed GF(2) replay for tiny/narrow WH2
description: At exact integration commit 8532963, K8/B64 and K100/B64 decoder receive solves have residual ranks 12 and 36, both one packed word, but decoder checkpoint policy selects the byte-expanded residual basis. Use the existing test-hook packed mode to run a same-binary forced-OFF/ON corrected native receive-to-success screen on frozen traces with isolated SMT siblings and A/A controls. Preserve equations, decoded bytes, outcomes, overhead, and logical work; include authentic deficient/resume/OOM coverage before any production dispatch change.
acceptance_criteria: Exact same-binary K8/K100 B64 frozen-trace evidence has valid A/A, isolated worker/controller siblings, thermal/EDAC attestation, and identical bytes/outcome/overhead/logical work. Retain only if every forced-ON/OFF cell is <=1.02 and the aggregate resolves faster; otherwise reject and stop without source promotion.
notes:
REJECTED bounded replay at exact 8532963a435691e988147e9606f265bf3bdbe523 (2026-08-06 UTC). Same hooks-enabled Release binary SHA-256 2c0d455c04ae23fc8d097a8a3080fc2c8e9c8e4b5425b51649c86963400225d8 forced byte OFF (-1) and packed ON (+1) on CPU125/core61 with sibling CPU61 free of pinned load. First eight frozen retry-0 B64 traces at K8 (ordinals 0..7) and K100 (16..23), formal invocations/slot 8192 and 656, corrected all-feed-through-first-success plus Recover scope, off/off and on/on A/A plus ON/OFF self-counterbalanced panels. All 16 cells decoded exact bytes at overhead 0; hook engagement exact (OFF uses 0, ON one use per invocation). Companion K+4 cold solves matched packet rows, peel/inactivation/residual rows and ranks, binary row topology/storage/allocations, and packet seed attempt; packed deliberately changed physical work (fewer muladds, sometimes more XORs). Existing precode solve differential passed authentic q=H NeedMore/resume, crossover, zero-budget suppression, and transactional bad_alloc/length_error cases; native codec/frozen timing tests also passed. A/A valid/tight: maximum raw ratio 1.001330. ON/OFF: K8 geometric 1.028347, log95 [0.023943,0.031963], max cell 1.037319 (all 8 cells >1.02); K100 geometric 0.960337, log95 [-0.045346,-0.035596], max 0.970586; aggregate geometric 0.993760, log95 [-0.025287,0.012769], unresolved. Fails both mandatory gates: per-cell <=1.02 and aggregate resolves faster. Stop; do not promote packed dispatch at one-word tiny/narrow cells. Artifact JSONL SHA-256 908e9fe4bc215c8c6749cee53a28883f1d6b2dcea631f0a86be16b5ff9f31999 at /dev/shm/wh2-smallk-packed-screen/artifacts/replay.jsonl. Thermal slice SHA-256 3b056f97259872d763b1ddadd7ae62480f1585af12758a7e808631c73ab70229: 12 rows, CPU 69.312C mean/69.625C max, hottest DIMM 44.021C mean/44.250C max, read errors/EDAC CE/UE all zero.
Physical operation deltas explain the crossover but do not rescue promotion: across K8 cells packed averaged +0.25 BlockXors (range 0..+2) and -14 BlockMulAdds (-21..-7) yet end-to-end receive was 2.83% slower, so one-word packing/materialization/control overhead dominates the small arithmetic saving. At K100 it averaged +77.125 XORs (+69..+87) and -154 muladds (-167..-141), enough arithmetic conversion to make receive 3.97% faster. Keep the existing B64 decoder byte threshold; a single one-word rule cannot serve both tiny and narrow K.
close_reason: Verified and rejected: forced packed replay regresses every K8/B64 cell, exceeds 1.02, and aggregate speed is unresolved despite K100 gain; no source promotion.

title: Reject WH2 cold-solve stats checkpoint aliases
description: Cold SolvePrecodeSystem accepts stats == &resume_state->Stats, a valid typed alias. On the documented over-cap NeedMore path it publishes diagnostic stats while promising cap failure leaves resume_state unchanged, thereby mutating the checkpoint through the aliased pointer. A root 541ff4e K=5000 duplicate-row probe returned NeedMore with output and sentinel state storage/scalars unchanged, but state.Stats.PacketRows changed 0x2468ace0 -> 5000 and InactivatedColumns -> 5014. Reject this exact alias before work, analogous to checkpoint/output vector guards, because both output contracts cannot be satisfied simultaneously.
acceptance_criteria: Every cold SolvePrecodeSystem overload returns InvalidInput before allocation or mutation when resume_state is non-null and stats == &resume_state->Stats; state contents, stats, vector backing identities/capacities, PersistentBytes, and output remain exact. Disjoint stats behavior on over-cap NeedMore, rank-deficient checkpoint publication, success, OOM, and validation failures remains unchanged. Header contract, strict Release, ASan+UBSan, MSan, and repeated source passes are clean.
notes: Integrated as 068b7a1 on top of 18d60e3. Exact pre-fix K=5000 over-cap reproduction changed aliased checkpoint Stats (PacketRows 0x2468ace0 to 5000; InactivatedColumns 0x13579bdf to 5015). Shared implementation now rejects exact stats/checkpoint alias before validation, row work, or allocation across public/runtime/validated entry points. Root combined verification: strict GCC13 Release solve/profile/decode/transactional/roundtrip all PASS; GCC ASan+UBSan solve PASS; Clang18 MSan solve PASS; exact state bytes, vector backing/capacity, PersistentBytes, and output no-write tests pass. title: Receipt benchmark exec success with a CLOEXEC handshake
description: The holdout's Python PDEATH wrapper can exit 125/126 or fail os.execv before the benchmark is ever executed. The controller currently receipts only the final child return code; if live exec observation loses the race, a wrapper/infrastructure exit is conservatively classified as a codec exit and permanently blocks promotion after a successful retry.
design: Create a parent-owned close-on-exec handshake pipe before Popen. The wrapper writes a bounded canonical failure receipt on every pre-exec failure; successful exec is proved only by EOF caused by CLOEXEC. Bind that evidence to the attempt PID/start identity and segment manifest without adding a timing-dependent /proc requirement. Preserve fail-closed behavior for torn/missing/ambiguous handshake evidence and controller-caused signal exits.
acceptance_criteria: Focused race/mutation tests distinguish wrapper 125/126/exec errors from genuine benchmark nonzero exits, including ultra-fast exit, abort, timeout, controller crash, partial receipt and PID reuse. Historical promotion treats proved wrapper failures as infrastructure but never erases a genuine codec exit. Full controller suite and repeated source review pass.
close_reason: Campaign-controller hardening is outside the focused codec critical path; bounded screens use minimal local receipts and the final gate owns release evidence.

title: Remove common H=12 fixed-H classifier heap allocations
description: The exact-final q>H fixed-H classifier improves packed cold-tail solve time by 15.33% at q25 and 17.11% at q76, but q13 remains flat. The common certified H=12 path currently allocates separate tiny vectors for the H-by-H basis, pivot flags, and working column; allocator overhead is a plausible reason the q13 gain is hidden. Add an allocation-free common-H representation with a validated dynamic fallback for experimental H up to 128, without changing algebra, receipts, or uncommon behavior.
design: Keep the existing streaming column-span and syndrome algorithms. Use bounded inline storage only for the production H=12-or-smaller case and retain the current checked dynamic path for H=13..128. Avoid adding a 16 KiB object to every solve stack frame; scope common-H scratch to the q>H helper call. Preserve the reported coefficient-storage metric as logical coefficient bytes and add a separate test diagnostic only if needed to prove zero classifier heap allocations.
acceptance_criteria: Dense packed/byte oracle covers H=0..128 boundary cases and produces byte-identical rank, pivot profile, syndromes, conflict order, counters, and terminal results versus the current implementation. H=0, q=H, q=H+1, q13/q25/q76, retained checkpoints, OOM hooks, and no-write semantics pass. Exact pinned ABBA against the fixed-H landing commit shows a reproducible q13 packed cold or retained-init improvement without a resolved q25/q76 or byte-path regression; otherwise reject the inline-storage change. Strict/no-hooks, ASan+UBSan, solve/decode/roundtrip/fingerprint, and repeated source audits pass.

Do not inline 128x128. Add explicit helper H<=128 guards, fallback oracle cases H=13,63,64,65,127,128 and reject 129. A test-hook-only dynamic-allocation counter can prove 0 allocations at H<=12 and 3 at H=13 without production branches. title: Fuse WH2 packet-slot lookup and insertion on decoder feed
description: WH2 normal decoder acceptance currently calls PacketSlotTable::Find and then Insert, hashing and probing an absent packet ID twice; at the half-capacity growth seam the target is searched three times. Fuse lookup and insertion without changing duplicate precedence, accepted-equation bounds, terminal behavior, transient-OOM replay, payload rollback, wire/profile behavior, or the concurrency contract.
design: Add tri-state FindOrInsert(Found/Inserted/Limit). Probe before enforcing EntryLimit; insert into the cached hole below the growth threshold; otherwise transactionally grow and reuse the cached hash in the new table. Preserve Insert as a wrapper. Use the fused operation on ordinary cold/resume acceptance paths while retaining lookup-only handling for poisoned terminal state, storage overflow, and unresolved pending-OOM replay. Preserve cold payload-vector rollback through Erase. Do not introduce a prepare/commit token.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover original-slot preservation, duplicate-at-full precedence, exact limit, arbitrary uint32 IDs/slots, grow success/OOM, clustered wraparound/backshift chains, wrapper parity, payload rollback, pending replay, terminal duplicates, and solve-OOM retry. Test hooks prove one normal lookup walk. Focused CTest, transactional tests, bounded stateful fuzz, ASan+UBSan, strict/no-hooks builds, and repeated clean source-reading bug passes succeed. Pinned same-source ABBA shows at least 10% lower small-width unique-prefix ns/packet, at least 3% decoder-feed improvement at bb=2 across K=64/1000/10000/64000, and no resolved >2% decoder-feed/full-decode regression at bb=1280/4096, all with exact semantic equality.
notes:
2026-07-30 preimplementation audit: use tri-state FindOrInsert {Found, Inserted, Limit}, probing before EntryLimit/growth, preserving the original slot on Found, caching the old-table hole below growth, and reusing only the incoming hash after transactional growth. Retain lookup-only handling for terminal Error, storage overflow, malformed/unresolved pending-OOM state; preserve duplicate precedence. Cold insertion snapshots and rolls back both receive vectors plus Erase before systematic-cache mutation. title: Peel search results must be validated against an unmodified codec
description:
Any search over peel parameters MUST verify its winner against a genuinely
unmodified codec before the result is believed. tools/peel_validate.py does
this; it exists because the proxy-ranked sweep produced regressions that
looked like wins.

Evidence: of 11 small-K anchors from the first ladder sweep, SIX were worse
than shipped once measured end to end. At large K the same check caught -16.3%
(K=4096), -25.3% (K=8192) and -54.6% (K=16384).

WHY AN IN-SEARCH INCUMBENT GUARD IS NOT ENOUGH. The obvious fix -- put the
shipped point in the candidate pool -- cannot express the incumbent here. The
shipped staircase degree scale is a sentinel (kStaircaseDegreeScaleUnset =
-1.0) that makes the codec compute the scale internally, so any pool entry
must name SOME scale and is therefore a hybrid: shipped law at a searched
scale, which is neither arm. That hybrid measured 1145.9 MB/s at K=4096 where
the true shipped point measures 1239.2 -- the guard guaranteed nothing.

The only honest shipped measurement is a run with NO overrides at all: no
WIREHAIR_V2_PEEL_DEGREES, no scale flag.

A 2% margin is required before a trained point may displace shipped.
Single-shot goodput carries a few percent of noise, and the trade is not free:
K=11 "won" by +0.2% while needing 1.3% of K in extra packets.

Also worth fixing in the validator: it uses a flat trial count at every K. At
K=8192 with a 4096-byte payload that is ~67 GB of data movement per arm and
takes 8 minutes for ONE measurement. Trials should scale down with K, since
throughput converges fast and failures are ~0 up there.

title: essearch coordinate boxes do not match what the codec builds (silent K loss)
description:
Two coordinate-box defects silently truncated the peel search. Both are fixed
in tools/peel_funnel.py, but the same class of bug is likely elsewhere in the
ES/essearch coordinate handling and the boxes are not derived from the codec.

1. --s-hi capped the staircase count S at 80, but the codec builds
   GetDenseCount(16384) = 114, rising to 390 near K=52224. Every block count
   at or above 16384 was rejected BEFORE a single candidate was evaluated, and
   the sweep reported only "FAILED to produce a winner". Box widened to [1,400].

2. --s-lo floored S at 2 where SmallBandStaircaseCount(2) = 1, which had
   already cost the K=2 anchor.

Neither produced an error at the point of failure -- the sweep just lost K
values. Worth auditing the other ES coordinate boxes against what the codec
actually builds, and making the failure loud: a config rejected for being
outside a box should say so per-K rather than surfacing as an empty result.

Related: essearch also has a CALIBRATED COST MODEL at only 26 block counts
(2 3 4 6 8 12 16 24 32 48 64 96 128 192 256 384 512 768 1024 1536 2048 4096
8192 16384 32768 64000) and rejects every other K outright, which is why an
every-1024 training grid produced nothing above K=4096. That constraint should
be documented where the sweep grid is chosen.

title: ES trainer audit: meta-grid result invalid, degree-shape search unconstrained
description:
Independent audit of the two ES trainers found 15 defects. Two invalidate results already reported.

S1 CRITICAL - the ES hyperparameter meta-grid measured RANDOM-SEARCH COVERAGE, not optimizer quality. meta_es.py tracked best = min(best, vals.min()) over every candidate ever evaluated, and evaluate() is a DETERMINISTIC function of the quantized tuple (all subprocess seeds are fixed constants). So the reported score is a min over every integer tuple the run happened to visit, and the final theta - the actual output of the ES - has no influence on it at all. With a 240-evaluation budget against a space of only 9*4*3*22 = 2376 points, this is close to random search with 240 draws. Larger sigma and larger lr spread the sampling wider, visit more distinct tuples, and therefore win regardless of whether the search converges. CONSEQUENCE: the conclusions 'sigma=0.7, lr=0.8, pop=8 is best' and 'low learning rate is worst' are both unsupported and are retracted. Fix: score the FINAL theta, not the running min.

S2 CRITICAL - es_degree.py, which produced the learned degree distributions and the 3D plot, has NO failure-rate constraint; it minimizes raw inact_mu. Worse, WirehairV2Bench.cpp:5657 accumulates inactivated columns for EVERY trial including failures and divides by trials, so a shape that fails more often - and fails EARLIER, with fewer columns inactivated at the point of rank failure - scores LOWER. The search was free to buy inactivation reductions with failure rate and nothing in the output would reveal it. The K=32/64/128 shapes and the reported 6.4/16.5/19.7 percent gains must be re-validated with the constraint applied before they are believed.

S4 HIGH - the u/(1-u) antithetic dither I added on user suggestion is the WORST of the three couplings, not the best. Measured over 400k draws, variance of the paired quantized difference: u/(1-u) 0.51-0.91, shared u 0.21-0.24, independent 0.26-0.46. It makes the two roundings anti-correlated so the pair jumps by 2 or 0 instead of 1 or 0. My code comment claiming it 'cancels the rounding bias exactly rather than only in expectation' is false - all three couplings are unbiased. Sharing u within the pair is the true minimum-variance control variate. This is 2.4-4.3x the noise on the only estimator the ES has.

S5 HIGH - rank shaping ignores ties, and ties dominate at small sigma. Mirrored pairs frequently quantize identically, giving d == 0 exactly: measured tie rate 59.9 percent at sigma=0.15, 26.9 at 0.35, 5.8 at 0.70, 1.0 at 1.20. Tied pairs carry zero information but receive full-magnitude +/-0.5 weights. At pop=8 all four differences can be zero, making the step a pure random walk. Because the tie rate is monotone in sigma, the meta-grid systematically penalized small sigma as a pure artifact - so the sigma conclusion was confounded twice over, independently of S1.

S9 MEDIUM - es_degree.py's knot map is rank-deficient when K < dims. With --dims 10, at K=2 the interpolation returns theta[0] and theta[9] exactly and theta[1..8] have literally zero effect on the objective; K=4 leaves 6 null directions, K=8 leaves 2. So the 'no gain below K=32' finding is partly an artifact of the parameterization rather than a property of the problem, and the saved theta at small K is mostly noise.

Other findings: S3 both-fail gives inf-inf = NaN which numpy sorts LAST, producing a maximum-strength wrong-way gradient on garbage; S6 unequal budget (pop=32 received 224 evaluations, not 240, from gens = evals//pop truncation); S7 one scalar sigma shared across coordinates of width 8/3/2/21, so a sigma large enough to move S drives N1 entirely into the clip; S8 the constraint is estimated from a fixed 1000-trial sample with SE 0.62pp against a 4.0 percent threshold and never re-checked on held-out seeds, so it is exploitable; S10 serial evaluations in the parent while the worker pool idles; S12 subprocess returncode never checked and partial seed coverage silently breaks CRN pairing; S13/S14/S15 minor.

VERIFIED CORRECT, do not re-investigate: gradient sign in both files, the half*sigma divisor (a factor of 2 absorbed into lr), theta clipping does NOT pin parameters at bounds (the gradient halves but keeps the right sign, so they recover), no mutable defaults or closure bugs, reproducible RNG streams.

WHAT STANDS - everything measured WITHOUT the ES is unaffected: the S-from-GetDenseCount bug, the H=8 band trim, N1=1 (direct A/B with a significance test), the exhaustive K=128 grid showing H=6/S=4 beats WH1 on both speed and error, and the aggregate 2.15 -> 1.25 improvement from direct race measurement.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid meta-grid and degree-shape claims remain retracted. Before closure, either restore/version the missing trainers or explicitly retire and replace them; the implemented path must score the final candidate, constrain recovery on independent held-out seeds, use success-conditioned cost or an explicit failure penalty, handle tied and both-fail pairs, equalize evaluation budgets, remove small-K null dimensions, check every subprocess/seed receipt fail-closed, and include focused regression tests. Update all stale source citations and record reproducible validation evidence.

title: Tiny-K exact MDS path: K=1/K=2 special case, and the MDS-vs-precode crossover
description:
SIDE-QUEST RESULT, parked for later. For K=2 an exact MDS code on the projective line over GF(256) beats both codecs by orders of magnitude with ZERO failure probability.

Construction: map block id to a coefficient pair - id 0 -> [1:0] = A (systematic), id 1 -> [0:1] = B (systematic), id i>=2 -> [1:c] with c = i-1 in [1,255]. These are exactly the 257 points of P^1(GF(256)), so any two distinct ids give determinant c_j ^ c_i != 0. Verified exhaustively: all C(257,2) = 32,896 id pairs decode correctly, 0 failures, at bb=2/8/64. Prototype at scratchpad/k2mds.cpp.

Measured at K=2: init + 2 systematic symbols 2.8 ns, per repair symbol 4.2-6.5 ns, decode from two repair symbols 9.5-17 ns. Compare WH2 general path 1803 ns and WH1 830 ns at the same K, both with 2.4 percent untuned failure. So roughly 640x faster than WH2, 300x faster than WH1, and the failure rate goes to exactly zero rather than 2.4 percent. K=1 is the degenerate case of the same code (every symbol a copy).

CROSSOVER (systematic Cauchy MDS vs the precode) is NOT a K threshold - it is a repair-count threshold, because the cost structures are opposite: MDS has ~zero init and pays K muladds x block_bytes per repair, while WH2 pays a large fixed init and ~3 mixed columns per repair independent of K. MDS wins while R*(K-d)*bb < init_wh2(K). Measured (scratchpad/mdsk.cpp): at bb=1024, K=32 MDS is 196 ns init + 493 ns per repair against WH2 init 6821 ns -> crossover near 16 repair symbols; K=100 is 799 ns + 1544 ns against 18258 ns -> near 13 repairs. At bb=2 and K=100 the crossover is near 120 repairs. WH2 init was measured at bb=2 and its flat floor grows 6.2 -> 9.1 us going bb=2 -> 1024, so those crossovers are lower bounds.

LITERATURE (user pointer, github.com/catid/cm256): CM256 is a GF(256) Cauchy MDS codec whose decode uses an O(N^2) LDU decomposition for Cauchy systems (Boros/Kailath/Olshevsky, 'Pivoting and backward stability of fast algorithms for solving Cauchy linear equations') rather than O(N^3) Gaussian elimination, and reports ~2x Longhair. Longhair (same author) is Jerasure-style Cauchy Reed-Solomon that expands each GF(256) element into an 8x8 bit matrix so encoding is pure XOR with no GF multiplies at all - the extreme version of minimizing GF(256) work while staying MDS - and reports ~3x Jerasure. The first Cauchy row normalizes to all ones, making one recovery symbol a plain XOR; CM256 shows 23 GB/s at one recovery block against 178 MB/s at fifty.

If picked up: ship K=1 and K=2 as exact MDS special cases first (unambiguous win, zero failure). Above that the decision is the deployment's repair budget, not K. Note the randomization idea for hitting a 1 percent target does not apply in the MDS regime - no loss pattern can do worse than zero - it only applies once K+R exceeds 256.
notes: Implemented on feat/wh2-k2mds-4azp from 51fd529 as explicit public profile WIREHAIR_V2_PROFILE_TINY_MDS_2026_07 (ID bf014b3fef75d128; canonical SHA-256 bf014b3fef75d128dc78d1dee5efc9f240e9df36db42db527466073e9ecba74c). K1 is repetition for all uint32 packet IDs; K2 maps IDs 0..256 to all P^1(GF256) directions and rejects larger IDs. Default CURRENT and dispatch-v1 are unchanged. Located original /tmp prototypes k2mds.cpp (sha256 651d77f3b675a51b76cc69e200590a8e37e23ca6c705af3796eafc8fe39992bb) and mdsk.cpp (a1b3a42297252f71d9ed46e02aee0b70b5ea6b44d24d54b0dd337d803aaa1cfe); the existing feat/wh2-tinyk-fastpath branch concerns the separate equation-preserving mixed-completion fast path, not exact MDS. title: WH2 peel: lazy-heap stale-pop pathology at mid-K instances
description: Peel-stage substage timers on feat/wh2-peel-fastpath (commit 848190e) show the degree-two lazy-heap selection phase is instance-dependent: mixed-p244-d4 seed 0xC0FFEE at K=8192 spends ~457us (33% of the 1.4ms peel) popping stale heap keys across 150 inactivation selections, while K=64000 spends only 156us across 571. An indexed (decrease-key) heap gives a provably identical argmax but back-of-envelope trades ~25k per-update sifts (~1ms) for the ~1k stale pops, so it likely regresses typical cells; a hybrid (rebuild-on-stale-burst) or per-refs bucket scan may cap the pathology. Any replacement must reproduce the exact selection sequence: argmax over live columns with refs>0 of key=(degree_two_refs<<32)|tie_rank.

2026-07-30 preimplementation proof: current-key-only compaction is exact at the queue-drained heap-selection seam. Every degree-two increment pushes the new current key; every decrement turns a live-two row into a singleton and immediately queues its other column; the singleton queue drains transitively before heap selection. Therefore an unresolved column cannot survive a decrement to another selection boundary, its reference count is monotone while unresolved, and its unique current key exists. Rebuild exactly one key for each unresolved column with refs>0; historical levels are unnecessary. First rebaseline the recorded K8192/C0FFEE pathology on current HEAD, then screen bounded stale-pop thresholds and retain only an A/A-clear realistic-payload full-solve win with exact selection/output equality.

title: Screen segmented-anchor plus degree-balanced composition
description: Test whether the raw four-0369 D12 segmented-anchor winner composes with deterministic degree-balanced staircase matching. Both changes preserve row/column counts and GF work and affect different binary substructures, so the combination may repair additional hard-loss cells at near-zero solve cost; interactions may also erase gains, so do not infer additivity. Compare four raw arms on identical K/seeds/schedules: two-anchor baseline, four-0369 only, degree-balanced only, and combined. Apply no K seed fixes, graph normalization, or outcome-selected cells.
acceptance_criteria: Report failures, repairs/introductions, weak-K count and multiplicity, q strata, per-seed/schedule results, paired XOR/muladd/inactivation work, and full-payload solve timing. Promote the composition over four-0369 only if recovery is Pareto-better or convincingly lower in aggregate without a material consistency regression and the isolated timing one-sided slowdown bound remains below 1%; otherwise retain the best individual raw architecture. Any later seed repair is a separate post-selection stage.
close_reason: Closed on component evidence without a combined campaign: degree-balanced staircase is speed-neutral (1.00077, CI crossing 1; bead 16.1.16.4) and segmented anchors carry a ~2.44% solve regression failing the <=1% gate in isolation (bead 16.1.17, sealed 2026-07-21). The composition's anchor cost is phase-additive and cannot be offset by degree balancing, so it cannot pass the same sealed speed gate; running the 4-arm campaign cannot change the promotion outcome. Reopen only if the anchor solve cost is first engineered away.

title: Screen packed residual row ordering by projected weight
description:
The mixed WH2 packed-GF(2) residual currently projects and inserts every unused binary row in arena order (codec/WirehairV2Solve.cpp:3755-3824). Although row order cannot change rank, recovery, or the unique solution, online Gauss-Jordan insertion order can change the number and locality of full-payload pivot-RHS XORs. Add a test-only bounded experiment that orders rows by their initial packed projected popcount (with deterministic row-id tie breaking) before InsertPackedBinaryResidualRow.

Treat this strictly as a speed hypothesis. Do not claim recovery improvement, retune packet seeds, or change any named profile or wire bytes. Counter evidence comes before wall time: prior wirehair-ht0 reduced matrix fill by 80-98% without reducing row operations, so popcount/fill alone is not evidence. Keep memory and projection-pass overhead explicit; compare a two-pass/index-bucket implementation with bounded coefficient caching only if the first screen warrants it. Coordinate with active p6b1 so its shared solver edits are neither overwritten nor confounded.
acceptance_criteria: First establish exact same-row-set equivalence for result, recovered bytes, residual rank, quotient rank, and all non-order-dependent counters under the packed residual oracle and replayed hard failures. Run a counter-first paired screen on residual-heavy K values and reject unless residual BlockXors fall by at least 1 percent without a residual-time regression after including sort/projection overhead. Only a survivor advances to pinned counterbalanced full-payload bb=1280,4096,16384 timing; retain only a repeatable solve/residual/cycle win with bounded memory, no semantic or other-phase regression, native/portable/sanitizer gates, and repeated source review.
close_reason: Rejected: ascending projected weight worsened residual BlockXors by 0.724%; descending improved only 0.437%, below the 1% advance gate. Experiment fully removed and branch restored cleanly.

comments.text:
2026-07-16 dedicated K3 ideation completed and locally audited. Installed latest k3mcp called moonshotai/kimi-k3 with max reasoning and a 256k completion cap over 265,067 chars of numbered WH2 source/context. The first five provider attempts returned 429; retry 6 completed normally: finish=stop, truncated=false, prompt/completion/reasoning/total tokens=77,569/24,304/19,563/101,873 (reasoning is included in completion), cost $0.597267, latency 801.547s. Full response/metadata: /tmp/k3_wh2_ideation_result.json.

Local math/source audit rejects most of its eight proposals:

* E1/E2/E3/E4 overclaim recovery. Let A be the supplied binary system and C the mixed heavy map. q=dim ker(A) is invariant under peeling, inactivation, substitution, pivot selection, and row order; the quotient is C restricted to ker(A). Changing a nullspace basis replaces B by B*T for invertible T, so rank(C*B*T)=rank(C*B). Thus residue-diverse pivots and E3's proposed binary basis exchange cannot repair a singular quotient; E3 is mathematically impossible for a fixed equation set. E1 also duplicates the measured negative Markowitz/min-fill bead wirehair-n34.1 (K32k deferred 255 vs 213, traffic 641.88 vs 629.52 MB, throughput 201 vs 673 MB/s). E4 degree-2 substitution can alter work/order but not q or recovery and overlaps the extensive degree-2/Karp-Sipser/row-action screens (wirehair-2xu, wirehair-ln5.1, wirehair-n34.13).
* E6 mixed resume is not new: generic affine resume is completed in wirehair-i998, and field-agnostic/mixed deficient-tail resume is already explicitly deferred in wirehair-1t0m.11.
* E7 rank-greedy repair-ID scheduling is not a decoder optimization under random loss: the receiver cannot inspect/select undelivered payloads or future packet IDs. It would require encoder feedback/access and changes the delivery schedule; using the local E2E encoder loop would benchmark an oracle protocol rather than the codec on the same loss stream.
* E9's bidirectional staircase proof is false as stated. The proposed own+previous+next parity submatrix is tridiagonal with determinant recurrence D_n=D_(n-1)+D_(n-2) over GF(2), D_0=D_1=1, and is singular whenever n=2 mod 3 (including certified tiny S=2). It is not a safe encoder/profile candidate.

Two distinct, falsifiable follow-ups were created:

1. wirehair-wbtw.1 (E5), strictly a recovery-neutral speed screen: order unused projected binary rows by initial packed popcount before InsertPackedBinaryResidualRow (current loop WirehairV2Solve.cpp:3755-3824). Row rank/output stay exact, while Gauss-Jordan RHS block-XOR count may change. First run a matrix/counter-only hook on residual-heavy hard cells; reject unless deterministic BlockXors falls >=1% without residual-ns regression, then pair bb=1280/4096/16384. Prior wirehair-ht0 is a strong negative prior (80-98% less fill but -0.1% to +0.3% row-op change), so keep this bounded and do not infer a win from fill/popcount alone.
2. wirehair-wbtw.2, salvaging E2 as diagnostics only: on a failed q<=15 quotient, compute a nonzero invariant witness v in ker(A) intersect ker(C), map it back to original inactive columns, and log support/residue/block-schedule structure on replayable failure IDs. This can test whether current K/residue resonances share an exact cancellation mechanism and guide a genuinely equation-changing GF2/GF256 experiment. Do not implement K3's basis/pivot policy; basis choice cannot change failure.

No source edits were made in this lane. E8 was folded into E2 by K3 and adds no separate proposal.

acceptance_criteria: Each candidate is separately interleaved against the frozen accepted binary across K10k/32k/64k and short/MTU blocks; exact coefficient/RHS equality, stats, resume/OOM behavior, portable fallback, strict tests, and sanitizers pass; reject any candidate with a representative regression.
notes:
Candidate A implemented in WirehairV2Solve unused-row construction: reuse the existing packed accumulator, XOR direct inactive bits and complete peeled projection words, then expand only final set-bit parity once into zeroed GF(256) coefficients. No allocation/state/stats/wire change; focused native solver/oracle suite passes. CPU16 interleaved current-vs-candidate, 20 pairs: bb64 residual/total K10k -61.40%/-33.98%, K32k -63.16%/-38.79%, K64k -63.87%/-45.37%; bb1280 K10k -46.90%/-16.63%, K32k -49.77%/-20.87%, K64k -49.61%/-24.31%. Project phase stayed within -0.3% to +2.1%, confirming the gain is localized to residual-row coefficient construction. Pending exact stats/output equivalence, review, portable/sanitizer gates.
Candidate A exact-output validation passed against frozen ba313bf across K10k/32k/64k at bb64 and bb1280 after normalizing only phase times; all printed seeds, ranks, counters, results, and decode outcomes matched. Existing focused K320 case exercises R=66 final-word padding; tiny dense oracle, hashed family, quotient boundary, rank-deficient resume, mixed solve, and global verification pass. Independent review found no issue. Candidate B's per-solve 3.9 KiB table was rejected after 20-pair A/B because representative K32/K64 cells were noisy-to-negative. Revised B caches the immutable production H12 table once with allocation-free std::array and keeps a generic local table for experimental H. Twenty alternating CPU16 pairs vs accepted A: residual/total at bb64 K10k -11.79%/-3.57%, K32k -8.73%/-3.31%, K64k -7.11%/-3.40%; bb1280 K10k -6.31%/-1.98%, K32k -2.31%/-1.17%, K64k -3.44%/-1.48%. Exact non-time outputs match A in all six cells; focused native suite passes. Pending adversarial review, portable/sanitizer/full gates.
Review correction: the initially described generic local table was not retained. Adversarial review showed a full-period table would regress valid tiny non-H12 profiles (notably H=1) and add an OOM point. Final candidate caches only the immutable production PeriodicCauchy H12 table; every non-H12 periodic and hashed profile follows its exact baseline on-demand allocation/coefficient path. Added independent dense-oracle + Verify coverage for periodic and hashed H=0/1/12/128; Release, Debug, and native focused suites pass.
Cold-start safeguard: even H12 now uses the baseline on-demand path while L<244. The static table is first materialized only when a solve spans at least one complete coefficient period, where baseline projection+RHS would compute at least twice the table's 2,928 coefficients. This avoids trading the large-K win for tiny-message first-solve latency; K10k/32k/64k measurements are unchanged.
Final accepted implementation includes packed residual parity accumulation plus the production-only periodic H12 cache; all non-H12/hashed paths retain their exact baseline dispatch. Exact outputs/stats remained unchanged. Final native 39/39, portable 42/42, and Clang ASan+UBSan 37/37 passed after source freeze; repeated focused/full reviews found no issue.
close_reason: Implemented, exact-output benchmarked, independently reviewed, and passed native/portable/sanitizer gates.

title: Add optional decoder fast-recover cache for received systematic packets
description: Existing WH2 wire profiles map systematic IDs to mixed intermediate equations, so Recover evaluates roughly eight full-block inputs for every source block. Across the profiled matrix WH2 recovery is 3-5x slower than legacy. Most delivered packets under common loss are systematic and already reside in ReceivedBlockStorage before solve, but success discards that storage and later recomputes every source packet.
design: A practical first experiment can retain the already allocated cold receive slots/id index on successful cold solve when the option is enabled, avoiding another K*bb allocation. Recover copies systematic IDs <K from their slots and calls EvaluatePacketBlock only for holes. Resume adoption frees cold storage before success, so either compact systematic packets at checkpoint adoption or document a separate bounded cache. Keep this local policy outside serialized profile fields.
acceptance_criteria: Design an opt-in local decoder policy that retains or compacts accepted systematic payloads after solve, directly copies cached source IDs during Recover, and evaluates only missing source IDs. Measure loss=0/0.1/0.5 and burst schedules across K=1000/10000/64000, bb=1280/102400; report recovery speed, decode/peak/retained memory, cache hit rate and duplicate-consistency behavior. Preserve default memory behavior and wire profile; validate partial tail, repair-only, resume, OOM transactions and public API exposure plan.
notes: Implemented default-off internal decoder fast-Recover cache behind distinct runtime-only CacheReceivedSystematicPackets. It allocates an uninitialized message-sized byte range transactionally (avoiding create-time zero/page touch), records exact accepted systematic bytes plus K occupancy bytes only after packet commit in both cold and resume branches, and Recover directly copies hits while evaluating only holes. Separate idempotent direct/facade release clears cache and falls back to full equation evaluation; serialized profile/wire/public C ABI unchanged. Compare now supports --precode-encoder-cache, --precode-decoder-cache, or combined --precode-cache and reports both flags; README documents memory tradeoff. Exact native A/B used the same binary/profile/common trace, encoder-only cache vs both caches. Recover MB/s: K1000 bb1280 IID10% 9565->37160 (3.88x), bb102400 5190->17302 (3.33x); K10000 bb1280 loss0 4432->21473 (4.85x), IID10% 4551->13713 (3.01x), IID50% 4796->7331 (1.53x), burst10% 4523->15326 (3.39x), bb102400 IID10% 4617->17530 (3.80x); K64000 bb1280 IID10% 2035->9632 (4.73x), bb102400 4077->16646 (4.08x). Receive-copy tradeoff: decode usually -3% to -12%. Peak RSS deltas matched touched systematic pages: +1MiB K1000/bb1280, +89MiB K1000/bb102400, +11.9MiB K10000/bb1280, +885MiB K10000/bb102400, +78.6MiB K64000/bb1280, +5.51GiB K64000/bb102400. Default decoder allocates zero cache bytes. Tests cover default-off, init/reinit OOM transactionality, exact/conflicting duplicates, partial final bytes, cold loss+repair E2E, explicit systematic append after ResumeState activation, release before first Recover, release after Recover, idempotence, facade states and exact payload fallback. Validation: full Release 41/41; full ASan+UBSan 36/36; sanitizer decoder-only cache benchmark passed; package/ABI/build-policy included; diff-check passed. Raw paired data: /tmp/wh2-cache-isolated; earlier independent old/new confirmation: /tmp/wh2-cache-bench. Public exposure remains parked in updated wirehair-x8rs.14. Additional final coverage: cache-enabled repair-only decode reaches success with zero cache hits and exact fallback recovery; Release and ASan+UBSan focused tests pass after adding it. Common schedule hit fractions are 100% at loss0, approximately 90% at IID10%, approximately 50% at IID50%, and trace-dependent under burst, explaining the measured recovery scaling.
close_reason: Default-off decoder systematic cache implemented; 1.5-4.9x representative and 3.3-4.1x large-block Recover gains validated with explicit memory/decode tradeoffs and full Release/sanitizer gates.

title: Evaluate production top-K boundary inactivation heuristic
description: Production PeelBinaryRows uses degree-two count then static reference-count selection, while WirehairV2Peel contains a richer top-K boundary/lookahead heuristic. Prototype the latter against actual WH2 CSR rows to test whether lower R/tails outweigh selection CPU.
acceptance_criteria: Common packet traces compare R mean/p95/p99/max, solve phases, and full payload outcomes at representative K/block sizes; preserve row/wire contracts; promote only with measured overall win and park otherwise.
notes: Rejected after isolated exact-system experiment; no production Solve edit. A copied current PeelBinaryRows implementation was checked against SolvePrecodeSystem InactivatedColumns on common rows, then compared with the existing KsBmaxTop16 boundary/component/lookahead heuristic through EvaluatePeelingRows. Systems used selected certified PrecodeSystem rows plus identical packet-id rows; order alternated for timing. IID OH0 bb1: K64/100 trials R 38.46->37.25 but peel 2.00x; K1000/500 88.31->91.29, downstream work model 1.035x, peel 2.75x; K3200/300 119.39->131.18, work 1.101x, peel 2.64x; K10000/100 188.77->217.93, work 1.156x, peel 3.13x; K64000/20 599.2->706.75, work 1.180x, peel 7.28x. bb1280 IID likewise regressed: K1k R84.32->90.45/work1.076/time2.27x; K3.2k 125.4->136.96/work1.094/time2.60x; K10k 178.61->194.39/work1.089/time3.21x. Sequential, burst, repair-only, OH1, and bb102400 screens were overwhelmingly worse. One isolated K3200/bb1280 repair-only profile improved R126->122 but took 2.84x peel and did not reproduce at bb102400, where R129->155. K64/bb102400 IID improved R41.70->40.91/work0.978 at 1.89x peel, but K16 regressed and larger K/profile/schedules did not support a robust conditional. Candidate-limit grid 1/4/8/16/32/all produced identical decisions and regressions at K1k and K3.2k, so top-k tuning cannot rescue the component heuristic on these graphs. The richer heuristic was designed for source-only LT graphs; on full WH2 precode+packet graphs current exact dynamic degree-two/reference selection is both faster and produces materially smaller R/tails. Unique linear-system payload/rank is invariant to inactivation order; zero-RHS production solves confirmed common-system validity. Isolated source/binary remained under /tmp only. No production follow-up filed.
close_reason: Rejected: top-K boundary heuristic is 2-7x slower and raises R/work/tails on representative full WH2 graphs

Final bounded LT screen (500 trials/cell): /tmp/precode_sim_final --K 1000,10000 --oh 0,2,8,32,128 --schemes codecport_ic --trials 500 --threads 8 --paired --packet-schedule <iid|permutation|repair-only> --loss <0.1|0.3|0> --identity-systematic --rowdist <lt_m1_c64|lt_m2_c1024|rs_c001_d50_c128> --seed 20260712. Safety-cap confirmation: /tmp/precode_sim_final --K 10000,64000 --oh 0,8,128 --schemes codecport_ic --trials 100 --threads 32 --paired --packet-schedule iid --loss 0.3 --identity-systematic --rowdist fixed44 --max-inact 4096 --seed 20260712. close_reason: Rejected identity-systematic repair retune after common-trace simulator and actual-solver certification. Fixed44/48, mixtures, staged laws, ideal LT, broader LT, and robust soliton cannot simultaneously match generic recovery, peeling speed, and schedule consistency; K64 fixed44 runs away beyond the 4096 cap through OH128.

title: Drop solved WH2 encoder's redundant precode row graph
description: MessagePrecodeEncoder solves the full PrecodeSystem, then PrecodeEncoder::InitializeSolvedSystem copies the complete StaircaseRows and DenseRowColumns graph into SystemValue even though packet-contract EncodeResult/EvaluatePacketBlockForValidatedSystemWithRuntime reads only SystemValue.Params, PacketConfig, PacketRuntime and solved intermediate bytes. This adds nested-vector allocation/copy work and persistent memory to every public WH2 encoder.
design: Preferred minimal change: after full validation, store only Params in the UsesPacketContract branch; retain complete SystemValue for the older ComputeEncodedBlockImpl branch. Audit tests/callers of BlockEncoder().System(): current production packet evaluation and collision helpers appear to use Params only, but document the narrowed solved-System() representation or provide a separate Params accessor if completeness is part of the internal contract.
acceptance_criteria: Prove packet-contract runtime evaluation needs only validated PrecodeParams (or safely move ownership without duplicate rows), preserve the legacy/internal unsolved PrecodeEncoder path and System() inspection contract, add a structural/runtime oracle, and measure encoder-create time/allocation/RSS at K=1000/10000/64000. Release/sanitizer/package/ABI tests pass.
notes: Implemented solved packet-contract compaction in PrecodeEncoder::InitializeSolvedSystem: validate the complete incoming PrecodeSystem, retain only Params plus packet runtime/intermediate bytes, and remove the guarded nested graph copy. Added HasCompleteSystem() and documented System(): direct legacy InitializeResult retains a complete validated StaircaseRows/DenseRowColumns graph and returns true; MessagePrecodeEncoder solved mode exposes complete Params, empty row vectors, false. Structural tests cover uninitialized/direct/solved/failed-reinit states; existing reordered/max-id manual packet oracle proves solved runtime bytes unchanged. Adjusted OOM injection and V2TransactionalTest from five to the four real partial-message guarded failures after full Release caught the stale expectation; focused Release+ASan transactional now pass. Static-linked global-new/RSS A/B, pinned CPU6: retained row graph per encoder K1000=64 alloc/35,484 B; K10000=100 alloc/365,444 B; K64000=360 alloc/2,323,900 B, all reduced to zero. Aggregate bb1 held encoders: K1000x20 allocations 4620->3340, bytes 9,568,000->8,858,320, RSS delta 1,220,608->~647,168; K10000x8 2712->1912, 37,205,440->34,281,888, RSS 4,669,440->733,184; K64000x2 1990->1270, 66,240,272->61,592,472, RSS 12,767,232->10,416,128. bb1280 confirms capacity savings and RSS: K1000x8 graph281,376 B removed/RSS -110,592; K10000x3 graph1,096,188 B removed/RSS -2,117,632; K64000x1 graph2,323,884 B removed/RSS -385,024 (payload/solver dominates peak). Isolated copy stage median saved 0.870us K1k, 33.836us K10k, 277.139us K64k; whole-create timings were small/noisy under concurrent load, with identical profile digests. Release encode/decode/roundtrip/seed 4/4 and fresh ASan+UBSan 4/4 passed; git diff --check clean. Also coordinated runtime-only CacheReceivedSystematicPackets option for .13, excluded from selected wire validation.
close_reason: Removed redundant solved encoder graph with structural/runtime, allocation, RSS, create-time, Release, and sanitizer evidence
