title: Expose WH2 systematic cache controls in the public V2 API
description: Design and expose ABI-stable public V2 opt-ins for the MessagePrecodeEncoder runtime-only systematic source cache and MessagePrecodeDecoder received-systematic fast-Recover cache, plus idempotent detach operations. Existing public create signatures have no options/flags channel, so this needs a deliberately versioned options surface or new entry points rather than changing ABI or conflating local storage policy with the serialized wire profile.
acceptance_criteria: Public cached encoder/decoder create and detach are documented; old create remains default-off and ABI-compatible; both cache policies are absent from serialized profiles and wire output; symbol/package allowlists and C/C++ API tests cover old/new consumers; exact/partial bytes, repair equality, resume, detach idempotence, OOM transactionality, sanitizer, E2E, and throughput/RSS gates pass.
notes:
PARKED FOLLOW-UP: both internal default-off caches are implemented with separate local flags (CacheSystematicSource and CacheReceivedSystematicPackets), but clean public exposure requires versioned C options/create entry points, permanent symbols, documentation, and package consumers. Existing public ABI remains unchanged. Decoder cache trades about one message of touched RSS at common loss for 2-7x faster Recover and can be detached before Recover to restore the default path.
Parked after the completed WH2 pass; safe follow-up with no current correctness blocker.
close_reason: Public cache-control API design is outside the focused codec recovery/speed roadmap and is not required to ship the selected profile.

title: Cache WH2 packet-domain primes in runtime row state
description: GeneratePacketMatrixRow and EvaluatePacketBlock recompute NextPrime16(K/P) even though dimensions are immutable per codec. This was intentionally split from wirehair-x8rs.8 because a correct cache needs runtime-only state threaded through cold solve, resume, encode, recovery, and standalone diagnostic fallbacks without changing the serialized profile or trusting caller-populated prime values. Proposed design: add a validated PacketRowRuntime containing source/precode counts and their primes; construct it only after IsPacketRowDomainValid, keep PacketRowConfig wire-equation fields unchanged, add internal cached row/evaluator overloads, let generic tooling recompute, and copy/rebuild the runtime cache in resume state. Do not add cache fields to serialized WirehairV2Profile.
acceptance_criteria: All public and internal cached paths prove the cached counts match K/P before use; malformed/stale caches cannot change equations; tiny, prime, composite, largest-prime, and K=64000 packet goldens remain identical; packet evaluator and cold-solve benchmarks show a repeatable win or the change is rejected; sanitizer, scalar, MSVC, and full suites pass.
notes:
Implemented runtime-only PacketRowRuntime cache (private K/P/mix + validated NextPrime16 values), cached row/evaluator/solve overloads, generic wrappers, encoder/decoder hot paths, cold solve, and resume checkpoint propagation. Public profile/equation bytes unchanged. Added named kBinaryQuotientMinBlockBytes=2048 boundary and resume coverage; K64/bb2048 independent dense-oracle success plus conflicting duplicate RHS Error/no-write; tiny hashed-family dense oracle. Runtime tests cover tiny, prime/composite, largest precode prime, K=64000, stale/malformed no-write, and row/evaluator/solve parity.

Validation: Release focused solve PASS. Fresh ASan+UBSan full ctest 36/36 PASS (including OOM, fuzz, transactional, policy, package/build-policy). Fresh scalar cross builds and qemu execution PASS for i686 and RISC-V: solve, policy, encode/OOM, decode/resume. git diff --check PASS. Native MSVC unavailable on this Linux host; code retains C++11/MSVC-compatible constructs and root will run integrated hosted/strict matrix.

Pinned taskset benchmark repeated. Cold-solve row-build stage K=10000/P=211: cache improvement 58.326% and 58.364%. Hot evaluator: bb1 31-33%, bb1280 2.2-6.7%; 100KiB approximately neutral to 1.3%; 1MiB neutral/noise as expected when bandwidth-bound. Immediate old/new precodefail cold E2E also preserved identical rank/failure results.
close_reason: Validated runtime packet-prime cache integrated across cold/resume/hot WH2 paths with unchanged equations and repeatable speedups.

title: Use common loss traces for legacy and WH2 comparison
description: The compare benchmark seeds legacy and WH2-precode loss RNGs differently, preventing common-random-number paired overhead analysis. Generate and reuse identical delivered-ID/loss schedules where codec domains permit, and add burst/permutation/adversarial patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy and WH2 arms consume demonstrably identical loss traces for paired modes; output reports paired overhead deltas and remains reproducible across thread counts. Existing benchmark modes/tests continue to pass.
notes: Implemented common random-number loss traces across baseline, V2-compatible, and WH2-precode compare arms. All arms now derive one monotonic packet-id loss stream from seed ^ 0x10fade; the compare header publishes loss_trace=common-id-v1. This removes the prior WH2-only 0x7632707265636f64 salt and makes overhead deltas paired by packet id. Extended burst/permutation/adversarial schedules are separately parked as wirehair-x8rs.13. Validation: wirehair_v2_bench rebuilt and wirehair_v2_bench_cli_test passed.
close_reason: All compare arms now replay the same packet-id loss decisions; CLI identifies the common trace. Non-IID schedules split to x8rs.13.

title: Remove WH2 decoder duplicate scans and redundant receive zeroing
description: Duplicate packets require an O(K) scan to find stored payload and unique full packets resize with zero-fill immediately before memcpy. Replace with bounded ID-to-slot lookup and avoid redundant full-slot initialization while retaining partial-tail zeroing and transactional memory policy.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate/conflict, allocation failure, partial packet, resume, and memory-policy contracts remain exact. Receive throughput and duplicate handling improve without peak-memory regression; sanitizer/fuzz/full E2E tests pass.
notes: Implemented bounded packet-id to cold-slot lookup with unordered_map, replacing duplicate O(K) payload scans while retaining the received ID set after checkpoint adoption. Cold unique packets append their valid bytes directly and zero only a partial tail; resume pending slots similarly skip full-slot zeroing. Rollback erases the slot mapping and shrinks payload storage on append/id allocation failure. Added cold late-slot tests for identical/conflicting UINT32_MAX recovery and partial-final systematic duplicates with count invariance. A/B pinned benchmarks: K=64000,bb=1 unique 1.109ms -> 0.909ms; 10k last-slot duplicates 137.670ms -> 0.039ms (~3568x), peak RSS unchanged 29,696 KiB. K=10000,bb=1280 unique 2.210ms -> 1.552ms (29.8% faster); 1k last duplicates 2.346ms -> 0.017ms (~139x). Release decoder/roundtrip/transactional + 10k stateful fuzz passed; ASan+UBSan same gates passed; full Release suite 40 non-build-policy tests plus separately rerun build_policy passed; large 64k systematic and recovery-only decoder cases passed. Repeated code-reading passes verified cold/resume duplicate conflict, partial zeroing, OOM rollback, successful checkpoint adoption, and unchanged 25% capacity accounting.
close_reason: Replaced linear duplicate scans and redundant full-slot zeroing with validated slot indexing/direct append; E2E, sanitizer, large-case, memory, and A/B performance gates pass.

title: Pool WH2 solve equations and transpose adjacency in CSR
description: Cold solve copies rows into per-equation vectors and builds vector-of-vector column adjacency, causing O(K) allocations and pointer chasing. Replace these with deterministic pooled/CSR column storage and a count-prefix-fill transpose while preserving peel order.
acceptance_criteria: Allocation count and peak bytes fall, deterministic peel decisions/output remain identical, and create/decode benchmarks improve at representative K. OOM no-write, fuzz, sanitizer, portability, and full recovery tests pass.
notes:
Implemented deterministic BinaryEquationArena with pooled row offsets/columns/Data pointers and CSR count-prefix-fill transpose. Reused existing degree_two_refs as the CSR fill cursor, leaving five backing allocations total (3 row + 2 adjacency). Row/reference order, duplicate references, per-column row order, queue tie-breaking, peel decisions, stats, RHS Data pointers, quotient/heavy algebra, and public packet equations are preserved. Added runtime storage counters and regression checks against the old vector-object lower bound.

Allocation/peak at K=64/1000/10000: old allocation lower bounds 204/2138/20210 -> exactly 5; pooled bytes 13,240/158,376/1,670,632 vs old peak lower bounds 16,456/192,536/1,993,944 (-19.5%/-17.7%/-16.2%).

Pinned saved-binary vs pooled direct cold-solve benchmark, 300 trials and identical algebra/failure histograms: bb1 K64 0.067->0.053 ms (-20.9%), K1000 0.753->0.668 (-11.3%), K10000 9.948->8.573 (-13.8%); bb1280 K64 0.065->0.052 (-20.0%), K1000 0.736->0.624 (-15.2%), K10000 9.994->8.595 (-14.0%). One-overhead cases improved 12-20% as well. End-to-end compare remained exact; normalized precode create/decode improved at K64/1k/10k (host frequency moved substantially during K10k, while matched v2 ratio improved ~18%).

Focused validation: Release solver/oracle/resume/storage PASS; K64 quotient dense oracle + conflicting RHS no-write PASS; ASan+UBSan focused solver PASS; ASan profile/stateful fuzz 2/2 PASS; fresh i686 and RISC-V cross builds plus qemu solver/oracle/storage PASS; git diff --check PASS. Repeated code-reading passes found no row-order, overflow, OOM, or lifetime defects. Root will run final integrated full suite. No staging/commit.
close_reason: Validated pooled row arena and CSR transpose reduce allocations, peak storage, and cold solve latency while preserving exact algebra.

title: Cache WH2 packet primes and optimize residual bit scans
description: Packet generation/evaluation recomputes NextPrime16(K/P) for invariant domains, and residual projection uses a manual trailing-zero shift loop. Cache validated primes in runtime state where practical and use the project portable ctz/BitScan primitive without changing equation generation.
acceptance_criteria: Golden packet equations remain identical across tiny/boundary/maximum domains and scalar/portable builds. Packet encode/decode and residual projection benchmarks show no regression and preferably a repeatable win; full tests and sanitizers pass.
notes:
Implemented the residual bit-scan half in the shared tree without staging/commit. Added wirehair::NonzeroLowestBitIndex64 to WirehairTools.h: GCC/Clang use __builtin_ctzll on 64-bit and split 32-bit __builtin_ctz operations on ILP32 (avoids a __ctzdi2 helper call); MSVC x64/ARM64 use _BitScanForward64 and 32-bit MSVC splits two _BitScanForward calls. The nonzero precondition is asserted in debug. Removed the manual shift loop from WirehairV2Solve.cpp and converted all four projection/resume call sites. Focused coverage exhausts singleton bits 0..63 and mixed words whose lowest set bit is 0,31,32,62. Existing tiny/boundary/K=64000 packet equation goldens and both heavy-family solve paths remain exact. Native object inspection shows direct tzcnt instructions at all four sites; rebuilt i686 object has no __ctzdi2 dependency.

Benchmark evidence on pinned CPU0, current shared Release tree: precodefail 300 trials, bb=1, OH0 reports solve_ms_mu 0.766 at K=1000 and 10.527 at K=10000; resume benchmark passes at 64.442ms initial/20.840ms 8-row resume for K=1000 and 377.029ms/288.715ms for K=10000. An earlier 3.193/63.968 precodefail and 123.881/1482.184 resume sample cannot be attributed solely to this bead because the recovery agent concurrently landed heavy-family/binary-quotient solver work; no isolated speed claim is made. The intrinsic implementation is nevertheless structurally constant-time, native disassembly is pinned, and current benchmarks show no regression.

Validation: focused Release and explicit ASan+UBSan solver tests pass; strict Release functional tests 40/40 pass. The separate build_policy_e2e gate twice lost its scratch directories to concurrent shared-runner deletion; root will rerun it after agents are idle. Fresh RISC-V scalar QEMU golden 1/1 and i686 scalar QEMU golden+allocation 2/2 passed; the post-ILP32-optimization i686 rebuild/golden passed and has no libgcc ctz helper. git diff --check clean.

Prime caching was deliberately not mixed into this solver edit: correct caching requires validated runtime state threaded through cold solve, resume, encode, recover, and standalone fallbacks. Adding fields directly to PacketRowConfig would risk stale/malformed values changing equations. The runtime-only PacketRowRuntime design and full remaining acceptance are parked as wirehair-x8rs.12; no profile/wire bytes changed here.
close_reason: Replaced manual residual scans with portable constant-time compiler/MSVC primitives, added complete bit-boundary coverage, and parked validated runtime prime caching as wirehair-x8rs.12.

title: Remove WH2 encoder initialization's full temporary message copy
description: MessagePrecodeEncoder currently copies the full padded source before its synchronous joint solve, then discards it. Borrow caller-owned full blocks during Initialize and allocate only padded-tail storage while preserving the documented post-return ownership contract and transactional OOM behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Peak initialization memory falls by approximately one message for representative N/block sizes; initialized encoder remains independent of caller memory after return; exact and partial final blocks, zeroing, OOM fault injection, sanitizer, full tests, and create benchmarks pass without output changes.
notes: Implemented encoder-only borrowing in MessagePrecodeEncoder::InitializeResult: complete caller blocks are borrowed solely across synchronous SolvePrecodeSystem calls; a partial final block allocates one zero-filled block and copies only valid tail bytes. The completed encoder still owns the solved intermediate vector and is independent of input after return. Added exact/partial caller-buffer release tests, tail-zero oracle, and partial-tail injected-OOM transactional preservation. Release gates: precode encode (2000 feasibility trials), roundtrip, decode passed; focused CTest 7/7 including constrained 64 MiB OOM; ASan+UBSan encode (200 trials), roundtrip, decode passed. Dedicated encoder-only before/after RSS at K=10000,bb=1280: 44,032 -> 31,744 KiB (12,288 KiB saved for 12.2 MiB message), elapsed 0.19 -> 0.17 s. K=1000,bb=102400: 320,512 -> 222,208 KiB (98,304 KiB saved for 97.7 MiB message), elapsed 0.50 -> 0.42 s. Repeated code-reading passes found no remaining issue.
close_reason: Removed full temporary source copy with exact/partial lifetime, OOM, sanitizer, E2E, and measured RSS/create validation.

title: Continuously test ARM64, 32-bit, and big-endian codec paths
description:
## Problem

Per-change CI covers only Ubuntu x86-64 and Windows x64, and scheduled emulation is x86-64. Distinct ARM/NEON, 32-bit address arithmetic, endian-sensitive code, Mach-O exports, and unlisted scalar architectures can regress without executing.

## Evidence

.github/workflows/ci.yml:23-59 contains only x64 matrix cells. gf256.h:56-109 and gf256.cpp:86-121/309-320 have architecture-specific code, while the audit found concrete big-endian and 32-bit defects. gf256.h otherwise falls through to x86/SSE includes, so a scalar RISC-V or WebAssembly target is also an important compile boundary.

## Scope

Add a cost-bounded portability matrix using native runners where available and cross-build/QEMU where necessary. Exercise runtime code where emulation permits it, not compile-only checks alone.
acceptance_criteria: ARM64 runs strict build, relevant CTest, GF256 SIMD self-test, and installed consumer. An i686 lane runs allocation/boundary and round-trip tests. A big-endian s390x or ppc64 lane executes the heavy-window oracle and golden round trips. A macOS ARM64 lane checks the Mach-O ABI allowlist and package consumer. At least one explicitly scalar non-x86 target such as riscv64 or wasm32 compiles, and runs a smoke round trip where tooling permits. Pin toolchains/emulators, surface architecture diagnostics, and document per-change versus scheduled budgets.
notes:
Implemented cost-bounded portability matrix without closing for hosted follow-up.

Files: gf256.h; CMakeLists.txt; test/PortabilityRoundTripTest.cpp; ci/run_portability.py; ci/test_run_portability.py; ci/run_ci.py; ci/README.md; .github/workflows/ci.yml; .github/workflows/scheduled.yml.

Implementation: GF256 now selects x86 SIMD only when SSE2 is actually available, keeps Android/iOS behavior, uses scalar fallback for baseline i686 and unlisted RISC targets, and only enables Linux ARM auxv headers under __linux__. New golden CTest prints architecture/pointer/endian/backend diagnostics, pins repair bytes, and recovers after loss. The portability runner pins GCC 13.3 and QEMU 8.2 families, asserts ELF class/data/machine, validates compile backend macros, runs QEMU via explicit sysroots, and can run ARM installed C/C++/plugin consumers. Per-change CI adds native ubuntu-24.04-arm NEON/package and i686 allocation/golden lanes (25+20 minute caps). Weekly/manual adds one 30-minute s390x+riscv64 cross job and one 30-minute macos-15 ARM job pinned to Xcode 16.4 build 16F6. CMake derives Darwin's underscore-prefixed exported-symbol list from abi/wirehair.map; the mac lane requires arm64-only dylib exports to exactly match the manifest and runs installed package consumers. ci/README.md documents the 45 per-change and 60 scheduled runner-minute budgets and reproduction commands.

Local E2E evidence on 2026-07-10: four final run_portability invocations all exit 0. aarch64 ELF64 little-endian reported NEON, GF256 differential passed, golden passed, and installed C/C++/plugin package tests were 3/3. i686 ELF32 reported scalar, allocation overflow/boundary and golden tests were 2/2. s390x ELF64 big-endian reported scalar, exhaustive/property heavy-window oracle and golden were 2/2. riscv64 ELF64 little-endian reported scalar and golden smoke passed. Baseline i686 initially failed SSE2 intrinsics and riscv64 initially failed on emmintrin.h; both failures were reproduced before the fix. A separate i686 -msse2 build retained the optimized x86 path and passed GF256 differential+golden 2/2. Native strict shared x86 passed GF256, golden, and positive/negative ELF export gates 4/4. GCC ASan+UBSan passed GF256+golden 2/2. A CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Darwin configure generated exactly 18 manifest symbols and the expected -exported_symbols_list linker flag. A non-Linux AArch64 preprocess probe enabled NEON but not LINUX_ARM. Python runner suites passed 35 tests; both workflow files parse as YAML; git diff --check clean. Full repeated source pass after preserving Android/iOS behavior found no further defects.

Remaining validation: the native macOS ARM64 job and its real nm/lipo result require hosted macos-15 execution after the parent integrates/pushes. Leave IN_PROGRESS until that hosted evidence is available, per orchestrator instruction.
Final pre-push integration rerun on current combined source: pinned GCC 13.3/QEMU 8.2 i686 strict cross build compiled the complete public library (including serialized V2 profile implementation), verified ELF32 little-endian/i386 scalar diagnostics, and passed allocation-overflow plus golden round-trip 2/2. In parallel, pinned s390x strict cross build verified ELF64 big-endian/S390 scalar diagnostics and passed exhaustive heavy-window plus golden round-trip 2/2. Current actionlint 1.7.12, 69 runner/binding tests, repository data-integrity lane, py_compile, and diff-check pass. Still IN_PROGRESS solely for real hosted native ARM64/macOS/Mach-O evidence after push.
Settled parent gates additionally passed strict Release 41/41 and fresh Clang ASan+UBSan 32/32 after final V2 public/profile and incremental fixes; exact public export count is now 30 and package C++/wire-doc gates pass. Independent integration review found no portability/build blocker. Keep IN_PROGRESS only for hosted ARM64/macOS/Mach-O run evidence.
Hosted closure evidence: main run 29122858609 passed Linux ARM64/NEON/installed-consumer job 86461744913 and Linux i686 allocation-boundary/golden-round-trip job 86461744919. Scheduled run 29122949984 passed macOS ARM64/Mach-O ABI/package job 86462028249 (exact 30-symbol allowlist plus package 3/3) and s390x big-endian/RISC-V scalar QEMU job 86462028288 (big-endian heavy-window/golden 2/2 plus scalar RISC-V golden smoke). Run URLs: https://github.com/catid/wirehair/actions/runs/29122858609 and https://github.com/catid/wirehair/actions/runs/29122949984. All native and cross-architecture acceptance conditions are satisfied.
close_reason: Implemented and locally/hosted validated across ARM64 NEON, i686, s390x big-endian, macOS ARM64/Mach-O, and scalar RISC-V, including installed consumers and exact ABI gates.

title: Eliminate redundant work from the hosted CI matrix
description:
## Problem

Each of six compiler/linkage cells repeats pure Python tests and the full CTest graph, including nested package producer builds. Unix cells also repeat the multi-build policy suite, spending substantial hosted time without adding independent coverage.

## Evidence

.github/workflows/ci.yml:23-59 defines six cells. ci/run_ci.py:558-573 calls python_unit_tests and full ctest in every cell. CMakeLists.txt:475-534 registers nested static/shared package and build-policy E2Es inside those runs.

## Scope

Split compiler/linkage-sensitive tests from pure validation and packaging/policy gates using CTest labels or dedicated jobs. Preserve meaningful ABI, compiler, sanitizer, and consumer coverage while avoiding duplicate push/pull-request runs.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a coverage map showing which job owns each gate. Python/validator, nested package producer, and build-policy suites run only in the minimum representative jobs; compiler/linkage-specific unit and installed-consumer coverage remains. Push and pull_request triggers do not run duplicate full workflows for the same commit where avoidable. Compare before/after hosted job-minutes and critical-path time, with all failure diagnostics retained.
notes:
Implemented CI ownership split. CMakeLists.txt labels only package_static/shared/both_e2e and build_policy_e2e as ci-once. ci/run_ci.py adds --repository-gates and --tool-smoke, exact JSON CTest-inventory validation, CTest parallelism, non-owner/sanitizer ci-once exclusion, Python-only owner semantics, and one MSVC tool owner. .github/workflows/ci.yml assigns repository gates to Linux GCC static, tool smoke to MSVC static, preserves every compiler/linkage build/install/external-consumer and every shared native-Python gate, restricts push to master/v* while retaining pull_request/manual, and expands failure artifact globs for nested configure/test logs. ci/README.md publishes a gate-by-gate coverage map, trigger contract, public hosted baseline (run 29113415903: 18.67 summed job-min, 12.28 matrix, 2:50 matrix critical, 5:33 baseline-set critical), local before/after measurements (serial full 70.26s, parallel owner 46.50s, lean non-owner 31.93s), and scoped planning estimate pending authoritative post-push hosted data. ci/test_run_ci.py has ownership/parser/orchestration/sanitizer/inventory/workflow/diagnostic tests. Validation: 28/28 runner tests pass; combined Python owner suite 36 CI/portability + 23 binding tests passes; 128 concurrent runner suites = 3584 tests pass; actionlint v1.7.12 checksum-verified and both workflows clean; PyYAML parse, py_compile, and git diff --check clean; actual configured inventory finds exactly 4 ci-once gates; all 4 nested gates pass; lean CTest selection excludes exactly those and currently passes 30/31, with sole failure wirehair_v2_policy_test duplicate-original terminal-state assertions from active root/V2 edits (reported). Strict GCC build succeeded after active V2 target wiring landed. Leave IN_PROGRESS until the combined push supplies authoritative post-change hosted job-minutes/critical-path measurement, then update docs/notes and close. No commit/push performed.
Checkpoint after latest shared-tree integration: strict GCC/Ninja build succeeds with current portability and V2 fuzz/oracle additions. Fresh owner-style full selection excluding only the known active wirehair_v2_policy_test blocker passes 34/34, including all four ci-once package/build-policy gates, new duplicate-packet coverage, both fuzz harnesses, and all install/package tests (37.40s at -j2). Lean non-owner selection chooses 31 tests and passes 30/31; sole remaining blocker is wirehair_v2_policy_test with five duplicate-original terminal-state expectations. Exact rzmb files/hunks remain .github/workflows/ci.yml (trigger, matrix owner args, diagnostics), CMakeLists.txt (ci-once labels), ci/run_ci.py (selection/inventory/parallelism), ci/test_run_ci.py, and ci/README.md. Bead remains IN_PROGRESS awaiting that unrelated V2-policy fix plus post-push hosted timing.
3cga integration update: repository-gate ownership moved from Linux GCC static to Linux GCC shared because the standard Python distribution E2E requires an installed DSO; the owner remains unique and all static/shared compiler coverage remains. ci.test_run_ci now rejects --repository-gates on static cells and validates the distribution command/log path. Current combined Python runner/portability/binding suite is 66/66 and actionlint/diff checks pass. This does not satisfy rzmb's remaining post-push hosted timing requirement; leave IN_PROGRESS.
Final current-tree selection rerun after V2 policy/detach integration: strict Release build succeeded; owner/full CTest selection passed 37/37 in 50.24s at -j8, including the exact four ci-once package/build-policy gates; lean non-owner  selection passed 33/33 in 18.19s. The previous wirehair_v2_policy_test blocker is cleared. Local selection has no remaining failure; bead stays IN_PROGRESS solely for the required first post-push hosted job-minute/critical-path comparison and documentation update.
Correction to preceding checkpoint: the lean command used CTest label exclusion -LE ci-once and excluded exactly the four owned gates.
Final settled pre-push evidence after all cross-bead fixes: complete strict Release 41/41 (including package static/shared/both and build-policy), fresh Clang ASan+UBSan non-ci-once 32/32, Python/runner 69/69, reproducible wheel/sdist full E2E, actionlint 1.7.12, py_compile, and diff-check all pass. Exact ci-once ownership remains three package variants plus build-policy; C++11 consumer propagation and installed wire-doc checks remain owner-only. Independent integration review clean. Keep IN_PROGRESS only for post-push hosted timing/ownership evidence.
Authoritative hosted after measurement is all-green run 29128713010 at 06d80d1. Public job timestamps: the same six compiler/linkage matrix cells fell from 12.28 to 11.47 summed minutes (6.6%); matrix critical path was 2:52 versus 2:50. The same nine-job baseline set was 20.47 summed minutes and 5:35 sanitizer-owned critical versus 18.67/5:33, reflecting the intervening expansion from 32 to 41 registered tests and longer TSan/package/ABI gates rather than a fixed workload. Added integrity/ARM64/i686 jobs contributed 1.77 minutes, making the full 12-job sum 22.23 without extending the 5:35 wall time. ci/README.md now publishes these observed values and replaces the linear estimate. Unique ci-once owner selection and exact inventory passed; failed precursor runs 29123055555 and 29128445380 preserved actionable logs/artifacts that led directly to the Windows fixes. Final local full CTest 41/41, Python 69/69, actionlint/py_compile/diff checks, and all hosted jobs pass.
close_reason: CI gate ownership is deduplicated and documented, trigger duplication removed, diagnostics retained, and authoritative all-green hosted before/after job-minute and critical-path measurements are published.

title: Ship the Python binding as a standard installable package
description:
## Motivation

The binding is installed as a standalone, misspelled module under a CMake prefix and must be located manually. It has no Python project metadata, wheel/sdist, import-version policy, or explicit native-library bundling/discovery contract.

## Evidence

There is no pyproject.toml or wheel metadata. CMakeLists.txt installs python/whirehair.py into a prefix-specific python directory, while ci/run_ci.py and ci/python_native_test.py manually locate and inject that module and DSO.

## Scope

Provide a normal Python distribution while preserving compatibility for existing whirehair imports. Decide whether wheels bundle the native DSO, depend on a system install, or provide platform-specific artifacts, and make that policy explicit.
acceptance_criteria: A PEP 517 build produces reproducible sdist and supported-platform wheels with package/version/license metadata. Installation into a clean virtual environment supports the documented import name, finds exactly the intended native library, and passes native loss/reorder/recover/conversion tests. Test uninstall, isolated/no-library errors, editable/source installs, static-only CMake policy, and Linux/Windows/macOS discovery without relying on the source tree.
notes:
Completed standard Python packaging. Added wirehair-fec 2.0.0 with pinned Hatchling PEP 517 metadata, canonical import wirehair, compatible import whirehair, SPDX/license/Python metadata, pure py3-none-any system-DSO policy, and documented deterministic discovery. WIREHAIR_LIBRARY and WIREHAIR_PREFIX are authoritative; installed-prefix, OS loader, Linux, Windows, and macOS candidates are covered. Prefix discovery is lazy so a direct hit avoids a recursive tree walk. Shared and dual CMake packages install both import names; static-only installs contain no Python. The Linux GCC shared matrix cell uniquely owns the distribution gate, while every main shared cell now checks automatic installed-library discovery before its explicit full native round trip.

The E2E builds the real checkout and a detached normalized source tree with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and requires byte-identical wheel and sdist output plus exact member allowlists. A synthetic native sentinel proves wheel-wide native exclusions. It verifies metadata and license bytes, no bundled DSO, clean wheel and isolated-sdist installs, canonical and compatibility identity, exact explicit-path and prefix-selected libraries, native loss/reorder/recover/block/conversion/detach behavior, authoritative missing-library errors, uninstall absence, direct source import, and isolated editable install/uninstall. Work-directory containment prevents the harness from deleting its source or native inputs.

Authorized Claude Fable max-plan adversarial review completed read-only. Accepted findings: global wheel native exclusions, exact artifact inventories and detached sentinel, minimum-version execution, lazy discovery, authoritative-prefix failure coverage, cleared discovery environment, required Python in shared package gates, and real automatic discovery in main shared CI cells. Findings about subset validation and WIREHAIR_PREFIX leakage described an earlier snapshot and were already fixed. The suggestion to disable build isolation was rejected because isolated PEP 517 builds are an acceptance requirement; network use and pinned direct frontend/backend versions are intentional. Windows receives real installed auto-discovery in its shared cell; macOS names/prefix behavior is unit-tested and the portable CMake package E2E performs env-free installed discovery when run there.

Final validation on the stable tree: Python 3.12 package E2E passed with byte-identical wheel SHA256 92d1446fdbda764a6ab67315a4cea3f5f5aeb3fa03ccbec5250630884e2d41e5 and sdist SHA256 4952d4b60a6a3032126e2382230c677b3f1612724f3503a9662cf95a40713b2b; full package E2E also passed under the declared minimum Python 3.8.20, including Metadata 2.4 handling. Current Python 3.8 native E2E passes. CMake package_static_e2e, package_shared_e2e, and package_both_e2e passed 3/3 in 4.00s. Combined binding/runner/portability suite passed 68/68; py_compile, actionlint, and git diff --check passed. Current full owner CTest selection passed 37/37 and lean selection passed 33/33. During integration the gates caught and root fixed static libm propagation, a ctypes retained-export graph, and a test dimension mismatch; all reruns are green. No commit or push performed, per parent instruction.
Post-closure integration hardening: Python docs now require the same-release native library and explain that major API 2 alone does not guarantee newer symbols; python/benchmark_buffers.py is included in the exact reproducible sdist and detached-source fixture because the shipped README advertises it. Fresh isolated real-vs-detached wheel/sdist E2E is byte-identical and all wheel/sdist/editable/native/uninstall checks pass (wheel fe8d7f97..., sdist 051dc4fe...).
close_reason: Implemented and validated reproducible standard Python packaging, native discovery, install modes, and CI ownership end to end.

title: Add allocation-free Python encode and recovery buffer APIs
description:
## Motivation

The Python wrapper allocates a ctypes output buffer and copies it into a new bytes object for every encode, full recovery, and block recovery. High-rate packet loops cannot reuse application buffers.

## Evidence

python/whirehair.py:351-359 allocates/copies encode output, and 392-413 do the same for recovery. The wrapper already validates bytes-like inputs but exposes no writable-buffer output methods.

## Scope

Add encode_into, recover_into, and recover_block_into using writable contiguous Python buffers. Keep current allocation-returning methods as convenience wrappers over the same validation contract.
acceptance_criteria: Support bytearray and writable contiguous memoryview with explicit count semantics: encode_into and recover_block_into return the exact packet/block bytes written; recover_into requires at least message_bytes capacity, writes exactly message_bytes, returns that count, and preserves any larger-buffer tail. A final systematic packet requires only its exact partial length. Reject readonly, noncontiguous, released, undersized, and overflowing buffers without native writes. Cover closed objects, conversion, and buffer lifetime against fake and installed native libraries; benchmark allocations/throughput and document thread/GIL behavior.
notes: Implemented and source-reviewed allocation-free reusable-output APIs in python/whirehair.py: encode_into, recover_into, recover_block_into share a strict writable C-contiguous buffer validator, precompute exact required lengths, reject readonly/noncontiguous/released/undersized/uint-capacity-overflow buffers before native calls, preserve tails, support exact partial-final systematic/block storage, validate native returned counts, and pin/release storage across success and exception paths. Existing bytes-returning methods now delegate to the same contract. Expanded ci/python_native_test.py with installed-library E2E, converted encoder coverage, closed/rejected buffers, exact counts/tails, post-call resize, and 16 independent codec jobs through 8 threads; documented ctypes CDLL GIL release and required caller synchronization in README.md. Added python/benchmark_buffers.py. Repeated full source pass and git diff --check clean. Files: README.md, python/whirehair.py, python/test_whirehair.py, ci/python_native_test.py, new python/benchmark_buffers.py. Left IN_PROGRESS and uncommitted per orchestrator.

title: Allow legacy encoders to detach source storage after recovery blocks are materialized
description:
## Motivation

A legacy encoder keeps borrowed or owned source-message storage for its full lifetime primarily to accelerate systematic block copies, even after EncodeFeed has solved and materialized the recovery set. Applications cannot release a large source buffer while retaining a usable encoder.

## Evidence

WirehairCodec.cpp:4918-4923 generates recovery blocks after solving. WirehairCodec.cpp:4998-5013 still reads _input_blocks for original IDs when the fast systematic path is active, while a decoder-converted encoder already proves originals can be regenerated from the recovery set at a documented speed cost.

## Scope

Expose a detach/compact operation that severs the source-buffer lifetime after successful feed and switches systematic IDs to regeneration. Borrowed buffers remain immutable until detach. Define behavior for borrowed/copy_input modes, failed/incomplete encoders, reuse, conversion, and concurrency.
acceptance_criteria: After detach, callers may free or mutate the original message and every systematic/repair packet remains byte-identical to the legal pre-detach encoder. The codec releases owned full-message or converted-decoder staging storage and never dereferences borrowed storage. Tests cover partial final blocks, repeated detach, failure states, reuse/conversion, C/C++/Python bindings, and ASan lifetime poisoning. Detach is explicitly not concurrent with encode/reuse unless a synchronization contract is added. Document and benchmark the systematic speed/memory tradeoff.
notes:
Checkpoint 2026-07-10: root claimed after legacy duplicate implementation reached clean Release/ASan/Valgrind/cross-architecture gates. Beginning private core state/lifetime implementation and LegacyCore tests first. Public include/wirehair header, ABI manifest, Python binding, and package tests are deliberately deferred until the active wirehair-3ufc and wirehair-3cga workers finish their overlapping additive edits. Keep IN_PROGRESS.
Design selected for ysv1 private core: add an explicit recovery-materialized state set only after GenerateRecoveryBlocks; detach is valid only for Encoder/Converted with materialized recovery, idempotently sets the systematic fast-path flag to regeneration, frees owned/decoder-staging input, and nulls borrowed input without freeing it. This distinguishes internal initialized-but-unfed encoders and failed/incomplete decoders. Planned tests: borrowed ASan lifetime poisoning/mutation after detach; owned allocation release; byte-exact all systematic + repair packets including partial final; repeated detach; converted decoder staging release; invalid lifecycle; codec reuse; C/C++/Python/package surfaces; systematic speed and retained-memory measurement. Detach is explicitly externally synchronized with encode/reuse.
Core implementation checkpoint: added materialized-recovery state, idempotent Codec::DetachInput, unconditional borrowed-pointer nulling in FreeInput, owned/staging release, and systematic regeneration fallback. LegacyCore coverage now verifies all 65 systematic IDs plus repair IDs and UINT32_MAX byte-for-byte across detach, partial final blocks, borrowed source destruction (ASan-visible), owned allocation release, invalid unmaterialized/active/completed-decoder modes, decoder conversion/staging release, repeat detach, and codec reuse. Release full core and dedicated --detach pass. Representative benchmark at N=1024/block=1200 over two systematic passes: attached 28-35 us, detached 310-355 us, releasing 1,228,800 bytes (~10-11x slower systematic generation for one message-sized allocation released). Public/integration checkpoint: exposed wirehair_encoder_detach_input through the installed C header, implementation, WIREHAIR_2.0 ABI allowlist, installed C/package consumers, Python Encoder.detach_input, native Python E2E, and user docs. Public core tests now exercise null, borrowed, owned, decoder, converted, repeat, and reused handles through the exported wrapper. Release dedicated detach, C/C++ static/shared consumers, and exact ELF positive/negative ABI gates passed. Installed static package E2E passed; initial shared/both runs found a real Python lifetime defect: ctypes.cast(buffer,c_void_p) retained the bytearray export in a GC cycle after native detach. Replaced create/decode arguments with value-only c_void_p(addressof(buffer)), factored synchronous borrowed-view release for both detach_input and explicit close, and added resize-before/after native tests. Also corrected the new native E2E to retain the original decoder dimension after deliberately resizing the released source. Current 28 Python unit tests, direct native Python loss/reorder/conversion/detach/close E2E, and diff-check pass. Fresh package artifact rerun is delegated and pending before closure.
Post-public lifetime gates: fresh Clang 18 ASan+UBSan RelWithDebInfo build passed dedicated detach plus C/C++ consumers and full legacy_core (13.15s) with leak detection/halt-on-error; duplicate target also passed. Accepted its two P3 hardening suggestions: explicit profile-create borrowed/owned detach lifetime documentation and a first-call detach-failure test proving the Python source remains pinned until a later success. title: Publish a versioned serialized V2 packet/profile contract and creation API
description:
## Motivation

V2 interoperability currently depends on passing an in-process C++ SeedProfile containing dimensions, attempts, contract versions, salts, and options. There is no stable public C/C++ representation to negotiate, persist, or transmit the exact equation contract.

## Evidence

codec/WirehairV2Seeds.h defines an internal SeedProfile with more than twenty fields, and codec/WirehairV2Codec.h exposes only internal C++ facade initialization. The installed public header contains no V2 create/select/serialize API or canonical packet descriptor.

## Scope

Define a compact, endian-stable, explicitly versioned descriptor containing only canonical equation-affecting inputs, plus public C and C++ creation/validation APIs. Derived/redundant profile values and local tuning metrics must not go on wire. Explicitly share a common version/hash vocabulary with the legacy profile work where semantics match, and document intentional differences.
acceptance_criteria: Specify canonical byte encoding, size/version negotiation, reserved-field rules, validation limits, and stable typed errors. Encoder selection serializes a descriptor; an independent decoder created only from that descriptor reproduces golden packet rows and message recovery across processes/builds. Add malformed/truncated/unknown-version and cross-endian fixtures, installed C/C++ consumers, ABI-size checks, and migration rules for future contract versions.
notes:

title: Add a stateful V2 property and sanitizer fuzz harness
description:
## Problem

V2 has strong example-based tests but no stateful fuzz target covering malformed profiles/systems, packet sequences, duplicates/conflicts, retries, object reuse, and small-system oracle equivalence.

## Evidence

codec/CMakeLists.txt registers deterministic policy/precode/round-trip tests. There is no libFuzzer/AFL-style target for V2 API sequences. PrecodeSolveTest.cpp:17-160 already contains an independent tiny dense reference solver that can be factored for fuzz-oracle reuse.

## Scope

Create bounded deterministic fuzz entry points for profile/system construction and encoder/decoder operation sequences. Reuse or extract the existing tiny dense GF(256) oracle instead of creating a divergent second reference implementation.
acceptance_criteria: ASan/UBSan fuzzing covers malformed dimensions/contracts/salts, packet IDs/sizes/order, duplicates/conflicts, rank deficiency, post-completion calls, allocation retries, and repeated V1/V2 initialization. Reuse the extracted tiny dense oracle for K<=128; cap generated block bytes at 4096 and any single fuzz-input allocation at 64 MiB. CI runs a fixed corpus plus at least 10,000 deterministic mutations per target with a 60-second cap and corpus artifacts below 5 MiB. A scheduled job uses pinned seeds for at least 30 minutes per target. Crashes preserve reproducible inputs and no target performs unbounded allocation.

title: Make the legacy decoder safely idempotent for duplicate packets
description:
## Motivation

Real datagram and retransmission systems routinely deliver duplicates, but the legacy public API forbids reusing block IDs. Duplicate systematic IDs fail the decoder, while duplicate repair IDs can consume equation capacity and work without a general identity policy.

## Evidence

include/wirehair/wirehair.h:306-309 makes duplicate avoidance an application precondition. WirehairCodec.cpp:5311-5316 detects only systematic IDs tracked in _original_row; there is no bounded all-ID duplicate policy equivalent to V2's ReceivedIds/content check.

## Scope

Choose and document an exact tracking model before implementation. Prefer a first-packet-wins ID set capped at N+1024 accepted unique IDs (or justify another fixed formula), with ExtraInsufficient/fail-closed behavior rather than silent eviction when full. Define whether content equality uses retained bytes or a documented at-least-128-bit digest and make clear that duplicate hashing is not authentication. Equality for the partial final systematic block covers only meaningful final bytes.
acceptance_criteria: Identical retained duplicates are idempotent and conflicting retained payloads return a stable error for systematic and repair IDs. Tests pin the exact unique-ID cap/formula, memory bound, digest/full-byte collision contract, and behavior for a new unique ID or repeated ID after capacity is exhausted; no accepted ID is silently evicted. Duplicate storms do not change rank, row count, or output. Quantify any robustness change from capping the legacy decoder's currently unbounded replacement attempts, and cover extra-row resume and post-completion states without adding unrelated OOM-retry semantics.
notes:
Checkpoint 2026-07-10: Implemented bounded first-packet-wins identity tracking in the legacy decoder. Current contract is N+1024 accepted IDs, no eviction, 24-byte records in a power-of-two table at <=50% load, fixed 128-bit two-SipHash payload equality, meaningful bytes only for partial final systematic packets, stable conflicts, and ExtraInsufficient for novel IDs at capacity. Added dedicated duplicate CTest and deterministic coverage for systematic/repair conflicts, partial tails, duplicate storms, post-completion state, UINT32_MAX, exact min/max memory bounds, extra-row resume, and active unsolved capacity using 1027 distinct IDs with identical equations. Current gates: Release core/duplicate/allocation/peel pass; ASan+UBSan pass; Valgrind 0 errors/leaks; real QEMU s390x big-endian and i686 32-bit duplicate suites pass. Independent review found no correctness blocker. Remaining before close: randomize/key the ID bucket hash to prevent crafted clustering, avoid payload hashing for novel IDs after cap, pin independent fingerprint vectors, skip redundant fresh-allocation table memset, correct <=50% wording, rerun gates, reconcile Fable Max review.
Independent adversarial review follow-up: addressed every actionable finding. ID bucket placement now uses a per-decoder process-local salt with a 64-bit mixer, preventing remote precomputation of linear-probe clusters; payload fingerprinting now occurs only after the ID probe, so novel IDs at cap return without reading/hash-scanning large payloads. Added 12 independently generated SipHash-2-4 vectors (0/1/7/8/9/15/16/31/63/64/65/257 bytes), verified both halves on native, i686, and big-endian s390x. Fresh calloc workspace skips redundant table memset; reused decoder workspace is explicitly cleared and tested. Corrected <=50% wording and documented up to 7 alignment bytes. Final local gates after fixes: Release legacy core + dedicated duplicate + allocation + peel 4/4; full ASan+UBSan legacy core and allocation pass; Valgrind 0 errors and 0 leaks; QEMU GCC 13.3 i686 and s390x dedicated duplicate suites pass. Awaiting the in-flight authorized Fable Max read-only report before closure.

title: Avoid full V2 decoder re-solves after every extra packet
description:
## Problem

Once a V2 decoder has K packets, every new unique overhead packet rebuilds the entire solve input and reruns sparse projection and residual elimination from scratch. Rank-deficient or adversarial streams can therefore cost roughly one full solve per extra packet.

## Evidence

codec/WirehairV2PrecodeDecode.cpp:202-250 rebuilds all SolvePacket entries and calls SolvePrecodeSystem. DecodeResult reaches AttemptSolve after each new packet, and accepts up to K+1024 packets. The V2 README currently notes that rank-failure resume rebuilds the sparse solve.

## Scope

Evaluate persistent factorization, solve checkpoints, staged/batched retry, or another algebraically equivalent resume design. State updates and allocation failures must be transactional and bounded, while results remain equivalent to a cold solve. Avoid assuming a new row can never change peeling/inactivation order.
acceptance_criteria: Compare the chosen resume design with cold re-solves over systematic-heavy, repair-only, rank-deficient, duplicate, conflicting, overdetermined, OOM-retry, and corrupted streams. Golden bytes/errors match. Using warm reusable objects, fixed packet streams, CPU affinity where available, and at least 20 interleaved A/B samples, cumulative solve time over eight overhead packets must improve by at least 50% at representative K=1000/10000 without regressing the initial K-packet solve by more than 5%. Additional persistent memory stays below 25% of existing decoder state or the excess is explicitly justified. Document worst-case fallback and bound memory through K+1024 packets.
notes:
2026-07-10 completed local implementation, uncommitted and unpushed per orchestrator.

DESIGN: codec/WirehairV2Solve.h/.cpp optionally materializes a rank-deficient affine checkpoint containing peeled-column constants and projections plus the reduced GF(256) pivot basis. ResumePrecodeSystem projects each appended equation into that fixed null-space basis and inserts it transactionally. The checkpoint represents the complete old row space, so it is equivalent to a cold solve even when the new row changes cold peeling or inactivation order. Duplicate validation uses independent scratch and does not mutate the checkpoint.

DECODER BOUNDS: codec/WirehairV2PrecodeDecode.h/.cpp adopts a checkpoint only after preallocating its one pending-packet slot and only when actual checkpoint plus slot capacity is at most 125 percent of the released receive payload and id-vector capacity. Otherwise it retains packets and cold re-solves. Residuals above kMaxInactiveColumns=4096 also use the cold fallback. Accepted ids remain bounded at K+1024. OOM before row insertion leaves algebra state unchanged; checkpoint-slot OOM retains all cold packets; a different packet after pending-row OOM first replays that row. Terminal inconsistent sets freeze while exact and conflicting duplicates retain Error and InvalidInput behavior.

COVERAGE: codec/PrecodeDecodeTest.cpp compares warm checkpoints with hook-disabled cold solves for systematic-heavy and repair-only distinct-id matrix-collision streams, rank-deficient progress, exact and conflicting duplicates, terminal inconsistent append and retry, overdetermined authentic and corrupt packets, altered independent data with matching recovered bytes, OOM retry followed by a different id, checkpoint-slot OOM, 25 percent memory accounting, and forced small-block cold fallback. codec/PrecodeSolveTest.cpp checks resumed solution equality and complete scratch and pivot nonmutation for duplicate checks. codec/V2ResumeBench.cpp and codec/CMakeLists.txt add the pinned acceptance target. Documentation is in codec/README.md and API comments.

BENCHMARK PASS: build/codec/wirehair_v2_resume_bench pinned CPU 0 and ran 20 alternating samples at bb=1280. K=1000 cumulative initial cold/warm 64.563/64.636 ms, ratio 1.0011; eight-overhead cold/warm 531.928/14.067 ms, 97.36 percent saved; checkpoint 1,512,567 versus receive 1,284,000 bytes, plus 17.80 percent. K=10000 initial 1347.622/1347.343 ms, ratio 0.9998; overhead 10843.414/275.379 ms, 97.46 percent saved; checkpoint 13,493,912 versus receive 12,840,000 bytes, plus 5.09 percent.

GATES: strict Release main build with WIREHAIR_STRICT_WARNINGS=ON passed. Release V2 ctest regex passed 14/14: policy, noinit, transactional, precode encode/decode/solve/roundtrip/seed-selection/OOM, profile, profile and stateful fuzz, and bench CLI. Fresh Clang 18 Debug ASan+UBSan strict build in build/i998-asan passed the V2 regex 12/12 with leak detection, halt-on-error, strict-string and UBSan stacktrace options; bench and OOM registrations were appropriately excluded there. Final benchmark rerun passed.

BUG PASSES: review found and fixed pending-row loss when a different id followed OOM, allow_insert=false scratch mutation, duplicate-consistency OOM misreporting, terminal inconsistent exact-versus-conflict retry loss, pointless cold terminal acceptance and re-solves, and unaccounted pending-vector allocator capacity. A subsequent complete source pass found no issue. git diff --check is clean.

EXACT TASK FILES: codec/WirehairV2Solve.h, codec/WirehairV2Solve.cpp, codec/WirehairV2PrecodeDecode.h, codec/WirehairV2PrecodeDecode.cpp, codec/PrecodeDecodeTest.cpp, codec/PrecodeSolveTest.cpp, codec/V2ResumeBench.cpp, codec/README.md, codec/CMakeLists.txt.
Post-closure independent adversarial integration review found and fixed two stats-contract issues plus one artifact: removed task-born unregistered V2IncrementalDecodeTest.cpp (it was not in CMake and its stale K=64 assumption failed the 25% checkpoint policy); seeded high-level cold/resume stats from the last committed attempt and made ResumePrecodeSystem return unchanged checkpoint stats on OOM/length failure; made cold SolvePrecodeSystem publish partial stats on every post-build terminal Error so PacketRows matches the incremental terminal path. Added field-wise same-decoder stats stability assertions across retryable OOM and terminal retry/conflict sequences, plus K+1 PacketRows parity. Strict focused solve/decode tests and the pinned K=1000/K=10000 benchmark pass after fixes (96.32-97.06% repeated-overhead savings; initial ratio 1.0006-1.0017). Final adversarial review still in progress.
Final independent review completed clean after fixes. Added K=1000 partial-final coverage (message size K*257-128) so systematic K-1 traverses cold and resumed append paths plus exact recovery. Reviewer reran Release and ASan+UBSan solve/decode, 100,000 stateful mutations, and K=1,000/10,000 benchmark; affine projection, pivot insertion, pending replay, duplicate/conflict, terminal state, bounds, and cold fallback were coherent with no remaining blocker. git diff --check clean.

title: Fuse V2 packet evaluation XOR passes
description:
## Problem

V2 packet evaluation initializes the destination with memcpy and then performs a separate full destination read/write pass for every remaining source and each of the fixed three mix terms. This needlessly increases memory traffic in encode and recovery.

## Evidence

codec/WirehairV2Solve.cpp:351-379 performs one memcpy followed by gf256_add_mem for each term. The certified packet contract uses MixCount=3, while gf256 already supplies addset and add2 fused kernels.

## Scope

Combine the first source with mix term 0 via addset and combine mix terms 1 and 2 via add2 where aliasing and backend contracts permit it, with a clear fallback for non-certified MixCount values.
acceptance_criteria: All existing golden packet vectors and recovered messages remain byte-identical. Document/enforce that block_out does not overlap intermediate storage, or implement a defined safe path. Tests cover source weights, alignment/tails, scalar/SIMD backends, and alias rejection. Use warm reusable objects, fixed rows, CPU affinity where available, and at least 30 interleaved A/B samples at approximately 1280 B, 100 KiB, and 1 MiB. Keep the implementation only if median wall time improves by at least 5% in one material production regime or measured destination memory traffic falls by at least 15%, with no regime regressing more than 3%; otherwise record a no-go result and leave production code unchanged.
notes:
Implementation and validation complete; intentionally left IN_PROGRESS for parent review/close.

Production design:
- codec/WirehairV2Solve.cpp uses gf256_addset_mem for the first two source terms, or source 0 plus mix 0 for singleton rows, then gf256_add2_mem for certified mix terms 1+2. Logical operation accounting is unchanged.

title: Strictly parse gen_tables --heavy-trials on LLP64 and 32-bit hosts
description:
## Problem

The --heavy-trials parser uses strtoul and compares the result with UINT_MAX. On LLP64/32-bit platforms unsigned long is already 32 bits, so negative or overflowing input can saturate to UINT_MAX and pass, launching billions of trials instead of failing fast.

## Evidence

tables/TableGenerator.cpp:1906-1919 lacks a leading-digit/sign check and does not reliably reject range errors for the destination type. The value drives loops at 1941 and 2005. Current CI smoke coverage supplies only zero.

## Steps to Reproduce

On MSVC/LLP64, run gen_tables --no-benchmarks --heavy-trials -1 and also an integer larger than UINT_MAX. Depending on CRT conversion, strtoul returns UINT_MAX; the value > UINT_MAX check cannot reject it and the generator begins an enormous workload.

## Scope

Use a strict unsigned parser with explicit syntax and range validation before any generator work starts.
acceptance_criteria: Reject empty, signed, whitespace-prefixed, trailing-character, errno-range, and destination-overflow inputs consistently on Linux, MSVC, and 32-bit builds. Define and document a finite operational maximum for --heavy-trials that cannot launch a multi-billion-trial accident; values above it reject before expensive work. Accept 0, the default, the maximum, and representative values within range. Negative CLI tests prove rejection occurs before initialization or output mutation.
notes:
Implemented strict decimal-only bounded parsing for gen_tables --heavy-trials. The CLI now rejects null/empty, signs, whitespace, non-decimal/trailing text, and values above a documented 10,000,000 operational cap before printing its banner or starting generator work. Added Bash regression coverage (including explicit empty argv, 32/64-bit overflow strings, cap+1, 0/4096/max) and cross-platform CMake execute_process checks used by the MSVC build-policy lane. Updated tables/HEAVY_MATRIX.md.

- git diff --check: pass

close_reason: Implemented strict bounded parsing and validated Linux plus cross-platform build-policy E2E

title: Make descending dense-count interpolation portable without unsigned wrap
description:
## Problem

Descending dense-count interpolation represents a negative quotient by converting it to unsigned, adding it to an unsigned base, and then assigning the wrapped value to int. The final out-of-range unsigned-to-signed conversion is implementation-defined.

## Evidence

WirehairTools.cpp:942-958 computes const int count = Count0 + (unsigned)(numerator / denominator). Descending segments make numerator/denominator negative, so mainstream two's-complement builds happen to recover the intended value through wraparound.

## Steps to Reproduce

Compile the interpolation logic with a compiler/target or conversion sanitizer that does not define out-of-range unsigned-to-int as two's-complement wrapping, then evaluate a descending dense point segment. Compare against direct signed interpolation.

## Scope

Perform the arithmetic in a sufficiently wide signed type, with explicit range assertions before narrowing, while preserving all shipped results.
acceptance_criteria: Check in a pre-change digest or golden vector for GetDenseCount over every N=2..64000, then prove the signed rewrite reproduces it exactly. Add focused ascending, flat, descending, boundary, and negative-intermediate unit cases plus strict-conversion/static-analysis coverage on GCC, Clang, and MSVC.
notes:
Implemented signed-width-safe dense interpolation without touching CMake.

Files/hunks:
- WirehairTools.h: added internal static-inline detail::InterpolateDenseCount. It explicitly converts uint16/unsigned inputs to int64_t before subtract/multiply/divide, asserts N0<N1 and N in range, and asserts 0<count<=UINT16_MAX before narrowing. Static linkage avoids adding a shared-library ABI symbol.
- WirehairTools.cpp: GetDenseCount now calls the signed helper; removed the signed->unsigned wrap and implementation-defined unsigned->int narrowing.
- test/LegacyCoreTest.cpp: direct ascending, flat, both endpoint, descending negative/remainder, and >INT32 product/UINT16 boundary cases; dedicated FNV-1a golden over every (N,GetDenseCount(N)) for N=2..64000.

Compatibility evidence:
- Detached clean pre-change commit 4bc5c31 built separately and produced all-N digest 1a472addbc37c434.
- Rewritten build produces the exact same 1a472addbc37c434 digest.
- Existing pre-fixup/current seed hashes and N=5550/2373 packet/profile hashes remain exact in every legacy_core run.

Validation:
- GCC 13.3 portable Release, WIREHAIR_STRICT_WARNINGS=ON, static+shared: 7/7 legacy/profile CTest gates passed.
- GCC 13.3 -march=native Release strict: 6/6 legacy/profile CTest gates passed.
- GCC Debug ASan+UBSan with leak detection and halt-on-error: 6/6 legacy/profile CTest gates passed.
- Focused TU compile with -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror=sign-conversion passed; no interpolation diagnostics. Six pre-existing unrelated -Wconversion warnings remain in PCG/column iteration/sqrt/prime/row parameter code.
- GCC -fanalyzer with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror passed.
- nm -D confirmed InterpolateDenseCount is not exported from libwirehair.so.
- git diff --check passed.
- clang++, clang-cl, cl, MinGW, and 32-bit multilib are unavailable on this host; Clang/MSVC acceptance still needs hosted CI after integration.

Repeated bug-review passes:
1. Found that an out-of-line testable helper would add a new C++ shared-library symbol; changed it to static inline internal-header implementation and reran all gates.
2. Re-read arithmetic bounds, signed division/truncation, duplicate graph-point selection, rounding, test coverage, and profile interactions; no further defects found.

Bead intentionally left in_progress for parent integration/hosted compiler evidence.
close_reason: Replaced unsigned-wrap interpolation with signed int64 arithmetic; exhaustive N=2..64000 fingerprint and focused edge cases preserve results; strict, sanitizer, sign-conversion, and analyzer gates passed. Independent source review clean.

title: Enumerate unique V2 seed-tuning candidates and report actual work
description:
## Problem

V2 seed candidate generation hashes the candidate index and truncates to eight bits without a permutation or deduplication. Expensive tuning evaluates repeated seeds, biases population statistics, and reports requested counts that are larger than the distinct work performed.

## Evidence

codec/WirehairV2Seeds.cpp:106-131 maps indices independently into uint8_t values, and tuning loops at 160-192 consume them directly. PolicyTest.cpp:1126-1130 checks only determinism and index-zero preservation. Audited defaults produced as few as 14/16 unique peel and 29/32 unique dense candidates; 256 requests yielded only 159-171 distinct seeds.

## Steps to Reproduce

Enumerate CandidateSeed(base, index) for indices 0 through 255 for representative shipped buckets, insert results into a set, and compare its size with 256. Repeat the default 16/32 candidate configurations and observe duplicate evaluations.

## Scope

Use a keyed permutation of the 8-bit seed domain that preserves the base seed at index zero, or explicitly deduplicate and report requested, distinct, and completed work.
acceptance_criteria: For every 8-bit base/bucket, indices 0-255 enumerate all 256 seeds exactly once. Tiny 16-bit dense base seeds remain candidate zero while subsequent 8-bit candidates are unique within their domain. CLI/results record requested, unique, and completed counts. Determinism, shipped profile selection, and bounded/full tuning tests remain stable or intentionally versioned.
notes: Implemented keyed odd-step permutations over Z/256 for peel and dense candidate traversal; index zero preserves the shipped base (including full 16-bit tiny dense seeds), every valid peel bucket/base and the full 16-bit dense-base domain are exhaustively checked, and representative values pin the new methodology version. Tune metadata and seedtable/densetune CSV now distinguish raw requested, unique, and completed counts, including 0->0/1/1 and 300->300/256/256. Persistent CLI CMake tests pin both schemas/count cases. Shipping SelectSeedProfile remains unchanged. Release/Debug strict, full CLI, ASan+UBSan, 128-thread transactional integration, and independent mathematical/source review pass.
close_reason: Candidate generation is now a duplicate-free keyed permutation, work accounting is truthful across minimum/capped requests, shipping selection is stable, and exhaustive domain plus CLI/sanitizer/review gates pass.

title: Correct and pin the legacy heavy-field polynomial contract
description:
## Problem

The legacy codec architecture documentation names irreducible polynomial 0x15F for heavy rows, while the initialized GF256 implementation and GFNI transforms use 0x14D. This misdocuments the equation contract and can produce incompatible independent implementations.

## Evidence

WirehairCodec.h:876-881 states 0x15F. gf256.cpp:579-592 selects polynomial index 3, (0xA6 << 1) | 1 = 0x14D, and gf256.h:74 and gf256.cpp:826/1658/1860 explicitly describe 0x14D.

## Steps to Reproduce

Initialize GF256 with the production call, derive the reduction polynomial/table from the selected index, and compare a pinned multiply/divide vector with the result specified by the WirehairCodec.h architecture comment. The documented 0x15F field disagrees with runtime 0x14D.

## Scope

Correct every public/internal architecture description and turn the production polynomial into a testable interoperability constant.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation consistently specifies 0x14D and distinguishes it from historical alternatives. Contract tests pin representative multiply/divide/inverse values and externally observable heavy-row/repair packet golden vectors after wirehair_init. Scalar, SIMD, GFNI, and cross-platform backends must reproduce those vectors; do not duplicate the already completed exhaustive GFNI campaign.
notes: Implemented the production GF(256) contract correction: WirehairCodec.h now identifies irreducible polynomial 0x14D, generator element 2, and records that historical 0x15F prose was erroneous. LegacyCoreTest pins GF256Ctx.Polynomial, multiply/divide/inverse vectors, and public repair packet id 12345 for the deterministic 128-byte message. Validation: native Release full CTest 26/26; portable strict Release legacy_core_test; native GFNI+AVX512 strict Release legacy_core_test with active GFNI/AVX512; ASan+UBSan portable legacy_core_test; git-history check confirmed 0x14D initialization since the initial codec import; final source/diff review found no remaining defect.
close_reason: Corrected the documented polynomial to the historical production 0x14D field and pinned internal arithmetic plus an externally observable repair vector across portable, native SIMD/GFNI, full CTest, and sanitizer validation.

title: Govern ELF shared-library exports with a versioned public-symbol allowlist
description:
## Problem

ELF shared builds export internal C++ codec and GF256 symbols in addition to the intended public C ABI. This creates accidental ABI commitments, interposition/collision risk, and limits linker optimization. A permanently hard-coded symbol count would also reject intentional future API additions.

## Evidence

include/wirehair/wirehair.h:49-63 controls visibility only for Windows. CMakeLists.txt:179-199 does not select hidden default visibility. nm -D --defined-only on the audited shared library reported 92 exports: the current 15 public wirehair_* functions plus 77 internal symbols.

## Steps to Reproduce

Configure a Release shared build on Linux, run nm -D --defined-only on libwirehair.so, and compare the complete defined-symbol table with the public functions intentionally listed in the installed ABI.

## Scope

Use hidden default visibility or an ELF version/export script and maintain a checked-in, reviewable public-symbol allowlist initially containing the current 15 functions. Intentional API features update/version that manifest; internal targets must not rely on leaked DSO symbols.
acceptance_criteria: Automated ELF CI requires the complete dynamic export table to equal the checked-in versioned public allowlist. Existing exact Windows gates are generated from or compared with the same intended ABI. Static-only, shared-only, and dual builds plus installed C/C++/plugin/Python consumers all link and run. Mach-O verification is owned by the portability task once a macOS lane exists.
notes:
Implementation complete and independently source-reviewed locally; intentionally left IN_PROGRESS for parent integration. Added abi/wirehair.map as the single sorted WIREHAIR_2.0 allowlist. It contains the current 18 public C functions (the original 15 plus three profile APIs added by wirehair-koh). Linux shared targets link with this version script and LINK_DEPENDS. Exact CTest inspection parses the map independently, requires each callable export to be symbol@@WIREHAIR_2.0, rejects every extra/missing name, normalizes only the optional linker-synthetic namespace row, and includes a fail-closed negative self-test. Installed shared and dual package E2Es inspect relocated/default-component DSOs with the same gate. ci/run_ci.py now loads the same manifest for MSVC dumpbin and MinGW checks; runner tests require exact parity with all WIREHAIR_EXPORT public-header declarations and reject wildcards, duplicates, unsorted, or malformed maps. Shared-primary internal V2/generator targets now use an explicit static support library instead of accidental DSO C++ exports. Docs explain the ABI update workflow.

Validation on 2026-07-10: strict GCC Release shared all-target build and 33/33 CTests passed, including static/shared/dual installed C, C++, plugin, native Python, package relocation, V2, exact positive/negative ELF checks, and build policy. Explicit shared-build gen_small_dseeds, gen_peel_seeds, gen_most_dseeds, gen_dcounts, gen_tables, and wirehair_v2_bench all linked through static support; smoke runs passed. Opposite dual orientation (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON plus WIREHAIR_BUILD_BOTH=ON) built; ABI/C/C++/V2 tests passed; installed C/C++/plugin/Python consumers passed. GCC ASan+UBSan shared build passed exact exports, legacy C/C++, legacy_core, and V2 transactional/policy tests. GNU ld.bfd, gold, mold, and GCC WH_LTO=AUTO artifacts each passed the 18-symbol check. An old 98-export DSO failed the checker as expected. A C consumer and plugin linked against the old unversioned DSO both ran against the new default-versioned DSO, confirming binary lookup compatibility. Combined ci.test_run_ci passed 23/23; py_compile and git diff --check passed. No source defects found on the final repeated review pass.
Parent integration independently configured a fresh strict shared-primary Release build, built all targets through explicit static internal support, verified the exact nm/readelf WIREHAIR_2.0 table, passed positive and fail-closed negative export CTests, and passed installed static/shared/both package E2Es. Source review of map grammar, linker dependency, shared/dual target selection, header parity, and installed relocation checks found no remaining issue.
close_reason: A versioned manifest is now the single ABI allowlist across ELF/Windows gates; Linux exports exactly 18 versioned C symbols, internals use explicit static support, and linker variants, LTO, sanitizers, negative leakage, compatibility, and all installed consumers pass.

title: Reject aligned-allocation size overflow before calloc
description:
## Problem

SIMDSafeAllocate adds alignment padding to size without checking SIZE_MAX - size. A near-address-space request can wrap to a tiny calloc allocation, after which alignment metadata and later writes escape that allocation. The primitive is unsafe on every size_t width; practical codec reachability is strongest through internal/experimental dense overrides on 32-bit.

## Evidence

WirehairTools.cpp:667-690 calls calloc(1, kSIMDSafeAlignBytes + size) directly. Callers check only that the unpadded request narrows to size_t. Verified 32-bit configurations include encoder N=77, dense=500, blockBytes=7,354,383 producing a UINT32_MAX workspace and decoder N=1170, dense=500, blockBytes=2,561,032 producing 4,294,967,294 bytes while passing the existing (N+507)*blockBytes guard. Normal default dense profiles retain megabytes of slack.

## Steps to Reproduce

Under ASan, call SIMDSafeAllocate(SIZE_MAX - 1) on any native width. For codec reachability, use a 32-bit internal OverrideSeeds/WH_SEED_KNOBS build with one of the verified configurations. The padding addition wraps before calloc and the subsequent metadata access or initialization is out of bounds.

## Scope

Add a pre-addition overflow guard in the allocator and keep every caller transactional on allocation failure.
acceptance_criteria: SIMDSafeAllocate returns null without calling calloc when size > SIZE_MAX - kSIMDSafeAlignBytes. Test a checked-add helper or injectable calloc at the largest safe and first overflowing sizes on native 64-bit without huge allocation. An i686 ASan/UBSan lane validates the exact encoder and decoder reachability cases, which must return Wirehair_OOM or InvalidInput without state corruption.
notes:
Implemented checked SIMD padding addition in WirehairTools: requests above SIZE_MAX minus the active 16/32/64-byte alignment return null before the allocator seam; the validated padded size is reused by the Linux huge-page branch. Added one-byte metadata alignment assertions and a thread-local WIREHAIR_TESTING calloc seam. Audited all three callers (input, matrix, workspace): each clears/retains valid ownership on failure; removed decoder debug traps on expected OOM so Debug builds return errors normally. Added test/AllocationOverflowTest.cpp and CMake registration. Tests pin largest-safe -> calloc exactly once with SIZE_MAX, first-overflow -> zero calloc calls/null, real zero/alignment/3MiB aligned calloc/free, injected failures and successful reuse for encoder/decoder input/workspace and solver matrix, and exact i686 encoder N=77 dense=500 block=7354383 plus decoder N=1170 dense=500 block=2561032 safe failure/reuse. Evidence: native GCC strict + DEBUG passed; ASan+UBSan+LSan passed; WH_ALIGN64+WH_HUGEPAGE passed including 3MiB path; shared strict production build passed; Valgrind leak/error clean; legacy_core_test passed; Debian i386 native 32-bit GCC 12 strict ASan+UBSan CTest passed exact reachability. Two complete source-review passes found no remaining allocator/caller/platform defect. Left IN_PROGRESS per orchestrator; no commit/close/export/push.
Parent integration independently verified the checked boundary proof: padding is positive and bounded, SIZE_MAX-padding reaches calloc exactly once via a rejecting hook, the next size clears output and never calls calloc, returned offsets remain representable, and huge-page length uses the checked total. Current combined Release allocation/legacy gates and ASan+UBSan+LSan allocation gate pass; source review found no remaining issue.
close_reason: SIMD-safe allocation padding is checked before calloc, all allocation callers fail transactionally and remain reusable, and exact native i386 overflow cases plus strict/debug/sanitizer/Valgrind/huge-page/shared validation pass.

title: Enforce a valid V2 packet-row domain above the last 16-bit prime
description:
## Problem

V2 packet-row generation accepts precode spans through 65535, but its distinct-column iterator depends on NextPrime16, which returns zero above 65521. Debug builds hit an invariant; Release builds silently emit duplicate mix columns and lower-rank packet equations. Structure-only precode construction has a broader valid domain and should not be conflated with packet evaluation.

## Evidence

codec/WirehairV2Precode.cpp:112-123 accepts structure spans through UINT16_MAX. codec/WirehairV2Solve.cpp:264-282 accepts K + P <= UINT16_MAX and calls NextPrime16(P) for packet rows. WirehairTools.cpp:195-199 returns zero for values above 65521.

## Steps to Reproduce

Build a PrecodeSystem with K=2, P=65522, SourceHits=1, then generate the audited packet row for id=153334 and peel seed 1. BuildPrecodeSystem and ValidatePrecodeSystem correctly accept the structure, while Release packet generation emits columns 0, 53755, 20987, 53755 and Debug trips columnCountNextPrime >= columnCount.

## Scope

Document and enforce separate structure-only and exact-packet domains. Either reject P > 65521 consistently in packet Generate/Evaluate/Solve paths or replace the iterator with a full-domain distinct-column generator, without unnecessarily rejecting valid structure-only systems.
acceptance_criteria: Boundary tests cover P=1, 2, 65521, 65522, and maximum total spans in Debug and Release. Unless the iterator is extended, P=1 remains structure-valid but packet-invalid, and P>65521 remains structure-valid but packet-invalid. Exact packet Generate, Evaluate, and Solve use existing failure conventions consistently and perform no output writes on rejection; certified facades cannot create an unsupported packet profile. Property coverage is exhaustive over packet IDs for small spans and uses checked-in fixed-seed boundary samples at P=65521/65522. Every accepted row has exactly MixCount distinct in-range precode columns.
notes: Implemented a shared exact-packet domain gate: K 2..64000, P 2..65521, K+P <= 65535, mix 1..min(3,P). Generate, public/validated Evaluate, Solve, Verify, systematic selectors, solved-system encoder initialization, and message-profile resolution now reject unsupported packet domains before iterators/output writes; BuildPrecodeSystem remains unchanged and accepts structure-only P=1 and P>65521 systems. Documented the split in codec/README.md and WirehairV2Solve.h. Added PrecodeSolveTest coverage for P=1,2,65521,65522, valid/invalid maximum total spans, exact seed=1/id=153334 reproducer, no-write output/stats/selector behavior, 65,536 tiny-span IDs, 100,000 fixed-seed accepted-domain samples, and all certified K=2..64000 profiles. Validation: strict Release V2 CTest 10/10; strict Debug V2 CTest 9/9; ASan+UBSan V2 CTest 8/8; 64/64 parallel message-codec round trips across varied K=2..4000/block sizes passed. Repeated source review found and fixed rejection ordering and widened P sums. Files: codec/WirehairV2Solve.h/.cpp, codec/WirehairV2PrecodeEncode.cpp, codec/PrecodeSolveTest.cpp, codec/README.md. Left in_progress and uncommitted per coordinator.
close_reason: All packet generation/evaluation/solve/facade paths now enforce the valid 16-bit-prime row domain with no-write rejection; strict, sanitizer, exhaustive/property, and V2 E2E passed

title: Warn public callers that FEC success does not authenticate recovered payloads
description:
## Problem
